📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the console release of GTA 6 is here, in case you hadn't noticed. And us PC gamers are desperate to get hold of a version of our own, particularly as modders say it'll be playable on god's own platform within a week. Be careful what you click on, though, as NordVPN's threat intelligence team has discovered a nasty-sounding scam package on the dark web.

The firm has posted a warning on X of a "GTA 6 PC scam kit" doing the rounds on the more dubious parts of the internet, using a fake GTA 6 PC port as bait.

According to recent reports, A “GTA 6 PC scam kit” — yours for just $200. That’s what our Threat Intelligence team found on the dark web: a crypto wallet drainer, a fake “GTA6 Keygen.exe” that steals accounts, a YouTube Shorts bot to spread it, and a hidden crypto miner. The bait? A fake “GTA 6 PC Port.” But GTA 6 is console-only — there's no PC version coming on launch day. If you see one, it’s a scam. If it doesn’t come from the creators, don't click it!November 19, 2026.

The package is stated to be for sale for $200, or twice what a single copy of Grand Theft Auto VI: Ultimate Edition costs at retail. Included is a crypto wallet drainer, a fake "GTA6 Keygen.exe," and a hidden crypto miner. There's also a YouTube Shorts bot within the package, designed to help it spread.

All of which sounds comprehensively designed to screw over PC gamers looking to get their hands on GTA 6 ahead of an official release.

It has been revealed that speaking to Tech Radar ahead of the games launch, NordVPN CTO Marijus Briedis mentioned: "Someone has packaged the whole scam and is selling it to anyone with $200. You don’t need any technical skills anymore.".

"People who play on PC have been waiting for news, and any link promising an early PC version will get clicks," indicates Briedis. "There is no PC version on November 19. If you see one, it's a scam.".

NordVPN isn't the only security provider warning of GTA 6 scams. Malwarebytes has detailed a number of dodgy sites that supposedly offer access to the game, each using the hype as a lure to convince you to give away your details and funnel you into various schemes.

Keep up to date with the most key stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Sources indicate that all of which compels me to restate the facts: GTA 6 does not have a PC release at the time of writing. In fact, it's not even been declared by Rockstar at this point. The game is available in Xbox Series X/S and PlayStation 5 versions only, and while modders seem to be beavering away on an unofficial PC version based on a leaked Xbox build, it's not available yet.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You know, I'm sure that Sony had every intention of following through on their intention to release 10 live service games by 2026, as they mentioned way back in 2022. Well, as far as an intention that's designed to please shareholders can go, anyway. And now here we are, almost five years on from that comment that continues to haunt them with the news Fairgame$ has been cancelled.

It has been revealed that this comes from a report from Bloomberg, who shared that, thankfully, there are no planned job cuts due to the game being cancelled. In a statement, Sony stated that, "The studio will shift its focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation Studios, while also exploring newly introduced creative opportunities, though didn't go into detail as to who those other teams are.

It has been revealed that bloomberg were also privy to a note shared with developers at Haven Studios from executives Sean Decker and John Doyle that follows a recent test of the game: "While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set. Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game.".

Sony have, notably, failed to capitalise on the live service trend; I'm sure I don't need to remind you about Concord. Hell, this isn't even taking the end of Destiny 2 into consideration, once a driving force of live service games, or how Marathon has struggled to pick up an audience in the way that Sony may want it to. You just can't force a game to be popular, especially in a genre like shooters.

For those that either missed or forgot about Fairgame$, it was unveiled back in 2023 and was supposed to be a "competitive modern heist game where you team up to break into exotic locations and steal the cargo," all while taking on security and other, real people. Gameplay was never formally revealed, only a CGI trailer, and was set to come to PC as well as PlayStation. Bloomberg also noted that the game had been reworked multiple times since the announcement and was set to be re-revealed with a fresh name. Ultimately, it looks like Katharine was a little generous with her timeline of six months.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, you’ve spent time wandering around Hyrule in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake, and you decided to pay the Happy Mask Salesman a visit.
  • Well, it reveals the inner thoughts of the game’s various NPCs.
  • Listening to the inner truths of the game’s various NPCs can get a bit wild, but these are the most unhinged and strange thoughts to be found in Hyrule.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, you’ve spent time wandering around Hyrule in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake, and you decided to pay the Happy Mask Salesman a visit. He gave you a few masks, you made a few sales, and you have received the Mask of Truth in return.

What does this mask do? Well, it reveals the inner thoughts of the game’s various NPCs. I am not sure if you have paid attention to Nintendo games recently, but they have been adding in some interesting NPC dialogue.

Listening to the inner truths of the game’s various NPCs can get a bit wild, but these are the most unhinged and strange thoughts to be found in Hyrule.

If you walk around the town square in Castle Town, you can find some rather colorful NPCs, but one of the most unassuming of them is the old woman who stares at the fountain. She seems so sweet, but she is actually a thief.

Listening to her inner thoughts, you see that they say, “The quality of the items people are losing has really gone downhill recently… Is that a recession indicator?”.

Recent findings suggest that this hits a little close to home considering many have questioned if the U.S. is entering a recession. Along with this, it is obvious that she is taking some of the goods that people have lost and keeping them for herself.

If you continue your search around the fountain in Castle Town, you can find a young couple who are dancing. While they seem rather sweet, their inner thoughts tell a completely different story.

Industry observers note that when you read the thoughts of the woman, it will say that she hopes that the man doesn’t break her heart. It is a sad thought to be had because she is clearly worried about her future.

When you read the man’s thoughts, you see they say, “Wait… What was this one’s name again?” Clearly, this isn’t his only crush, and he is stringing this poor woman along so he has someone to dance with. Yes… dance with.

It has been revealed that some of the guards around Castle Town aren’t very excited about their job. In fact, some of them find it boring doing patrols all the time. One guard in particular thinks about it pretty frequently.

Recent findings suggest that when interacting with the guard in the room with the pots, his inner truth will say, “Guards… Soldiers… Heroes… It’s their fault there’s so much peace around here. Hm… What if I…”.

In a recent development, the thought trails off after that, but you can clearly tell what he is thinking about. The man wants some chaos, and he is clearing thinking about being the cause of mentioned chaos if something doesn’t happen soon.

You may have seen the bearded man wandering around Castle Town in the past and Kakariko Village in the future. His beard is magnificent, and he will definitely tell you about it. However, he is secretly questioning its cleanliness.

When you listen to his inner thoughts, they say, “I wonder if it’s true that beards are about as dirty as toilets…” For someone with such a massive beard, he shouldn’t be thinking that he is dirty, unless he wants to shave it off.

This is a massive contrast to what he will tell you when you speak to him, as he will typically say that he has a fantastic beard, and will even offer to locate Ganondorf.

Recent findings suggest that shiro is one of the many NPCs you can find around Kakariko Village, and you also help him out by rescuing him from the Gerudo as an adult. Well, he isn’t the happiest carpenter around. In fact, he is rather depressed.

According to recent reports, his inner thoughts read, “How does one escape their own dreary life? ‘Cause I can’t do this forever.” Granted, he didn’t seem the happiest when I rescued him from the Gerudo, but I never would have guessed that he was this depressed.

Looking into his thoughts, he seems like he could use some therapy because it sounds like he has been hanging around Lumiose City in Pokémon Legends: Z-A for too long.

Recent findings suggest that there’s a pair of laughing men who appear in Castle Town and Kakariko. No matter what is happening, the pair consistently laugh at one another. They typically talk about stories they find funny, with the one laughing at the other for getting caught sneaking into the castle or falling off a horse.

However, when you read their inner thoughts, the one notes, “It’s exhausting wearing this forced smile all the time.” The other one will remark about how he knows his friend’s smile is fake.

Sources indicate that it’s sad that they continue to laugh constantly. Maybe they should just try to chill out for once and give up on the laughter. Are they cursed? Maybe they are cursed.

Sources indicate that if you have explored Kakariko Village, you are for sure aware of the cucco lady. All of her cuccos get out of the pen, and you must go rescue them for a reward. In the future, she is living with a questionable character.

If you use the Mask of Truth while you are an adult, you will catch her inner thoughts. They say, “That guy who lives with me always makes the most intense eye contact. He must really love cuccos…”.

In a recent development, what she is describing does not sound healthy at all. In fact, it sounds almost like something bad is going to happen and she is just waiting for the inevitable. Maybe she should choose a different place to live or kick the guy out.

In a recent development, there is an old man who likes to wander around Castle Town. He will go in and out of shops, but mostly he will walk around the fountain. Just be careful listening to his thoughts because he has a particular woman on his mind.

His inner thoughts read, “This kid… The mask’s neat and all, but I’m more interested in finding a particular damsel…” While it doesn’t seem so bad at first, if you talk to him, you can piece things together.

Sources indicate that talking to him, he will make remarks about how he is looking for a lady who can make a potion, and will gawk at how beautiful she is. He will also casually talk about how we are at the age to be thinking about that.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that britain's Marc 'Caedrel' Lamont and Dan Gaskin were among the winners at the 2026 Esports Awards in Miami, where Counter-Strike 2 was named game of the year and Team Vitality and BLAST also took industry honours. The results crown a strong Counter-Strike year eight days before the next CS2 Major begins in Singapore.

Recent findings suggest that the 2026 Esports Awards honoured two British figures from the streaming and broadcast side of the scene. Caedrel is a League of Legends streamer and co-streamer. Gaskin works as a caster.

In a recent development, the ceremony took place on the evening of 17 November at the Adrienne Arsht Center for the Performing Arts of Miami-Dade County. It is the scene’s main end-of-season awards show. The event began in London in 2016.

At Worlds 2026, Caedrel was the top co-streamer for both hours watched and peak viewers, according to Esports Charts.

It has been revealed that his co-stream success came in a softer year for the tournament overall. Worlds 2026 peaked at 3.98 million viewers, which was 41% lower than the previous year. Caedrel’s numbers show how much attention a single co-streamer can hold even when the event’s headline peak falls.

Gaskin was not the only caster honoured in Miami. The other broadcast honours went to Alex ‘Machine’ Richardson for Play-by-Play Caster of the Year, Iain Chambers for Host of the Year and Anthony ‘NAMELESS’ Wheeler for Analyst of the Year. iShowSpeed was named Streamer of the Year.

Counter-Strike featured prominently among the industry prizes. Vitality’s award as best organisation came alongside Esports PC Player of the Year for Mathieu ‘ZywOo’ Herbaut. OpTic Texas were named Esports Team of the Year.

BLAST, which stages many of its events in Europe, was named Esports Tournament Organiser of the Year.

Vitality’s results through the year back up their award. They beat Spirit to win IEM Rio 2026 on 19 April, giving them back-to-back ESL Grand Slam titles. ZywOo took his 31st career HLTV MVP award at that event.

"When I won this award in 2023, I never thanked my parents" 😅❤️.

Esports Colour Caster of the Year — @DanGaskin pic.twitter.com/oZBw5FItEJ.

— Esports Awards Presented by Thunderpick (@esportsawards) November 18, 2026.

Recent findings suggest that the team’s form held into the autumn. Vitality swept MOUZ 3-0 in the ESL Pro League Season 24 grand final on 11 October. That was their second title in a row after winning StarSeries Fall in September.

The PGL Major Singapore 2026 runs from 25 November to 13 December with 32 teams and a US$1,250,000 prize pool, The Kallang reported. The final stages will be played at the Singapore Indoor Stadium from 10 to 13 December.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that hoYoverse just wrapped up a big Honkai: Star Rail Special Program.
  • Industry observers note that the upcoming major release is dubbed No Aha at Full Moon for a very good reason.
  • Planarcadia is a place whose description sounds a bit like a Warhammer 40,000 Eldar homeworld, and is quite open about its cyberpunk inspirations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that hoYoverse just wrapped up a big Honkai: Star Rail Special Program. We’ve been waiting for this one for a couple of weeks now thanks to a delay, but the developer has finally delivered all the news on Version 4.0, which will arrive February 13.

Industry observers note that the upcoming major release is dubbed No Aha at Full Moon for a very good reason. Aha's Planarcadia is the substantial newly introduced world headlining Version 4.0.

Planarcadia is a place whose description sounds a bit like a Warhammer 40,000 Eldar homeworld, and is quite open about its cyberpunk inspirations. In-universe, however, it was born out of the pages of an art canvas, and it’s a world where pleasure is king.

In a recent development, the squad’s host in this chapter is Madam Pearl, who will oversee the the Astral Express’ return to the place where they first began their journey. Duomension City is where you’re going to land, and meet the creatures that dwell in this world.

According to recent reports, the imagenae of Planarcadia require attention to survive, and they feed off people’s Wishpower. If they don’t get any attention, they perish, which does tie into the general themes of the place. Duomension City has other interesting locations that you’re going to visit, such as the Graphia Academy art school, the commercial district of Dovebrook, and a few other places hidden behind mysterious entrances.

Industry observers note that the Phantasmoon Games is another highlight of Planarcadia, a competitive spectacle where you’ll have a chance to compete to become Aeon for a Minute. If you make it to the final stages, you may earn an audience with The Laughter.

Much like the world where the games take place, the whole point of the competition is to attract the most attention, so rules are a bit loose as to how you manage to do that. The event will bring together several of the game’s factions, though not everyone is there for the competition.

As you explore Planarcadia, if you have characters on your team who are on the newly-playable Path of Elation, you’ll earn Punchlines. The more you accumulate, the closer you get to catching Aha’s attention, which triggers Aha Instant.

Version 4.0 introduces two upcoming 5-Star characters to Honkai: Star Rail. General Yao Guang (Madam Yao) is one, a Seer Strategist from the Xianzhou Alliance's Yuque. If you’ve been playing the game, you may already be familiar with her voice, as she's previously been in touch with our heroes via radio link. But V4.0 marks her first on-screen appearance, as well as her playable debut.

General Yao Guang is a Physical character on the Path of Elation whose specialty is using Weal and Woe Lots in battle, which she uses to increase Elation for allies, and grant everyone Punchline any time she uses a Skill. If an Aha Instant is triggered, she casts Woe Lots, which debuff enemies, causing them to take increased damage, all while regenerating Skill Points for the rest of the team.

Her aptly named Certified Banger buff adds one extra instance of Elation to teammates’ attacks. And her Ultimate grants the team Punchline, and triggers an extra Aha Instant.

The other fresh arrival is likewise a Path of Elation devotee. Sparxie is a suspiciously familiar streamer who uses her influencer skills in combat. When she fights, she turns the fight into a battle for attention, as she forces enemies to engage in a race for upvotes.

When you consume Skill Points, Sparxie will get gifts, which in turn cause her to regenerate Skill Points and Punchlines for the team. You can continue doing this to increase your damage. When Aha Instant is triggered, Sparxie unleashes a lucky draw that deals damage to enemies with each bounce.

She also benefits from the Certified Banger state, which causes the gifs she receives to deal more Elation damage to a random enemy target. Her Ultimate also deals more Elation damage.

Version 4.0 will see a few re-runs, too. Black Swan, Evernight, and Hysilens will be part of the first half's Warp events. The second half will see the return of Sparkle, Cerydra, and Rappa — that's right, HoYoverse have finally remembered Rappa exists, after one of the longest rerun waits in the game's history! Both Black Swan and Sparkle are getting a few tweaks to their kit with this version, too, so the timing works.

In a recent development, finally, the other major news is a Fortnite collaboration. Starting February 26, Kafka and Blade will join Epic’s battle royale shooter. On that day, you’ll find skins of the two Stellaron Hunters in the Fortnite Item Shop, and the newly introduced outfits are even compatible with Fortnite's LEGO styles. You can also expect other customisation bits like Back Bling, Pickaxe, and more to be part of the package.

It has been revealed that if you download the game on the Epic Games Store, and take part in Honkai: Star Rail-themed activities, you’ll also get the Blade character outfit in Fortnite for free. Event schedule and timing will be declared at a later date.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Last night, Xbox Game Studios and Halo Studios have confirmed a free revision for the recently-released Halo: Campaign Evolved, which promises to add the four-player co-operative PvE mode, Firefight, to the game.

According to recent reports, "For nearly two decades, Firefight has been a Halo favorite, challenging Spartans to team up, hold the line, and survive wave after wave of enemies," indicates Halo Studios director of competitive engagement Tahir Hasangjekaj mentioned in a dedicated post on the Xbox website. "The tradition continues this winter as we add the four-player cooperative PvE mode to Halo: Campaign Evolved in a free enhancement.".

It has been revealed that though we don't have a release date for the update yet, Hasangjekaj does explicitly state "this Winter" as a window, and promises that we'll hear more information about the update at Halo Fest - due to run from 12th to 13hth December in Seattle, Washington. My money would be on a release around then, therefore.

"We're kicking things off tonight at Xbox FanFest, where attendees will be the first to jump in and experience Firefight across newly introduced maps and armed with plenty of weapons to help even the odds." It seems there's already a playable build of the mode, then.

Recent findings suggest that it's worth noting that this is quite an odd news blast from Xbox, since the last official information we heard about the Halo brand was that the next major Halo game being developed by Activision, as Halo Studios all but closes as part of Microsoft's Xbox 'restructuring' that saw one key member behind Halo: Campaign Evolved promoted and laid off within the same week. As things stand, we don't know anything specific about the future of the series, but there are plenty of rumours that the next title will be a reboot developed by Call of Duty's Sledgehammer Games.

According to recent reports, it's been fairly busy 24 hours for Xbox: as well as this Halo revision, we've heard from Asha Sharma as she celebrated the 25th anniversary of Xbox by seemingly going all-in on Gen AI. Elsewhere, we got the announcement that Wolfenstein 3 is in development over at MachineGames, headed up by Hugo Martin.

Today's the launch day for Tanuki: Pon's Summer, a delightfully vibrant mail delivery sim/Tony Hawk's Pro Skater but for bikes about restoring a shrine before the end of summer.

I've been enamoured by the vibe of Tanuki: Pon's Summer since it was announced in no small part because of how in some small ways it reminds me of Boku No Natsuyasumi, a cult-classic, Japan-only game series that's mostly just about hanging out in the Japanese countryside. This one isn't so lackadaisical, as you do have a job to do in delivering mail, but I think a similar spirit is there.

In a recent development, when it comes to delivering mail, there is a Death Strandingian element to it in your need to place your boxes on your BMX (which you can do sick tricks and flips on, of course) to maximise how much you can deliver. A bit less stressful than Kojima's joint, obviously, though elements are still there. Any money you earn from this gig can then be spent on restoring the shrine that you oh so love, which falls onto the sim side of things with the ability to fully customise how the shrine looks.

It has been revealed that there are also a whole heap of minigames to perform that helps you get to know the locals. I'm talking baseball, sumo wrestling, working in a sushi restaurant and, of course, fishing. You can see bits of that in the launch trailer above, which comes with as 2010s an anime opening song you could wish for with some animation so good it makes me want an adaptation of the game. In time, perhaps! You can pick it up on Steam right here.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Infinity Nikki is making headlines with its latest controversy about including Maye Musk in their 3.0 introductory trailer for Chinese players, but it seems that there are actually great surprises, according to other livestreams.

Today, in the main dev livestream for Chinese players (translated by YouTuber Whimsy Haven in English), which is where most things are revealed before the patch actually drops.

In the Infinity Nikki universe, people are coming up with theories and release schedules, where we are all travelling to next, and what the next abilities are.

With Grand Theft Auto 6 grabbing everyone’s attention, it seems like a genius nod that the cosy styling game decided to show its claws and add guns to the mix.

Nikki, in all her infinite universes and extended lore, is no stranger to guns, but so far it has been discussed heavily by fans whether Infold would take a safer approach and not give Nikki guns in the latest game.

Thankfully for all lovers of shooters, that is not the case. Nikki already has a huge backdrop of dark lore, and it only makes sense that they would dim the vibes in-game even further with the addition of guns to use against foes and Esselings.

The addition of a pink Barbie-esque convertible makes the Grand Theft Auto comparisons even funnier for fans of both, as we are all consumed by the hype for the Rockstar instant classic.

According to recent reports, unlike Rockstar, Infinity Nikki fans also got a glimpse of her dancing with a new character, which looked very suspiciously like Oscar from Rose of Versailles. Some fans are taking it as a further nod to the queer fans and those locked into Nikki lore, where rumours of her sexuality have floated from the early games.

Industry observers note that but of course, the main star of the show is Nikki and the fresh character using guns. Now, with her new 'gal pal,' you can switch guns on the go as you fight foes, from a semi-automatic pistol to a short-barreled shotgun, as shown in the livestream.

This is not the first gun in Infinity Nikki, as in 2.4 Nikki had a hunting shotgun which would only show up when the ability was used and wasn’t as flexible, leaving many fans disappointed but hopeful for more guns further on.

Infinity Nikki fans also got a glimpse of dancing with a new character, which looked very suspiciously like Oscar from Rose of Versailles.

The other upcoming weapons seem to be wizard staffs, as we have already had a few wands in accessories rather than actual weapons, which makes sense in a game with a heavy dress-up mechanic.

Industry observers note that the controversy with Maye Musk, Elon Musk’s mother, certainly put a dent in Infinity Nikki’s reputation, and the conversation between fans and devs has been strained. Nikki and her games are no strangers to controversy, and with the latest fiasco with Love and Deep Space still ongoing about Valko, only time will tell how Infold will react to all the communication between them and fans.

Infold has generally been receptive to Infinity Nikki fans, who have been asking for guns, darker storylines, more romance (even if only hinted at), among other things.

Sadly, we’re not sure if you can do drive-by shooting Grand Theft Auto style yet, as the footage of the car mostly focused on the streets of Cicia, but knowing Nikki and how you can summon the unicorn, bike, or motorcycle in different areas, the car should be able to breeze through weird forest terrain.

It may make sense to ask for drive-by shooting mechanics in the next questionnaires for more fun updates, as the devs do listen to what the fans want to see next.

It has been revealed that all in all, interesting things are happening in the next major Infinity Nikki update! No mention of poor Giovanni, though; he’s still in the basement.

Infinity Nikki is available on PC, macOS, PlayStation 5, and iOS and Android phones.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Heartopia has officially shared initial details about its first-ever collaboration event. The game, which launched a month ago to great success on mobile, as well as Steam on PC, has already been a staple among fans of Animal Crossing and The Sims.

Things are kicking into gear, it seems, because the game is already about to host its first collaboration event, and it is with My Little Pony.

The Heartopia X My Little Pony event officially begins on February 14, but a pre-launch login event is now live through the actual collaboration’s start. The limited-time event offers players sign-in puzzles every day that will unlock time-limited Exhibition Passes.

According to recent reports, the first actual piece of My Little Pony-themed content can be yours if you complete all puzzles, as that gets you a limited edition costume for your pet, based on the show’s Spike. The event itself, which will be available until March 15, brings My Little Pony’s Tree of Harmony into the world of Heartopia.

The ponies need your help to Wield Elements of Harmony so they can reawaken the tree, and bring it back to Equestria. In gameplay terms, you’re going to want to perform daily sensing at the tree in order to earn three of the six Elements of Harmony: Honesty, Generosity, Loyalty, Kindness, Laughter, and Magic.

The more you do this, the more the tree’s Energy goes up, and the more rewards and resources you stand to earn. Even more time-limited Exhibition Passes, and Moonlight Crystals can be earned as you water the tree.

Recent findings suggest that badge Pull Tokens are your big reward, which is what you’re actually going to use to get the special Pony Series badges. You’ll earn ten time-limited Exhibition Passes each time you complete one of the three sets of Pony Series badges. Collect all three and you’ll earn Town Collaboration Series badges.

Heartopia is a free-to-play game, so you know there is a Gacha component to this event. Expect six non-replacement Gacha Pools that each map to one member of My Little Pony’s Mane Six. Within each pool, you’ll be able to earn five outfit pieces, and one vehicle.

We also recently updated our guides on how to catch Frostspore fish - and if you’re into cooking, how to obtain every recipe and variant. If you haven’t already, definitely see if you missed any of these Heartopia codes, too.

  • In a recent development, fnatic has made its first confirmed exit official as it rebuilds its LEC roster for 2027.
  • Sources indicate that the club marked the departure with a farewell video titled “Thank You, Iván”.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fnatic has confirmed the departure of its longest-serving player, jungler Razork, who is set to join Team Heretics. With support Lospa also set to leave, the London club faces a near-total LEC roster rebuild for 2027.

In a recent development, fnatic has made its first confirmed exit official as it rebuilds its LEC roster for 2027. Razork was the London club’s longest-serving player and its main playmaker. He leaves after five seasons in the jungle.

Sources indicate that the club marked the departure with a farewell video titled “Thank You, Iván”. In it, Fnatic recalls him arriving as a young player with huge ambition. He had entered the LEC with Misfits Gaming in 2020 before moving to Fnatic in 2022. The club later extended his contract to run through 2026.

According to recent reports, his next stop appears to be Team Heretics. Sheep Esports reported that the 26-year-old will play alongside midlaner Jackies and support Jun. Heretics had already tried to sign him a year earlier. On that occasion it agreed a buyout with Fnatic but could not agree terms with the player.

Industry observers note that the rebuild runs deeper than the jungle. Every Fnatic team member except Lospa was due out of contract in 2026. The support was signed until the end of 2027.

That deal will not keep him at Fnatic either. Lospa has reportedly agreed verbally to join SK Gaming for 2027. No buyout is involved in moving his contract between the two clubs. With that move, the one contract running beyond 2026 also leaves the club.

In the jungle, Yike is set to replace Razork in a 2027 line-up of Soboro, Yike, Vladi, Doggo and Labrov, according to Sheep Esports sources.

The overhaul follows a difficult year. Fnatic finished eighth in LEC 2026 Versus. It then placed seventh in Spring, which ended on 10 May. Summer brought the same finishing position.

According to recent reports, A loss to GIANTX on 30 August kept the team out of the Summer playoffs. That defeat left the club absent from Worlds for the first time since 2016.

Recent findings suggest that 5 years of memories. it was an honour to see you grow into the person and player you are 🧡 https://t.co/F3TWY9WZqq pic.twitter.com/K3K3EQICZ1.

— FNATIC (@FNATIC) November 17, 2026.

Industry observers note that for the UK scene, the scale of change matters. Fnatic is one of the LEC’s best-supported clubs among British fans.

The club has also opened a search for a League of Legends General Manager. Its job advert says Fnatic goes into a rebuild in 2027. The newly introduced hire will run recruitment of players, coaches and staff, including transfers and benchings, and will manage the team’s budget.

Tech Report: Will GTA 6 break the internet? UK broadband operator braces for impact, saying "GTA 6 has been on our radar for a long time"

💡 Key Takeaways
  • As Grand Theft Auto 6 breaks pre-order records on the PlayStation and Xbox stores, and looks poised to break many more sales records once it launches next week, questions of whether it will also break the internet arise.
  • According to recent reports, major game releases register nationally for broadband use: we know this from an investigation into gaming downloads and how much they cost the environment we published in 2021.
  • Industry observers note that for this reason, Openreach - the organization that runs the largest broadband network in the UK - has been tracking Rockstar's latest game closely.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As Grand Theft Auto 6 breaks pre-order records on the PlayStation and Xbox stores, and looks poised to break many more sales records once it launches next week, questions of whether it will also break the internet arise. Collective network load will undoubtedly spike around its release - will regional infrastructure be able to bear it?

According to recent reports, major game releases register nationally for broadband use: we know this from an investigation into gaming downloads and how much they cost the environment we published in 2021. We also know that UK communications regulator Ofcom negotiates with gaming companies to try and avoid major game rolls out happening alongside major cultural occasions, such as sporting events, which are likely to spike broadband use. The network pipes can be clogged, and there's arguably never been a game as anticipated as GTA 6 to clog them.

Industry observers note that for this reason, Openreach - the organization that runs the largest broadband network in the UK - has been tracking Rockstar's latest game closely. "GTA 6 has been on our radar for a long time," Trevor Linney, Openreach's director for network technology, told Eurogamer. "We know from games like Fortnite and Call of Duty that a major release or patch can drive huge amounts of data across the network, so it'll be fascinating to see just how much GTA moves the needle. Our network and teams are ready, and GTA 6 is certainly one we'll be watching for a latest download record.".

Sources indicate that A spokesperson for Ofcom, meanwhile, said: "Broadband networks should be well placed to handle this download. Ofcom's Broadband Code of Practice means providers must give customers clear, realistic information and guarantee a minimum speed. If you’re not getting this, you may be able to leave your contract penalty-free. Check your speed now, so you can focus on the game rather than the loading screen." Ofcom has a website with sections devoted to broadband speeds and changing providers, in case you're interested.

Alongside yesterday's announcements that GTA 6 had become the most pre-ordered game in Xbox Store and PlayStation Store history, Sony and Microsoft shared strongly worded advice that players download the game ahead of time to avoid complications caused by "unprecedented demand". We saw last year what happened when Hollow Knight: Silksong arrived, causing chaos on Xbox, Steam, and Nintendo servers, and that game's reach was an order of magnitude less than GTA 6's. I don't recall a Selfridges store takeover in London for Silksong - do you?

The wait for GTA 6 is finally nearly over, as it arrives next Thursday, 19th November.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Joe Locke states he was totally unaware of the surprise post-credits scene at the end of VisionQuest... because it didn't come with his screeners.

"I didn't know Wanda was in it," Locke said on The View. "I watched the episodes a few months ago because they sent it to me. And then the day that episode came out, I saw everyone online talking about Wanda being back, and I'm like, 'Well, that's not true!' And then I watched and was like, 'Oh, okay, it is true!'".

Don't worry, Joe: It didn't come with our screeners, either. Ruiardh Mollica, who plays Tommy Maximoff in the show, also expressed on his personal Instagram story that he, too, was unaware of the post-credits scene. Either it was a last-minute decision, or Marvel decided to keep it a massive secret for a reason. Either way, the inclusion of the scene sent ticket pre-sales for Avengers: Doomsday sky-high, and made perfect sense for the 'family reunion' aspect of VisionQuest season 1, so it all worked out for the best.

It has been revealed that the scene sees good ol' Victor von Doom appear to resurrect Wanda Maximoff from the dead after she brought the Darkhold castle down on her at the end of Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness. When she wakes up, however, her eyes glow a ghastly bright green... implying that she is now under Doom's control. Ruh-roh!

Avengers: Doomsday hits UK cinemas on December 16 and worldwide on December 18. For more, check out how to watch the Marvel movies in order.

#63521. Keeping hold of Manufacturer of Heroes was essential for Relic to leave Sega, Relic CEO says – "Without it we would have been a dead studio"

📅 11 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1069 w)
📖 Baca
Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rockpapershotgun ↗ Open Full Page

Keeping hold of Manufacturer of Heroes was essential for Relic to leave Sega, Relic CEO says – "Without it we would have been a dead studio"

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1069 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that in the nearly 30 years since they opened their doors, Relic have been an enormously influential studio.
  • Without naming names Dowdeswell points out that there are "numerous examples" of studios that weren't able to survive on their name alone.
  • Recent findings suggest that dowdeswell joined Relic shortly after Sega acquired the studio in 2013.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that in the nearly 30 years since they opened their doors, Relic have been an enormously influential studio. Responsible for lauded RTS series Homeworld, Dawn of War, and Manufacturer of Heroes, they also dabbled in other genres with third-person shooter The Outfit and the original Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine. Yet, despite this history, in 2024, when Relic were negotiating their sale from Sega to UK investment firm Emona Capita, CEO Justin Dowdeswell knew the rights to Company of Heroes had to be part of the deal. "Without it we would have been a dead studio," he tells me.

Without naming names Dowdeswell points out that there are "numerous examples" of studios that weren't able to survive on their name alone. Not only did Relic need the ability to make more games in the series that they were known for, but they also needed the income from back catalogue sales a series like Company of Heroes provides.

Recent findings suggest that dowdeswell joined Relic shortly after Sega acquired the studio in 2013. This was in the immediate aftermath of publisher THQ's bankruptcy auction, where studios and franchises were sold off to the highest bidder. While Sega bought the studio, they didn't buy the licenses to everything Relic had created. "The other games that Relic made – Homeworld, Impossible Creatures, The Outfit... formative games in many people's memory – they were all split up, scattered," Dowdeswell indicates. "I think that was... I won't say a tragedy, but it's unfortunate because Relic is the home of those games. It would have been great for them to stay with the studio.".

Recent findings suggest that just as a hint of the messy history of acquisitions and auctions: this year we see Dawn of War 4 coming from studio King Art Games and published by Deep Silver. Deep Silver are a subdivision of Plaion, formerly called Koch Media, which was acquired by Embracer Group back when they were called THQ Nordic. Not that they were actually the THQ that originally published Relic's Dawn of War, Nordic Games renamed themselves THQ Nordic after they bought the THQ trademark at auction.

As for Homeworld, Borderlands developer Gearbox picked up the license to the sci-fi RTS in the bankruptcy auction, then contracted Blackbird Interactive's support on the remasters, before handing the latter lead development on Homeworld 3. That chain of events does have a more clear throughline to Relic's past however, as Blackbird was created by two of Relic's co-founders Rob Cunningham and Jon Aaron Kambeitz. (Speaking of studios struggling without the series they made their name with, Blackbird was on the verge of bankruptcy before Gearbox got in touch with the Homeworld work. So we very nearly existed in a world where they never got to make the brilliant Homeworld: Deserts of Kharak and Hardspace Shipbreaker.).

Sources indicate that anyway, this is all getting side-tracked. Back to holding onto Company of Heroes when separating from Sega. "Fighting for Company of Heroes when leaving Sega was crucial because I already lamented the fact that the other games didn't come with Relic," Dowdeswell states. "I couldn't really imagine a Relic where none of the games that the studio has made and was known for were any longer part of it.".

Relic and latest owner UK investment firm Emona Capital LLP were able to negotiate Company of Heroes as part of the sale from Sega and since then the studio has spent the past two years focusing largely on supporting the WW2 RTS and restoring their back catalogue. The most recent upgrade is the massive 3.0 patch to mark the series' 20th anniversary. Which, among many changes, overhauls the Mediterranean-set RTS game's special effects, audio systems, NPC AI, and makes significant changes to the singleplayer grand strategy-inspired Italy campaign, as well as adding a whole set of autumn and winter-themed assets for community map makers. They've also released a series of DLCs adding new factions to Company of Heroes 3's skirmishes and multiplayer, re-released Dawn of War with a definitive edition and announced they're doing the same for the original Company of Heroes, along with Blackbird Interactive's help. Dowdeswell states foundation building masks a lot of the work going on behind the scenes: "We now self-publish all of this," he explains. "There were a number of things that we had to learn, skills we had to develop, capacity and capability that we had to build at the studio very, very quickly.".

I ask if it was always the blueprint to focus on their back catalogue, or if they had prepares to release new games. Dowdeswell says spending four years quietly working on a new game wasn't an option: "It's almost impossible to do it that way because of the current climate in the industry. We don't have a financial safety net." Though, the team do have larger ambitions. "We want to make new games, we want to provide a modern Relic game," Dowdeswell says. "That ambition to re-establish Relic as an innovator in this strategy space is a substantial part of what drives our creative direction on new games." Focusing on updating Firm of Heroes 3, releasing DLC for the game, and making definitive editions of Dawn of War and the original Company of Heroes is what gets the studio to the place it can make a new game.

Recent findings suggest that however, Dowdeswell resists any framing of Relic's work on Company of Heroes 3 as spinning their wheels or resting on their laurels while working toward a latest game. He argues the game "sits in between" Relic's past and its future: "It's an established game that came out three years ago, but it's also a way for us to take some chances, experiment a little bit, and while doing that staying really closely connected to the players, That's what the idea was behind the updates because it was a way to have very quick iterations and touch points with players and provide, honestly, a way for us to fund everything in the future.".

Industry observers note that as to what Relic is making next, Dowdeswell wouldn't say. Though, he revealed trying genres besides real-time strategy was "almost a certainty", before adding "I don't think it's going to be a vast departure for where we are, so it will still be strategic gameplay. We're not going to go build a racer.".

10 Best Metroidvania Boss Fights of the 2020s (So Far)

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1625 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Modern Metroidvanias, largely influenced by Soulsborne titles' formula, have heavily emphasized boss fights as the core of their gameplay, and I'm quite happy about it.
  • I can't deny my absolute fascination with formidable adversaries that test my reflexes, adaptability, and resolve, and this genre in particular has understood those keys better than most.
  • With each passing year, we not only receive more outstanding Metroidvanias but also specifically more experiences that utilize this gameplay concept to its fullest potential, usually representing the high points of their respective adventures.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Modern Metroidvanias, largely influenced by Soulsborne titles' formula, have heavily emphasized boss fights as the core of their gameplay, and I'm quite happy about it.

I can't deny my absolute fascination with formidable adversaries that test my reflexes, adaptability, and resolve, and this genre in particular has understood those keys better than most.

With each passing year, we not only receive more outstanding Metroidvanias but also specifically more experiences that utilize this gameplay concept to its fullest potential, usually representing the high points of their respective adventures.

Therefore, if you're like me and fascinated by a good duel with health bars and numerous phases, I invite you to read this list of the ten best Metroidvania boss fights of the 2020s (so far).

Well Dweller is a magnificent video game that, as the pinnacle of Kyle Thompson's craft, is brimming with spectacular yet accessible special bosses, such as The Queen.

The plethora of sequences, attacks, and projectiles that unfold during your final encounter is breathtaking, truly connecting with the idea that royalty rules with an iron fist because they actually possess the power to dominate others.

Disfiguring the face of your family's kidnapper is fitting for a title that's cozy on the surface but profoundly dark beneath it, materialized in a demanding fight in terms of positioning and movement that makes you feel like you're constantly swimming against the tide.

While the bosses in Well Dweller wouldn't be my primary reason for recommending this gem, The Queen, in particular, demonstrates the wide variety that Metroidvanias can offer, rather than simply reducing everything to dodging and attacking in between.

The entirety of Shinobi: Art of Vengeance is a moving marvel with choreography worthy of the best action sequences of recent years, thanks to the tremendous animations and magnificent display of audiovisual effects for bosses like Lord Ruse.

Its imposing arena and visual design provide the perfect backdrop to prepare you for the epic duel this tormented villain has in store, whose tragic origin story is only surpassed by the way his darkness permeates the fight.

What was once an honorable man surrenders his body and mind to an abject power that threatens the balance of the world, making it fitting that his fight resembles that of a ninja against a natural phenomenon capable of defying the laws of physics.

The gameplay is very satisfying, forcing you to use all the tools and combos at your disposal to evade and attack effectively, leveraging the title's glorious combat system, where, after dominating all the combos, you can truly perform a martial aesthetic feast.

The gimmick of having you constantly face a boss throughout a game is quite difficult to pull off successfully, but Gilroy, the Administrator from Ender Magnolia: Bloom in the Mist is a perfect example of when it's done well.

While the game's roster of bosses is quite varied, its developers understand the magic of fighting a humanoid adversary who, true to FromSoftware's philosophy, forces you to decipher a rapid and relentless attack pattern where the slightest mistake is punished with death.

Gilroy is a challenge that evolves in each of the three encounters, always leaving room for more secrets, until the final confrontation arrives with the full weight of the narrative, where you must fight one last battle that is as bittersweet as it is satisfying.

Ender Magnolia is a game that relies heavily on its aesthetics, story, and music to amplify its emotional impact, so the campaign reaches its peak when you must defeat this recurring and memorable figure one last time.

Speaking of recurring tropes throughout video game history, Tunic presents The Heir as the final boss very early in the story, allowing you to become familiar with its power while simultaneously understanding how far you are from completing your journey.

Games with such a strong emphasis on exploration and adventure as this one must make every element contribute to the sense of progress, and nothing demonstrates your growth more than a superpowered entity with whom you gradually close the gap.

Checking your evolution through repeated attempts over many hours is captivating, as is finally realizing you're on par and understanding the remarkable challenge it truly holds, hidden behind complex and rapid combos, diverse area attacks, and far more resistance than you initially expected.

The Heir's fight is simple but makes the most of Tunic's functional mechanics, and the satisfaction of delivering the final blow after so many hours lost and disoriented is unparalleled.

Ori and the Will of the Wisps constantly surpasses itself with each new boss, escape sequence, and scene, culminating in a Shriek encounter that ranges from breathtaking to utterly devastating.

The franchise is a relentless litany of tragedies and victims that exact a toll on the kindness of those who suffer them, leading you to confront a majestic yet deeply traumatized owl amidst what appears to be the end of the universe.

The screen seems to crumble as your confrontation with Shriek unfolds dynamically, with both combat and platforming sections taking place as the boss moves in and out of the frame with truly enviable dynamism.

More than just a boss fight, the sequence feels like a genuine battle where a force of nature truly wants to defeat you; sensations enhanced by the magnificent soundtrack and the sheer madness of particles and colors displayed during the fight.

Fighting Vahram in his godlike form inside the borders of time itself is among those images that stay with you forever, something Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown does quite regularly.

These former brothers-in-arms clash in a magnificent duel where time freezes and reverses, beams of light and swords appear from all sides, and your adversary manipulates the laws of physics as if they were clay, making it a truly spectacular show.

As you whittle down his health and he becomes cornered, the fight's complexity increases considerably, building to a tremendous crescendo where you feel the climax approaching and the adrenaline surging.

Vahram is one of those bosses who can destroy you dozens of times in a row and you'll still be happy, because he's so well and precisely designed that each new opportunity to fight him again feels like a gift.

True final bosses are usually the ultimate display of difficulty, depth, and passion that a Metroidvania has to offer, including Shii in MIO: Memories in Orbit.

Fighting the companion who guided you throughout the story not because of some villainous adversity, but because of a genuine conflict of beliefs about what constitutes the most desirable outcome, is heartbreaking yet captivating, especially given the challenge that awaits.

Shii lives up to his title, offering a multi-layered duel that demands you be as adept at recognizing openings as you are at dodging, jumping, dashing, grappling, flying, and more to evade its endless array of varied and omnidirectional attacks.

The boss also flies, vanishes, glides, and crawls in an organic clash that makes the most of MIO: Memories in Orbit's environment and mechanics, resulting in an absolute delight.

Blasphemous 2 boasts one of the most fluid and satisfying combat systems in the entire genre, but none exploit its flow state's sweet satisfaction quite like Eviterno, Last Desecrator.

While the rest of the game is relatively manageable, this timeless warrior subverts expectations and delivers the beating of your life, proving that all the challenges you've overcome so far were just the tip of the iceberg he embodies.

Far from the abominations and colossi you face during your crusade, the title presents, in its climax, a knight equal to you whose speed, power, and versatility demand pixel-perfect decision-making every second, regardless of your build.

The best bosses are the ones that push you to your limits, and considering Eviterno penalizes even a millisecond off-timing or being a pixel too close, he's a clear contender for the decade's finest.

Eigong is a mentor to our protagonist in Nine Sols both in story and gameplay, as no other encounter teaches you to appreciate its prodigious combat system so profoundly.

There are fierce contenders throughout the campaign, though the one tasked with opposing Yi at the very end exponentially raises the demands of mechanical control, as any performance less than perfect will result in the same outcome: a return to the checkpoint.

With three hellish phases brimming with rapid and agile movements—horizontal and vertical, parryable and unparryable, close and long range—it's an unstoppable barrage of abilities unless you know Yi's powers like the back of your hand.

Only absolute, unwavering concentration will give you a chance against Eigong, whose defeat quickly transforms from a painful climb into one of the most magical memories a Metroidvania has ever offered.

Being the only one on the entire list who isn't the game's final boss, which already hints at her unparalleled quality, Skarrsinger Karmelita is Hollow Knight: Silksong's highest point.

That Team Cherry's masterpiece has the genre's best boss this decade is undeniable, with representatives like Trobbio, Second Sentinel, Cogwork Dancers, and Lace to justify it, but ultimately it's the queen of the ants who gets the recognition.

It's a majestic encounter from the very beginning, leading you through the halls of a theater with her glorious singing, and then, after gifting you her minions as an offering to start the fight with full silk, appearing on stage to give you the concert of your life.

The song, setting, art direction, attacks, rhythm, duration... Everything is perfectly timed to ensure a flawless experience, whether it takes you one try or a thousand (which is more likely).

Skarrsinger Karmelita, I dare say, is among the best bosses in video game history and a perfect example of why this gameplay concept has gained so much relevance over the years.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Marvel Cosmic Invasion was a bit of a dream game for me; I loved the X-Men arcade game in the '90s, so when Tribute Games released the excellent Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Shredder's Revenge in 2022, I immediately hoped they'd revitalize other licensed brawler franchises released by Konami in the late '80s and early '90s. While we still haven't heard any word of a latest brawler starring The Simpsons, Tribute did follow up its Turtle triumph with Marvel Cosmic Invasion, another throwback side-scrolling beat 'em up, this time starring Marvel's mightiest.

I played through Marvel Cosmic Invasion multiple times and had a blast, but I moved on swiftly, as I didn't feel the need to collect different palette-swaps of the many heroes on offer. Even after Cyclops and The Thing joined the roster as DLC in May, I still saw Cosmic Invasion as a game in the rearview. That changes this week, as The Siege of Castle Doom not only adds two additional playable characters (Invisible Woman and Doctor Doom), but also a mode that has the potential to bring me back for more runs for the foreseeable future.

Seeing that Annihilus is threatening the universe, Doom decides to take matters into his own hands. Unfortunately, much in the way that it seems that he may try to fix the multiversal incursions in the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday, Victor Von Doom's solution in Marvel Cosmic Invasion – the Cosmic Inductor – would lead to untold death and destruction. In The Siege of Castle Doom, you select your team and fight your way through various floors of the stronghold belonging to the man who is perhaps Marvel's greatest villain. Your goal is to fight through the winding, randomized hallways of Castle Doomstadt, charging Reed Richards' Stabilizer and tactically bolstering your team along the way, before Doctor Doom can enact his initiative.

As for the new playable characters, Doctor Doom is less agile, but his attacks pack a whallop, while Invisible Woman's force fields and speed make her the more versatile pick. I don't know that I see either of them replacing my mains from the base game, but I had fun experimenting with them throughout this mode. Regardless of which character you choose from the expanding roster, you still must traverse Castle Doomstadt before Doom achieves his objective.

Fighting through waves of enemies across differently themed and booby-trapped rooms, you encounter all manner of foes from the base game, as well as new minion types from Doom. When you defeat enemies, they drop batteries that charge your Stabilizer, letting you even the odds and stop Doom. Conversely, each time an enemy hits your character, it charges Doom's Cosmic Inductor, inching him closer to victory and making his minions faster and stronger in the process. As you might expect, the rooms get harder the deeper you go, and while each player starts with two characters to swap between, if a character completely depletes their health, they're gone for good, making it even tougher. As such, you need to keep your eyes on each character's health and swap them out when it makes sense.

In a recent development, as you complete each room, you can choose which path to take to augment your characters with new special abilities. True to the roguelite structure, as you complete rooms, you can also buff your characters' stats within the run. Certain rooms offer extra batteries to help your Stabilizer charge, while others offer new and upgraded equipment. There's also one that promises random events that can easily alter the trajectory of your run for better or worse. Though I often enjoyed boosting attack stats to make enemies less like damage sponges, I had to balance that against buffing their health to keep them alive and charging the Stabilizer to have a fighting chance.

It has been revealed that beyond the in-run upgrades and modifiers, you can also amp up the action run-over-run through upgrades in Reed's Lab, which add to the pool of modifiers you can select from at the start of each run. The expansion also adds new palettes for existing heroes, plus new music by composer Tee Lopes. While I've only done a few runs of The Siege of Castle Doom (each taking between 45 and 90 minutes, depending on how successful you are), I feel a revitalized sense of excitement for Marvel Cosmic Invasion. Tribute claims completionists can spend upwards of 15 hours in this new mode, which has me champing at the bit to dive back into what will likely be my primary way of interacting with Marvel Cosmic Invasion going forward.

Marvel Cosmic Invasion – The Siege of Castle Doom is available today on all platforms, and it is a strong addition to an already great game. You can read our review of the base version of Marvel Cosmic Invasion here.

Back in 2021—which feels like an age ago now—Rockstar added a weird picture to a house in San Andreas in its Grand Theft Auto: The Trilogy—The Definitive Edition. It captured a small UFO hovering over a cream coloured bungalow with two palm trees in its front garden. It stood out because unlike some of the other pictures, players weren't really sure where it came from, but now we have an answer: It came from the future—bet you didn't see that one coming.

Recent findings suggest that well, actually some people did see it coming as they took it to be a tiny easter egg for a future GTA's Florida-setting, which we now know is correct. The picture wasn't just hinting at the location of Grand Theft Auto 6, though, it actually depicts a real location that players can go visit.

Industry observers note that I saw this thanks to xGarbett's easter egg video, but rapidly sent our own Mollie Taylor after the scent. After driving around Belville for a little while we found it: the UFO house. Mystery solved—or was it? Well as it turns out you can go into this house during the day and inside is yet another mystery.

Walking into the garage of this home, players will be met by a sprawling mind map plastered across the wall with "IT'S A SIMULATION" written in major red letters in the middle. Oh dear, an NPC has gained sentience.

There are other phrases across the cork board such as:.

I'm no psychologist, but this may be an glitch.

We didn't encounter the owner of this house, luckily, but there were brochures scattered around about a boat. Seems like he's going to try and head for the open ocean in a bid to break through the map and finally gain freedom. Good luck buddy, I wish you well. Hopefully, if it all goes sideways out there the jetski dog will help him out—that'll probably make it on the conspiracy dream board.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Xbox boss Asha Sharma has confirmed Wolfenstein 3 is in development at MachineGames, the Swedish studio behind the acclaimed Wolfenstein: The Newly introduced Order, Wolfenstein 2: The New Colossal, and 2024's celebrated Indiana Jones and the Great Circle. Additionally, she revealed Doom developer idSoftware - one of the Microsoft-owned studios heavily impacted by sweeping Xbox job cuts earlier this year - is now working on a new game.

Sources indicate that sharma has, of course, been on a bit of a PR offensive of late, positioning herself alongside snippets of positive news at a time Xbox is embroiled in a massive business "reset" effort that has resulted in proposed studio closures and mass layoffs that will ultimately see 3,200 Xbox employees lose their jobs. This week's Wolfenstein 3 reveal similarly arrived in the form of a tweet posted directly from her social media account.

Recent findings suggest that "Wolfenstein 3 is officially in production at MachineGames," Sharma wrote on X. "One of gaming's most important franchises, and a team that has done remarkable work bringing it forward. Looking forward to sharing more." As for idSoftware's new project, confirmation of that - again attributed directly to Sharma - appeared in a post on Bethesda's website. "Slaughter Mode comes to Doom: The Dark Ages - Revelations on Monday," she wrote, "and the team is already working on its next game.".

Sources indicate that in July, sweeping job cuts at Xbox resulted in 96 of idSoftware's 136 employees being laid off in a move one former team member described as a "bloodbath". Since then, idSoftware co-studio director Marty Stratton has attempted to downplay the cuts, recently insisting the studio was "doing great". He added id was "working more closely than ever" with MachineGames - a studio which appears to have escaped Sharma's restructuring efforts so far.

This week's Wolfenstein and idSoftware news follows similar efforts by Xbox to reassure fans their favourite franchises are unaffected by the recent layoffs. Shortly after substantial job cuts at Bethesda were confirmed, the company moved to insist The Elder Scrolls 6 was still "on the way" and that its plans were "unaffected" (the company has since released a trailer announcing its subtitle). It also confirmed a new Fallout game was in development.

Xbox's year of bad news - which includes ongoing boycott efforts relating to Microsoft's controversial involvement with the Israeli military - comes as the division celebrates its 25th anniversary. Earlier this week, Sharma shared a memo to staff marking the occasion, albeit one in which she seemingly championed a gen-AI future for games development, enthusing that, "A small team will be able to build worlds that today demand hundreds of developers".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Content warning for discussion of extreme violence and self-harm.

In a recent development, you haven't died in a videogame till you've died in Casualties: Unknown, a profoundly unwholesome cousin of Spelunky that simulates injury, infection and sensory distress with the same gusto Crusader Kings 3 reserves for papal politics. This is an intricate and imaginative celebration of pain - not merely an exacting survival game full of gauges to manage, but a laboratory study of just how many ways an animal body can feel, before it finally gives up the ghost.

I am one of a million canine hominids, created to undergo spectacular indignities by vicious human scientists, in a universe of suffering that spans several games from developer Orsoniks. I am the sorrowing vat-grown pup of a conclave of star-faring Dr Moreaus. My task is to collect... something, some gadget of great importance, from a cave on a deathly planet, located beneath three kilometres of booby-trapped and infested, poisonous and hateful rock.

Sources indicate that presently, I am trying to burrow into a sealed titanium drop pod with my bare paws, so that I can sleep somewhere warm. Too warm, in fact. The drop pod heaters feel like they were vindictively designed to discourage occupants from lingering, but I'm finding that dehydration is easier to address than hypothermia - there are pools of groundwater around that harbour only a slight risk of "minorly" fouling my intestines. So into the pod we go. After ripping away a layer of rubber, I smash some glass panes and promptly step in the fragments.

My computer screams, a hideous jangle of chords and static. The interface becomes a fritzing, flexing sphincter of pinks and reds. My punctured dogsbody flops and writhes, spurting yellow fluids and gobs of unintelligible text, ignoring my button inputs. They are my avatar no longer. They have been reduced to a squirming facet of the simulation's agony.

I gawp in guilt and terror at the status bar, now jammed with pulsing icons, then switch to my health display and determine that I am "bleeding catastrophically" from my right hind paw. I need to bandage that paw promptly. But first, I need to remove the glass. This takes the form of a 'minigame' in which I guide a shaking clawed hand with the cursor, hauling out shards even as my poor character threatens to pass out from the ordeal.

Sources indicate that I've got two of five shards out when the earthquake kicks in. Already doubled over and delirious, my pioneering pooch is launched over the nearest cliff. They fall about 50 feet, rag-dolling off crags with a concussive whump, till they smash into a flooded wooden platform. The anatomical diagram on the health screen lights up like a wickerman. I don't appear to have broken any bones, but everything is hurting. What's more, I am soaking wet and hypothermia is taking hold, stretching blue veins through the clenching colours of my pain. The screen begins to look like some exotic, putrid flower.

Wringing my hands, I allow my mutant mutt about 10 seconds to recover from the shock of the fall, then open the health screen again and slowly tug out the last three shards of glass. It's actually easier than before, but not for the happiest of reasons: landing on my head appears to have numbed my senses. There will be longer term consequences, probably. Now I just have to bind the wound… except that I must have dropped my roll of gauze, while tumbling through the abyss. With sirens still flashing on the HUD, I peer about for a cave plant or other source of crafting materials. On the other side of the platform, I spy the corpse of another pitiful lab experiment. Perhaps there's a bandage in that huddle of clothes?

I hoist my sagging and babbling starpup to their feet, and limp over to investigate. Then I step on a pressure plate, and a six foot blade shoots up through my left thigh.

The screen is almost obliterated by crimson snow. The noise is... indescribable. I open the health screen again to assess the damage but I can't, because my dogperson has fallen into utter derangement. They want to be rid of their too-fruitful arteries, their stinking yellow blood. The clawed hand reappears, and I am forced to rake my own torso with it to regain access to the controls.

In a recent development, I am now gushing my life out from head to foot. Going by my plummeting heart rate, I have about 30 seconds to burn before I lose consciousness forever. I see no means of recovery, and I can't bear to watch my character bleed out. So instead, I detonate the chip embedded in their brain - the same chip responsible for the interface's rash of icons and warnings. According to the subsequent mission report print-out, my canine pioneer was feeling "dejected" when their head exploded.

The worst thing about the scenario I've just recalled is that it represents Casualties: Unknown at its least punishing. All of the above took place in the first of the game's 11 biomes - each procedurally generated, and 300 metres high - on the default "Tough" run setting. Resources are more plentiful up here, while active threats are fewer. There is scope to faff about and prepare - gathering plant matter for a crude woven bag, so I don't have to carry everything in my hands or mouth or tuck it into the folds of my body. There is time to crack open supply crates, and craft an implement of some kind.

The main danger, traps aside, is falling. Casualties: Unknown's terrain generator is not your pal. As regards the opening couple of biomes, at least, it works like a broken muck spreader, ejecting a mix of filthy clogs and particles that snag your jumps and often oblige you to dig through rock and gravel. You'll frequently be doing that in the dark, and even the smallest of exertions takes a perceptible toll – whimpers of effort, wheezing breath, double vision. The one major consolation is that you can wall-jump and slide down surfaces, a mocking touch of Prince of Persia.

Industry observers note that still, further down is where life gets truly unpleasant. There are sonic traps in certain biomes that cause brain damage and massive hemorrhaging. There are vast, rumbling insects you simply cannot afford to get close to, because they are guaranteed to bite off a limb. And the absolutely dreadful thing about that is that it won't necessarily end your run: given a tourniquet and antibiotics, you may yet pull through. Perhaps you'll find or craft a prosthetic. The game's characters are, in general, astonishingly tough for all their immense capacity for anguish.

Casualties: Unknown is a brilliant and unusual piece of design, uninhibited by any commercialised and sanitary notions of 'fun' and 'difficulty'. It's committed to recreating the surge of sensation through flesh. There's something intrinsically vital about this. Like Project Citadel, perhaps, its extravaganzas of torment are about feeling more present and alive in a twisted world, more in control. I'm not the writer to discuss this, and I know little about the developer's circumstances, but it feels like an exploration of trans survival in the face of a brutalising biopolitical regime: the online wiki notes that the game's zoomorphic Experiments or "Expies" have their own ideas about gender, though I'm finding it tricky to distinguish those accounts from the categorisations of the evidently unfriendly boffins who engineered them.

I would like to get to the bottom of things. I would like to find that goddamn gadget. I would like to return to the surface and massacre the bastards who sent me down here. Still, I'm not sure I have the willpower to witness everything my avatar might have to endure: barotrauma, sepsis, strokes, ruptured ears, hallucinations... As I've hopefully made clear throughout this piece, it remains an open question as to whether I am them, or simply one of their human tormentors. You can read more on Steam and Itch.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that nongshim RedForce have brought 2022 world champion Deft back to the LCK and paired him again with Kingen and Pyosik. The move follows an eighth-place 2026 for the club and comes days after BLG ended Korea's four-year hold on the World Championship.

In a recent development, kim ‘Deft’ Hyuk-kyu’s signing was confirmed on 19 November. The club used its official social media channels to make the announcement. Deft began his military service after the 2024 season ended.

The deal reunites him with two members of the DRX side that won the 2022 World Championship. Jungler Hong ‘Pyosik’ Chang-hyeon joined later the same day, alongside support Moon ‘Andil’ Gwan-bin. Top laner Hwang ‘Kingen’ Seong-hoon had re-signed a day earlier.

Sources indicate that deft’s signing was revealed at 7pm. The Pyosik and Andil additions that followed completed Nongshim’s five-man starting line-up, Inven Global reported. Mid laner Seon ‘Calix’ Hyeon-bin provides continuity. He has been with the organisation since 2021 and extended his deal on 18 November.

Industry observers note that deft brings a long winning record. He made his debut with MVP Blue in 2013. His titles include the LCK, the LPL, the Mid-Season Invitational and the 2022 World Championship.

Kingen first joined Nongshim for the 2025 season. Pyosik arrives after a difficult 2026 at DN SOOPers. That team lost a run of matches, and rookie Sharvel took his starting place.

In a recent development, the move had been signalled. About a month before the announcement, Sheep Esports reported from Korean sources that Nongshim planned to sign Deft. The same report said rookie AD carry Diable would need a new team.

In a recent development, the signings mark a sharp change of direction after a poor year. Once the league campaign was over, the team lasted just a single match in the play-ins.

Recent findings suggest that the deal lands days after a setback for the whole league. Bilibili Gaming’s victory over Gen.G came at the Barclays Center in Latest York. It gave the organisation its first Summoner’s Cup.

Recent findings suggest that BLG won all four of its series against LCK teams at the tournament. Every LCK seed fell to the Chinese side on its way to the trophy. The title is also the LPL’s first since EDward Gaming won in 2021.

'Deft' has signed a contract as the new ADC of NS RedForce LCK Team.

Please look forward to and support Deft, who has written fresh history with an unbreakable spirit through countless trials, as he takes on new challenges and delivers great… pic.twitter.com/bHa1uJWwKV.

— NS RedForce (@NS_RedForce) November 19, 2026.

For Nongshim, a line-up built around three 2022 champions now has an international calendar to aim at. Riot Games has moved First Stand 2027 from Southeast Asia to China and renamed it First Stand: All In. It will be a one-off expanded edition with more teams and players.

Spain gets its debut as a Mid-Season Invitational host in 2027, with Valencia’s Feria de Valencia as the venue. Before that, Riot plans to publish First Stand: All In’s format and qualification process in January.
