10 Best N64 Racing Games That Still Hold Up Today

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1725 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Let's just get something out of the way swiftly – you don't necessarily have to be great at a genre of games to enjoy playing them.
  • In a recent development, most of the time I spent with racing games was on older consoles, most especially the Nintendo 64.
  • Industry observers note that there's a lot of great games here, and so to avoid unnecessary bias, I've ranked them in large part based on their review score aggregates.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Let's just get something out of the way swiftly – you don't necessarily have to be great at a genre of games to enjoy playing them. I mean, sure, I'm quite good at platformers and deckbuilders, and play a ton of those. But if I just stuck with them, I'd get bored eventually. Which is why I enjoy genres I'm not particularly good at, like racing games.

In a recent development, most of the time I spent with racing games was on older consoles, most especially the Nintendo 64. I clocked tons and tons of hours in many of them back then, and not just the most generic car racing games. I also played snowboarding games, water sports and even futuristic race car rallies. And honestly, every game on this N64 list still holds up today.

Industry observers note that there's a lot of great games here, and so to avoid unnecessary bias, I've ranked them in large part based on their review score aggregates. Though in some cases, I did shuffle the order a bit when common sense called for it. So get ready, get set, and let's go through some epic N64 racing games!

Sources indicate that nintendo doesn't always have the most luck with launch titles, at least when they're not heavy hitters like Mario or Zelda. Which is why I was so delighted with Pilotwings 64 heralding the upcoming console. It was very stylish, and built on the previous SNES adventure in great ways.

Your goal is to prove your stuff to earn a variety of pilot licenses in the game, and you'll have to accomplish some challenging feats. Those include autogyro, jet pack and hang gliding, even a human cannonball. Feats that aren't for the timid.

Industry observers note that even though the game is graphically less impressive today, the core gameplay still holds up, and offers a robust challenge and plenty of bonus activities for players. And thanks to the hard work Paradigm put in researching military vehicles and flight sims, Pilotwings 64 is just as relevant today as it was back then.

According to recent reports, it indicates the breadth of the racing game library on the N64 when the first futuristic racer isn't F-Zero X, but instead is Extreme-G. Which isn't a dig, mind you, since both games offered a lot. But for this particular adventure, the highlights were some really epic weapons like homing missiles and laser mines, as well as really innovative, gravity defying courses.

The game also featured frenetic deathmatches, which made sense on paper, but in execution were a bit muddled. Sure, there's the likes of capture the flag, competitive racing and battle mode, but they were less fun than they were stress inducing.

Industry observers note that the biggest reason Extreme-G isn't ranked higher on this list is likely due to the graphics, which were fine but not overly impressive or creative. Still, if you had a need for speed and didn't mind using powerful weapons, this was a thrilling adventure.

Sources indicate that while your mileage with arcade machines may vary, generally speaking they're big, bold and visually impressive. And that goes double for racing games like San Francisco Rush 2049. Thankfully, they ported it to the N64, and brought high-octane energy to Nintendo's console.

Recent findings suggest that what was most impressive about this adventure on consoles is that you could extend wings from your vehicles and glide in mid-air. You'll mostly use that in the stunt mode to rack up crazy points as you do complex maneuvers.

Best of all, you had a lot to unlock in San Francisco Rush 2049, including new cars and tracks. Meaning that even now, this is a racing game you'll be spending a lot of time playing on the Nintendo 64 and even PC.

Sources indicate that since the developer of the Wipeout series was owned by Sony Computer Entertainment, it makes sense most of the games weren't on Nintendo consoles. The one exception was Wipeout 64. While perhaps not a true sequel to Wipeout 2097, this standalone Nintendo adventure offered a lot to enjoy.

In a recent development, perhaps the most impressive way Wipeout 64 differentiated itself from the others in the series was a split screen allowing up to 4 players to play together. Even with that aside, the game offered robust anti-gravity racing and truly superior track design.

If you enjoy racers with a variety of weapons, great tracks and a variety of gameplay modes, this N64 game had you covered. That mentioned, perhaps the graphics were a step down from some of the other entries, but this was still a remarkably fun game.

Much as I love Nintendo, sometimes you have to wait a long while between sequels. Zelda fans know what I'm talking about, but even they didn't have to wait as long for a sequel as fans of the original Excitebike on the NES. 16 years later, it got its first sequel in Excitebike 64.

In a recent development, as you might expect, the jump from 2D to 3D was a substantial one, and you're capable of epic tricks in Excitebike 64. Brake, slide, turbo boost and even tilt the bike in midair, there's a lot of options. Better yet, the various playable athletes have distinct stats, allowing players to pick the one that works best with their style.

My favorite aspect of the game is playing through the extensive season mode, unlocking newly introduced content along the way. But the one part of the game that really sets it apart is using the track editor to make your own insane obstacle courses.

Racing games on Nintendo consoles often lean into the fantastical, patterning themselves after the likes of Mario Kart. But one that really took a massive swing was Diddy Kong Racing. Not only did it feature different vehicles ranging from car to hovercraft to aeroplane, but there were also several different drivers and even a story involving the nefarious Wizpig.

It has been revealed that like any of the Donkey Kong games, there's a lot of unlockables here, including obtaining amulet pieces to battle the true final boss. And if that wasn't enough, you'll even deal with actual boss battles of sorts, and use balloons to gain a huge variety of powerups, ranging from missiles to speed boosts and shields.

Best of all, Diddy Kong Racing was quite pretty for the time, and the graphical style still looks great years later. Sure, it could get a bit repetitive, but this was still a really outstanding game you'd need to play on Nintendo 64.

I mentioned earlier that I'm not the best at racing games, but I'm especially bad when they're on water. Which perhaps makes Wave Race 64 especially intimidating. That said, if you put in enough practice time, even a rookie at the genre would find themselves loving this innovative and stunt-filled racing adventure.

In a recent development, playing against the clock while trying to steer your way around buoys and avoid the hazing of your opponent could be really tough. If you're skilled, you'll power up and go even faster, but if you fail, you'll get way behind. Thankfully, though, this is a quite attractive N64 game which is even better when racing against a friend.

According to recent reports, if you're more skilled at racing than me, you'll probably adore Wave Race 64. It's the sort of retro that still holds up today, and it offers a phenomenally fun time, assuming you can react promptly to the choppy waters.

Even though I never played any skateboarding games, I really adored Snowboard Kids. I'm not sure what it was about this N64 adventure, but it hooked me hard. Maybe it was the cute, cartoony graphics, or the simple yet well balanced gameplay. But this was one of those games I found myself playing again and again.

The simple hook of the game is doing tricks while airborne to get coins, and then using them to buy powerups on tracks. You can have active and support items, such as hurling rocks at your opponents or turning temporarily invisible.

Industry observers note that perhaps the most surprising aspect of Snowboard Kids was that it was published by Atlus, who are usually known for JRPGs. But this is just one of those games that is still a ton of fun today, which I can attest to having played it recently with my close friends on their N64.

It has been revealed that even though I'm not amazing at racing games, I spent many, many hours playing Mario Kart 64. I barely touched Super Mario Kart, didn't do much with the later entries, but that N64 game was one I kept returning to with friends.

There was just something about this game that made it one of the most iconic entries in the longrunning series. Maybe it was the quirky cast of Mario characters, maybe it was tracks like Rainbow Road. But this was a truly fun racing game that appealed to players of various abilities.

It has been revealed that mix in various engine classes, a wide class of racers and amazingly fun attack items, and you have a great game in Mario Kart 64. But if that wasn't enough, it also features some of the best courses in the series, complete with really catchy tunes.

If you have a need for speed, you need look no further than F-Zero X. This futuristic series featured some of the most blisteringly fast courses and crazy racers you'll see in any series. And honestly, F-Zero X is still probably one of the best racers ever. So even though it's shameful we haven't gotten a sequel, you might not need it either.

Industry observers note that death Race offered a truly unhinged way to play the game, and the randomness of X-Cup could keep you playing the game for a long time. So even though it's not the most graphically impressive game, the high framerate and fantasically weird drivers made this a worthy contender.

Plasma Powered hovercars turned made racing even more fun, and so long as you can keep up, you'll find one of the best racers ever in F-Zero X. Here's hoping it gets an even better followup on modern consoles one day.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that if you're playing GTA 6 on Xbox, you should turn off your console's automatic upload feature or you could risk having your Xbox account suspended. An Xbox user on Reddit reported receiving a two-day, unrepealable ban for automatically uploading a 28-second clip of GTA 6 characters at the beach. According to the Reddit user, sangobar, the clip was almost immediately flagged by the Xbox Network for either violating the Xbox Community Standards or Microsoft Services Agreement terms (the email they received from Xbox doesn't specify which). However, the user claims the clip only demonstrated characters in beachwear and the clip was therefore incorrectly flagged.So, to avoid the risk of an Xbox ban it is better to be safe than sorry, to disable your Xbox automatic upload feature, and to understand what Xbox's guidelines are around the content you can upload to the Xbox Network.

Automatic uploads to the Xbox Network are enabled as standard on Xbox, meaning the GTA 6 clips you capture on your console are automatically uploaded to the Xbox Network. To turn off your Xbox Series X's automatic uploads feature, follow these steps:.

One Drive is more lenient in what you can upload, but if you'd rather not automatically upload any of your GTA 6 capture, it's best to set both it and Xbox Network to 'Don't Upload'.

GTA 6 clips could potentially violate the 'Keep your content clean' term of the Xbox Community Standards, specifically the 'Make stuff that's suitable for all audiences rule', which states: "The Xbox community must be friendly and accessible to everyone, this isn't the appropriate place for sexual content. Keep your public posts and messages suitable for all ages and audiences.".

According to Xbox, some examples of content that could violate this term include sharing or distributing non-consensual intimate imagery, links or imagery that displays pornography, screenshots or game clips that include mature sexual content, custom gamerpics that contains nudity, lewd messages to other players, and distasteful or inappropriate pictures. In other words, be careful before sharing images or clips of GTA 6's more mature content, like GTA 6 strip clubs.

Industry News: Watch Diablo 4 reveal the second class coming with Lord of Hatred here

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Blizzard has recently been celebrating its major running games by hosting substantial livestreams to reveal some major changes, and it’s now Diablo’s turn.
  • The Diablo 30th Anniversary Spotlight is set to kick off today at 2pm PT, 5pm ET, 10pm GMT.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Blizzard has recently been celebrating its major running games by hosting substantial livestreams to reveal some major changes, and it’s now Diablo’s turn. The Diablo series is 30 years-old, so this all just ties in nicely with some of the reveals planned for tonight’s showcase.

The Diablo 30th Anniversary Spotlight is set to kick off today at 2pm PT, 5pm ET, 10pm GMT.

The biggest reason why you might want to tune in is, of course, that a whole chunk of the event will focus on Diablo 4. Blizzard will unveil the second class coming to the game with the Lord of Hatred expansion. The developer, of course, released the first of two classes - Paladin - immediately at the upcoming expansion’s initial reveal back in December.

It has been revealed that lord of Hatred is set to arrive April 28, and there’s even more it’s bringing to the core game that will be shown off during the livestream. Blizzard said we can expect a deeper look at the revamped skill trees, as well as endgame mechanics and features Lord of Hatred is set to introduce.

It has been revealed that beyond Diablo 4 itself, the showcase will feature updates on Diablo Immortal, and even Diablo 2: Resurrected. Blizzard hasn’t been teasing any other announcements, but many still hold out hope for a proper Diablo 1 remaster.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that slay the Spire 2, which released into early access earlier this year, is expanding once more with a major latest beta enhancement. This introduces the deckbuilder's first new character since launch - a whimsical musician armed with a bow - alongside two new modes, and more.

When Slay the Spire 2 arrived back in March, it was to much enthusiastic acclaim. Eurogamer's Bertie Purchie is a big fan, and has trumpeted its successes on multiple occasions, calling the sequel's co-op mode "transformative". And it was a commercial hit too, managing to shift over 5m copies in just a month of release. All of which means there are plenty of eyes on Slay the Spire 2, eager to see what developer MegaCrit does next.

Recent findings suggest that so far major updates have brought the likes of buffs, balance adjustments, art updates, UI improvements, bug fixes, and more - and MegaCrit has also made other substantial adjustments including the jettisoning of third act boss Doormaker, after it decided the encounter was overly complex. And now, as 2026 nears its conclusion, the studio has released its "biggest (beta) patch yet", including a sweep of major additions.

It has been revealed that as per MegaCrit's v0.113.0 patch notes, the headliner is The Fool; Slay the Spire 2's first newly introduced character, who's described as a "silly musician who wields a bow". Unsurprisingly, The Fool doesn't arrive in their final form, and the studio says it expects to make a "great number of content and balance changes" before the character is ready for the main branch.

According to recent reports, accompanying The Fool are two latest game modes: Blitz and Dread. Blitz is described as a "condensed and chaotic" mode focused on deckbuilding. Unlocked after completing an Ascension run of any difficulty, it comes with five levels of Ascension shared across all characters. "The Merchant's wares feel a bit off," MegaCrit teases, "the map is gone, and Gold no longer matters??".

If you're looking for a more gruelling challenge, though, there's the "brutally difficult" new Dread mode, designed for players who've reached Ascension 10 on all characters, including The Fool. All ascension modifiers are enabled, according to MegaCrit, while bosses are stronger and buff all enemies found across their Act. And if that's still not enough to get your heart racing, MegaCrit notes curses will also pile up as you climb the Spire.

Beyond the headline stuff, v0.113.0 tweaks rest sites so they appear one floor earlier every act, and that's alongside the usual list of UI changes, art additions, nerfs, balance adjustments, and more. Full patch notes can be found on Steam.

Those players eager to put Slay the Spire 2's latest additions through their paces will need to enable the beta branch by right-clicking on Slay the Spire 2 in their Steam library and navigating to Properties > Game Versions & Betas and selecting 'public-beta' from the dropdown menu. MegaCrit notes the game's main branch has also been updated with all content and changes from the previous beta.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that warning: I'm probably about to make you feel old.
  • "You might ask yourself why, after all these years, we have put any more work into polishing and even adding new content to Bruma," the Beyond Skyrim team wrote in an article about the making of their version of Bruma's 2.0 update.
  • In a recent development, "The reason for this patch is actually a technical necessity," the modders continued.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that warning: I'm probably about to make you feel old. Today, November 11th 2026, is the 15th anniversary of Skyrim's release. The first one, before it was re-released on every other platform under the sun. Fittingly, one of its best expansion mods, Beyond Skyrim: Bruma, has gotten a beefy 2.0 revision to commemorate the occasion. Though, its creators insist the main driving force behind the update was more a matter of "technical necessity". There are upcoming quests, dungeons, and corners of Skyrim-era Cyrodiil to explore either way.

"You might ask yourself why, after all these years, we have put any more work into polishing and even adding new content to Bruma," the Beyond Skyrim team wrote in an article about the making of their version of Bruma's 2.0 update. "We are, of course, working on the whole province of Cyrodiil, and have made significant progress which you can follow on our social media. With so much still to go however, it was not out of nostalgia for a 15 year old Skyrim or a nearly 10 year old Bruma that we decided to revisit the first, and as of the time of writing, only major Beyond Skyrim release.

In a recent development, "The reason for this patch is actually a technical necessity," the modders continued. "The problem we have with Bruma is that it is based on a very very old version of Cyrodiil, which had been branched off of the main development build of Cyrodiil soon after Bruma's initial release in 2017. Whenever we updated Bruma, that meant we had to merge our changes into two builds, the public Bruma build and the WIP Cyrodiil build." So, in order to solve that behind-the-scenes problem, the team have developed a "build stripper" tool which means they'll not have to juggle maintaining two builds going forwards.

In a recent development, as laid out in the showcase video above, the modders have also used Bruma 2.0 as an opportunity to overhaul and add to vast chunks of their recreation of Cyrodiil's northernmost county. A fully voiced quest called All The Wrong Places which was cut from the mod's initial release, "several new dungeons and interiors", and an expansion of the explorable area all grace the changelog.

It has been revealed that more clothing, armour, weapons including the mod's first spear, enemies, spells, enchantments, world encounters, books, and treasure maps have also been shipped in with the 2.0 version, alongside overhauls to boss fights. A latest opening title splash will greet you upon entering Bruma for the first time, you should benefit from higher FPS as you explore the city, and the modders have even added an apple to Jerall View Inn. That's far from the end of the tweaks, so it's well worth reading the full list if you've got time.

Industry observers note that "All in all, Bruma 2.0 has been a massive journey, one where we have built and learned a lot, and most importantly, made many advancements to prepare us for the future," the modders concluded. If you've not given Beyond Skyrim: Bruma a go, I can very much recommend it. You might find yourself wandering back across the border into Skyrim once you've had your fill of nostalgia-tinged exploration and staring at a distant Imperial City you can't visit, but the original version's still good for hours of extra Elder Scrollsing.

You can grab the 2.0 version of Beyond Skyrim: Bruma from Nexus Mods. It's worth noting that you'll need "a recent version (1.6 or higher) of Skyrim: Special Edition's upgrade.esm and update.bsa" and a separate mod containing Beyond Skyrim's shared asset repository. Saves made using previous versions of Beyond Skyrim: Bruma won't work with the 2.0 update, so it's likely worth starting a fresh playthrough or relying on an in-progress one you've yet to use any mods with.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Indeed, the broader goals BF Studios shared with players in a new blog post reflect some of what Labs players already went hands-on with, while others are the result of work on long-standing challenges with both the game itself, as well as free-to-play mode Redsec.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ahead of the start of Battlefield 6’s Season 2 next week, Battlefield Studios has shared some insight into a few of the major goals the developer has with the Season 2 patch. The game’s second season was delayed in mid-January, and the developer even brought back Battlefield Labs to test out some of the new content and features coming with the new season.

Indeed, the broader goals BF Studios shared with players in a new blog post reflect some of what Labs players already went hands-on with, while others are the result of work on long-standing challenges with both the game itself, as well as free-to-play mode Redsec.

We know that Season 2 is introducing a substantial new map to the game, Contaminated, which the developer has been teasing. The map will indeed arrive in the first part of the season, and it’s going to do so alongside a new LTM that “introduces a new element of tactics.” A second, “high-intensity map” will debut later into the season, alongside another LTM where players battle through an underground base, in darkness.

The real meat of the blog post, however, covers the broader gameplay changes everyone will see once the new season kicks off. There’s a massive focus on player progression, especially when it concerns free-to-play Redsec players.

According to recent reports, challenges are being streamlined yet again, with more broad parameters that don’t require specific modes. Some, like dailies, will also allow for assists to count towards their criteria. Less restrictive challenges are welcome, but even more so is the faster battle pass progression.

Sources indicate that BF Studios is changing the rate at which battle pass Tokens are earned from career XP, and making it so they’re earnable by playing the game normally, and by completing weekly challenges. These changes should also help Redsec players, who will also benefit from faster career and weapon XP earn rates - across both battle royale, and Gauntlet. In general, the career experience should feel more rewarding, especially for earlier ranks.

Weapon balance and recoil are two areas that will continue to evolve in Battlefield 6, it seems, and Season 2 is specifically tackling recoil patterns to make them more consistent when you compensate for them.

Movement is being adjusted with the Season 2 patch, too, though thankfully it’s limited to general feel that touches areas like vaulting, ladder transitions, and acceleration curves. You should also see better continuity and consistency between animations and feel.

Audio is getting a pass with the upcoming patch, especially when it comes to footstep and interaction audio. This also extends to something the developer has been working on improving for a while, and it has to do with how the game decides which audio tracks to prioritise in busy situations.

Tomorrow, the full Battlefield 6 Season 2 trailer will be released, while a more detailed roadmap is expected by the end of this week.

GTA 6: Criminal Profile Guide

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that grand Theft Auto 6 has pulled plenty of mechanics from previous Rockstar titles, mostly focusing on revamping systems from previous GTA titles to make them feel incredibly in-depth.
  • Titled the Criminal Profile, both Jason and Lucia have distinct mental and social states based on how they handle their criminal and civilian lives around Leonida.
  • Grand Theft Auto 6’s Criminal Profiles are split into 5 different categories, with 4 that you can freely move between over the course of the game with little consequence.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that grand Theft Auto 6 has pulled plenty of mechanics from previous Rockstar titles, mostly focusing on revamping systems from previous GTA titles to make them feel incredibly in-depth. Even with this clear focus, some standout parts of other Rockstar titles have made the jump, including a revamp of Red Dead Redemption’s Honor System.

Titled the Criminal Profile, both Jason and Lucia have distinct mental and social states based on how they handle their criminal and civilian lives around Leonida. More so than Honor, the Criminal Profile affects various story moments, the game’s ending, and central mechanic functions from fight to fight. Let’s go over all 5 distinct states, what they offer, and how to ensure your Criminal Profile stays consistent.

Grand Theft Auto 6’s Criminal Profiles are split into 5 different categories, with 4 that you can freely move between over the course of the game with little consequence. These 5 tiers include Professional, Hardened, Violent, Psycho, and Irredeemable.

In a recent development, the profiles split down the middle: Professional and Hardened lean toward more controlled, non-lethal play, while Violent and Psycho reward wild aggression and quick thinking. Depending on your Criminal Profile, Jason and Lucia will act differently both toward each other and the events of the story.

Leaning one way on the scale or the other will also alter how you regain Focus in combat, allowing you to more accurately land shots and handle threats.

Professional and Hardened characters regain extra Focus via nonlethal gun takedowns, knockouts, and stealth takedowns.

Violent, Psycho, and Irredeemable characters gain boosts of Focus while landing headshots, lethal takedowns, or finishing off downed opponents.

Either way, your Criminal Profile rewards you for leaning into the identity of the profile, with extra Focus gain if you’re further along the scale (Professional or Psycho/Irredeemable).

It has been revealed that your Criminal Profiles are also a major factor in your eventual ending, heavily altering how Jason and Lucia act during major story events. In short, play how you want Lucia and Jason to act, either as professionals with an outer goal in mind, or as menaces who love the chaos they cause.

It has been revealed that irredeemable is an outlier, as there is no way to leave it once you achieve it. As the name implies, becoming Irredeemable requires repeated acts of incredible, heinous violence for the sake of it. An Irredeemable Criminal Profile is deliberately impossible to achieve by accident, as you’re given repeated warnings and chances to bring yourself back.

To earn each different Criminal Profile, you’ll need to play in the ways that each profile rewards, making the process of earning and benefiting from the profiles rather natural. For example, if you want to be seen as a Professional, play professionally. If you want to be a Psycho, walk around Leonida lashing out and kicking puppies, you sicko.

Taking on drug dens, robberies, and optional missions is a great way to earn points either way, especially if you want to correct your Criminal Profile before you continue the main story.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, since they released The Outer Worlds 2 around this time last year, the world has rather turned upside down for Obsidian. The studio lost a chunk of staff to Microsoft's mass layoffs and have pivoted to making a new Fallout game as a smaller group shoved underneath Bethesda in Xbox's corporate structure.

Given all that, The Outer Worlds 2's two-part story expansion is likely arriving in vastly different circumstances than those the studio might've imagined when they began sketching out DLC plans. Part one of the expansion, dubbed Side Effects Guaranteed, is set to release early next month.

Sources indicate that 'Oof, that looks a lot like it's been given what could turn out to be a death spot parked right in the aftermath of GTA 6's initial launch on consoles' is what I thought when I first saw that Side Effects Guaranteed's launch date is December 2nd. That stated, Obsidian have also made clear that a second DLC in the two-part narrative expansion to the sci-fi RPG is set to follow in spring 2027. So if this does turn out to be the end of the series, with a third Outer Worlds game at the moment looking very unlikely following the substantial upheaval I mentioned in the intro, at least it won't risk being totally obscured by a Rockstar crime game-shaped eclipse.

As for what this first dose of extra Outer Worlds 2 has in store for December, Obsidian summed it up as follows:.

Recent findings suggest that as you pursue the cure and set course for Elysium, an area home to former subjects of base game authoritarian collectivist faction the Protectorate, you'll be faced with the choice of whether to side with Gordon Hazen or Algernon Lankester. Both are agents of black market smuggling organisation Sub Rosa, with one sounding like the goody-two-shoes diplomatic type and the other wanting to "exploit the subjects for his own personal gain". Sounds more Saturday morning cartoon than serious RPG story with serious choices, but that's always tended to be how The Outer Worlds leans.

In a recent development, rounding out the expansion are fresh enemies, gear, flaws which give your character build a funky twist, and a bumping up of the level cap from from 30 to 36. Fittingly given I'm writing this on Skyrim's 15th birthday, one of the new flaws is named 'Must Have Been the Wind' after the meme of enemies in the likes of Bethesda and Obsidian's games returning to chill mode after being shot in the face with an arrow or facing some other obvious sign they're under attack. To encourage folks to dive back in, The Outer Worlds 2 is getting options to respec your character's skills and edit how many skill points are dished out per level up via an upgrade alongside Side Effects Guaranteed.

As much as I'm resigned to the series' likely fate as Obsidian return to Fallout and won't pretend The Outer Worlds 2 was great rather than good, I'm still hopeful it can go out with a bang in these two expansions, if indeed this is the studio's last trip to space for the foreseeable future. It's worth noting that if you bought The Outer Worlds 2's premium edition, these expansions are included as part of it and so will come to you at no extra cost.

It has been revealed that with less than a week to go before GTA 6's hugely anticipated release, the game's final map - or at least a stylised poster version of it, depicting the state of Leonida's key landmarks - has surfaced online. It was reportedly snapped during Selfridge's sizable GTA 6's takeover, and is seemingly the physical map included in Rockstar's £350 collector's edition.

Sources indicate that fans have been pondering GTA 6's map for some time now, cross-referencing previous map leaks with official trailer footage in an attempt to gain some insight into the major landmarks and regions Rockstar has in store. And while the newly leaked map is far from granular, it does at least appear to confirm Leonida's rough layout and the key locations players can visit this time.

Assuming the map's veracity, it's all rendered in an art style somewhere between mid-century tourism poster and Adult Swim, featuring the phrase "The Goodtime State" up top - a riff on the actual Florida's nickname, The Sunshine State - while Leonida's most notable points of interest are interspersed with cartoon figures.

There's a toking turtle (or possibly a tortoise - I'm no expert), a golfer proudly wearing assless chaps, a flying saucer, and more. I'll spare you the geographic details confirmed on the map in case you want to go in unspoiled. One point of amusement though: the way the map photo is cropped means fans searching for confirmation of an in-game Key West are still none the wiser.

Sources indicate that it's not entirely clear where the wonkily angled photo originated from, but prominent Rockstar Games community insider Videotech, who shared the image on social media, suggested it came from a "naughty Selfridges employee" during Selfridges' GTA 6 takeover. The map itself appears to be the "double-Sided souvenir poster with map of Leonida" included in Rockstar's eyewateringly expensive GTA 6 Collector's Edition. This costs £350 and doesn't come with a copy of the game. Or assless chaps, for that matter.

In a recent development, this isn't the first time GTA 6's map - officially stated to be twice the size of GTA 5's - has leaked online, although previous leaks have been notably more controversial. Earlier this year, a group calling itself CyberLeek shared unofficial gameplay and map details in the name of what it called "Gamers' Rights". In August, with Netflix's official GTA 6 unveiling looming, the group cashed out nearly £200,000 from its crypto scheme.

Amid all this, Rockstar has been embroiled in legal action after it was accused of union busting following the firing of over 30 employees. The case's conclusion has been delayed until next week, meaning a verdict could arrive just as GTA 6 goes on sale.

Cloud9, ENVY, M80, FlyQuest and LYON were also on that list. Riot now has eight partner teams in each of its four regions.

The Swiss Stage runs from 20 to 22 November 2026. Every match is best of three. Two wins send a team through to the playoffs, and two losses knock it out. The eight teams left after the Swiss phase move into a double-elimination bracket played over six competition days, with the playoffs set for 1 to 6 December. The event is listed as an online, A-Tier Riot Games qualifier for 16 teams.

Industry observers note that shopify Rebellion Black’s next opponents are Oafs, who also won their opening match 2-0, against QoR. Both teams are therefore one win from the playoffs. Oafs already have a record against Xora. They knocked them out of the Qualifier 1 bracket on 8 November with a 2-1 win. Xora had still reached the Qualifier Playoffs by finishing joint third in the 512-team North America Qualifier 1.

Across 83 rated matches, Shopify Rebellion Black hold a 59-24 record. Before this event their most recent series was a 2-3 defeat to 2GAME Esports at the VCL Americas Last Chance Qualifier 2026. Earlier in that event they had beaten 2GAME Esports 2-1 and Contra 2-0.

The organisation’s second line-up had a harder start. Shopify Rebellion Gold lost 0-2 to Maryville University. Several of the other organisations left out of the partnership programme won their first matches. Cloud9 beat counterfeit 2-0, Team Envy beat Yellow Dragon Gaming 2-0 and FlyQuest edged Masterclass 2-1. Elsewhere, Winthrop University beat SaD Esports 2-0 and YFP Gaming beat Wildcard 2-1.

The prize for coming through the bracket is a place in São Paulo. Riot will stage the 2027 VCT Americas Kickoff in Brazil. Its eight Partner Teams get direct entry. Non-partner teams can win four places: one guaranteed slot each for North America, Brazil and Latin America, plus one for the Americas Last Chance Qualifier. For a non-partner side, a later run to Masters would be worth a fixed US$200,000 and a place at Champions US$400,000, Dot Esports reported. The regional Kickoff events are due to start on 14 January 2027 and run until 7 February 2027.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Diablo 4’s segment in the big Diablo 30th Anniversary Spotlight was among the biggest, even if the reason most of us tuned in was somewhat spoiled earlier in the same livestream. Blizzard unveiled the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.

The first class, being the Paladin, is already available to play for anyone who pre-ordered the expansion, but the Warlock won’t be accessible until the expansion arrives in late April.

It has been revealed that the Warlocks are positioned as the opposite of the Paladins, in that they don’t mind utilising forbidden knowledge, drawing on the powers of Hell itself to fight its own overlords. The Warlock is the edgy, antihero counterpart to the Paladin’s purity and devotion to the Light.

Industry observers note that the livestream did not show off any Warlock gameplay, but Blizzard is planning a dedicated livestream to show off the upcoming class’ gameplay, and dig deeper into its lore and abilities. That show is scheduled for March 5.

Industry observers note that what we did get to see was our first look at Skovos, the expansion’s newly introduced region. This Mediterranean-inspired location is where the new story arc will unfold, but it’s also being positioned as the endgame destination for Diablo 4 once the credits roll.

Lord of Hatred, of course, as previously revealed, introduces two newly introduced endgame modes in War Looks, and Echoing Hatred.

War Looks lets you create a custom playlist of up to five endgame activities to target specific rewards and create your own experience. There’s a latest activity tree that works with all endgame activities, and creating War Plans is how you earn progression there.

Echoing Hatred, on the other hand, is a rare event that pits you against legions of Mephisto’s minions. It’s triggered through a rare lootable item that unlocks access. It’s essentially horde mode; where you’ll face unending waves of enemies, though not without a couple of twists.

Recent findings suggest that we also got a bit more colour on the expanded class skill trees, which all players will benefit from when the expansion arrives. The Talisman system, which unlocks set bonuses, was also shown off. And, of course, the return of the iconic Horadric Cube, which gives you control over Affixes.

According to recent reports, the Anniversary Spotlight should’ve had a Year of the Warlock subtitle, because the class is also making its way to both Diablo Immortal, as well as Diablo 2: Resurrected. The showcase revealed the Reign of the Warlock DLC, which adds the aforementioned Warlock to D2R - its first new class in 25 years.

Reign of the Warlock, which is available now in D2R, also makes a few updates to the game, such as new quality of life features, the Colossal Ancients endgame encounter, updated Terror Zones and more. You also get some cosmetics in Diablo 4 if you purchase this expansion.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that XBOX controllers have changed considerably during the company’s 25-year history.
  • However, the most impactful XBOX controller change could be on the horizon, if XBOX goes ahead with a patent filed by Microsoft.
  • According to recent reports, as spotted by Insider Gaming, the patent was first filed in May 2025 and was published in November 2026.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that XBOX controllers have changed considerably during the company’s 25-year history. In fact, XBOX recently released a 25th anniversary console and controller as a throwback to the translucent green days. From the iconic XBOX 360 controller to the sleek peripheral we see today with the XBOX Series X|S versions, each generation has still managed to maintain a familiar feel, despite its evolution.

However, the most impactful XBOX controller change could be on the horizon, if XBOX goes ahead with a patent filed by Microsoft. It appears that Microsoft has an interest in swappable thumbstick modules, allowing players to replace damaged thumbsticks rather than purchasing an entirely new controller to resolve a thumbstick problem.

According to recent reports, as spotted by Insider Gaming, the patent was first filed in May 2025 and was published in November 2026. Thanks to the filing being published publicly, we can get a peek into what XBOX could be planning for the future of its hardware.

The Microsoft patent application relates to a game controller thumbstick that pops in and out through the use of a single screw that is secure enough so that it never falls out of the module.

It has been revealed that information provided by Patentlyze shows that the replaceable input module has three parts. A seating protrusion (a small lip), which hooks into an opening in the controller's side wall, a locating pin on the opposite side neatly slides into a matching hole to line everything up, and fastener that acts as a hole for the screw that pulls the module down into place.

Tightening the screw is done to press the flat bottom of the module against a flat surface inside the controller. According to the patent, this mechanism also pushes angled surfaces on the lip against matching angled surfaces on the controller, to keep the module in place.

Recent findings suggest that if the modules were to be made available to the public, they would have to be easy for everybody to install. The drawings filed show that the process of removing the thumbcap and switching the swappable unit is fairly straightforward. There are no details on whether the replaceable thumbstick will come in different colors for further customization options, or if Microsoft will stick with the default black design.

Sources indicate that the benefit of this is innovation lies in your thumbstick being damaged, worn out, or you’re experiencing stick drift, and you don’t have to purchase an entirely fresh controller or send your controller in to be repaired. Instead, you can simply attach a new thumbstick and continue playing. Depending on its price point, swappable thumbsticks would likely be a welcome option, since most gamers know how expensive it can be to buy a new gamepad.

A seating protrusion (a small lip), which hooks into an opening in the controller's side wall, a locating pin on the opposite side neatly slides into a matching hole to line everything up, and fastener that acts as a hole for the screw that pulls the module down into place.

The patent mainly uses an XBOX game controller as an example, but it mentions keyboards, laptops, and even drone controllers, too.

It’s worth noting that the application was rejected in the examiner's first review, but the reasons are unknown. Usually, this allows the firm to respond or make amendments where needed, so the original filing could be far from the end product.

Recent findings suggest that it’s unknown whether Microsoft will make use of this patent for its hardware until an official announcement has been made. With Project Helix in the works, who knows, perhaps the next generation of XBOX controllers could feature the ability to swap out controller thumbsticks.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that despite all the outrage and criticism around game developers and publishers using generative AI in gaming, a upcoming report from the Game Developers Conference (GDC) calculates that as many as 40 percent of developers active in the industry use the controversial tools in their work.
  • That's according to the latest State of the Game Industry report from GDC, which gathers data from more than 2,300 respondents including, but not limited to, game industry professionals, made up of developers, producers, marketers, executives, and investors.
  • The report notes that 57 percent of developers who say they do use it, use gen-AI for "text generation, research, early prototyping, coding, and presentations".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that despite all the outrage and criticism around game developers and publishers using generative AI in gaming, a upcoming report from the Game Developers Conference (GDC) calculates that as many as 40 percent of developers active in the industry use the controversial tools in their work. This is up four percent compared to the same report last year.

That's according to the latest State of the Game Industry report from GDC, which gathers data from more than 2,300 respondents including, but not limited to, game industry professionals, made up of developers, producers, marketers, executives, and investors.

The report notes that 57 percent of developers who say they do use it, use gen-AI for "text generation, research, early prototyping, coding, and presentations". There appears to be a big split between triple-A studios that use gen-AI (with 27 percent of triple-A developers noting that they "feel encouraged or pressured" to use it) and indie devs, of which only nine percent say the same. Perhaps unsurprisingly - given how vocally against gen-AI a lot of 'frontline developers' have been - the tools are mostly used by "business operations and services, mobile-only studios, and free-to-play developers".

It has been revealed that there seems to be a gap in the ages of those willing to use AI tools as well; per the report, over half (54 percent) of people 45 years or older reported using the tools - an eight-point increase from last year's survey. There is also more usage among men (45 percent) than women (33 percent).

What is perhaps more striking is that more people responded to the survey saying that they think AI is having a negative impact on games (55 percent) than responded saying they use the tech, suggesting a trend of caution rather than widespread adoption. Notably, respondents saying they are wary of the technology increased one percent since last year, so more people think AI is having a negative effect on the industry now than at the same time in 2025. Perhaps that's because of the sweeping layoffs we've seen across the games industry, often mentioned in the same breath as AI. Or the 'AI slop' that's been flooding Steam and pushing more traditional developers out. Orr some of the abysmal projects we've seen launch that have clearly used gen-AI assets.

The use of generative AI remains controversial in the games industry, though with substantial companies like Epic and Microsoft doubling down on the tech, it seems this split between developers that want to embrace it and those that don't is only growing larger.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that loot boxes, dark patterns, virtual currencies, subscription services, pay-to-win systems, and many other trappings of diabolical digital serfdom all face extensive regulation under the European Commission's proposed Digital Fairness Act, which has been formally presented to EU member states today.
  • According to recent reports, you can now read the draft text here on the EU Commission's official site.
  • Sources indicate that here's a summary from me, based on a quick delve through the text.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that loot boxes, dark patterns, virtual currencies, subscription services, pay-to-win systems, and many other trappings of diabolical digital serfdom all face extensive regulation under the European Commission's proposed Digital Fairness Act, which has been formally presented to EU member states today. The full draft text of the regulation leaked earlier in the week. If it passes into law - and there's plenty of debate and revision ahead - it'll have big consequences for the developers and publishers of games like Overwatch, Dota 2, and GTA Online.

According to recent reports, you can now read the draft text here on the EU Commission's official site. The organisers have also published an introductory explainer that takes us through the timeline of the Act's gestation, dating back to 2020, and summarises its provisions. If passed, the Act will apply to any organization doing business in the EU, not just those based in member states, with individual governments able to impose fines and consumers able to seek financial compensation if they think they've been harmed.

Sources indicate that here's a summary from me, based on a quick delve through the text. The Act proposes a number of provisions regarding "unfair" commercial practices, including omission and distortion in advertising and PR communication at large. Amongst other things, it takes aim at "dark patterns" – that is, "visual, auditory and other components" of online interfaces that are designed to manipulate or deceive. The text also forbids personalised advertising and pricing aimed at children, and prohibits influencers from making "direct exhortations to minors to buy products or to persuade their parents or other adults to buy products in commercial communications".

The items that are probably of greatest interest to us smelly gamers are the passages on virtual currencies, "variable reward systems", and addictive design.

According to recent reports, the Act would require game publishers who sell virtual currencies to indicate the real-world monetary value of the currency and anything bought with it. It would also require companies to disable paid-for virtual currencies by default for kids, unless a parent or guardian has given approval.

As for paid-for "variable reward systems", aka "loot boxes", "surprise mechanics", "Schrödinger's Giftbombs" or however publishers may prefer to describe them, the Act would require companies to state the "types" of object they might cough up, together with the probability of obtaining them. It would also oblige publishers to disable paid-for "variable reward systems" for minors, and give everybody an "easily accessible" way to switch them off.

Recent findings suggest that the draft Act outright prohibits "pay-to-progress and pay-to-win mechanisms" for kids. More generally, it suggests further constraints for publishers and developers who "design, organise or operate their digital products in a manner that is intended, or can reasonably be foreseen to encourage compulsive or excessive use". Again, it wants companies to give people options to switch these features off.

Industry observers note that that includes "features enabling automatic play of content and uninterrupted content consumption without effective and regular interruption moments that enable deliberation by the consumer on their willingness to consume more content". Also, "notifications not triggered by, or not directly related to, the consumer’s interaction or activity on the service", "features incentivising engagement at regular times or with greater frequency, including through penalties or loss of benefits", and "features and system behaviours that encourage continued use by simulating interpersonal relations," such as nagging prompts.

According to recent reports, if you'd like a more 'expert' account of the Digital Fairness Act - how dare you! I have read several Wikipedia pages - the bespectacled nabobs of GamesIndustry.biz went and got notes from an actual lawyer. All this follows a change in EU rating law last month aimed at safeguarding the weans from predatory habit-forming devices and instruments of financialisation - games with lootboxes are now PEGI 16 by default, while blockchain games are always rated 18. Across the pond, meanwhile, lawsuits are underway in New York and Washington against Valve's tolerance of lootboxes on Steam, which the lawyers in question define as illegal gambling.

According to recent reports, against Stallions Esports, the semi-final went the full distance. No Org No Problem took the opening map in 48 minutes. Stallions Esports levelled on the second, winning a 54-minute contest. No Org No Problem then closed out the decider in 43 minutes.

Stallions Esports won Middle East Qualifier 2 from 16 to 18 November, ahead of Mayhem. Mix My Miks won North Africa Qualifier 1, a single-elimination event from 9 to 11 November, ahead of BAAM Esports. Each of those qualifiers had 64 teams.

Alongside the MENA winner, Europe sends two qualifiers to Berlin and Türkiye sends one. The partner teams already in the field are BBL Esports, Fnatic, FUT Esports, Gentle Mates, Karmine Corp, Team Heretics, Team Liquid and Team Vitality. Fnatic were confirmed in October 2026 as staying on as a VCT EMEA partner for 2027.

The tournament will be played in person at the Riot Games Arena in Berlin in early 2027. For the MENA winner, the trip carries direct financial value. Riot’s support for non-partner teams starts at Kickoff, and the sums rise for teams that progress further through the season.

Non-partner teams that qualify for Masters receive US$200,000, and those reaching Champions receive US$400,000, Dot Esports reported. Europe’s route to Kickoff runs in parallel. The Europe Kickoff Qualifier Playoffs begin with a Swiss stage from 25 to 29 November, followed by playoffs from 3 to 5 December.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GameStop boss Ryan Cohen (last seen attempting to buy eBay) has called for the return of physical game discs, lamenting the lack of control players have over digital purchases in a chat with Bloomberg held on the eve of Grand Theft Auto 6's release.

Sources indicate that in case you missed it, a media meteor impacted yesterday and blasted our landscape free of life. Grand Theft Auto 6 is here and—despite our Ted Litchfield's noble attempts to get you all thinking about Queen's Domain instead (you should play Queen's Domain)—it's all the world can talk about. It's also only available digitally.

"Unquestionably, the decision to move to all digital has hurt consumers, and it’s also hurt GameStop", noted Cohen, remarking that players ought to be able to do with their purchased games as they will: "When you buy a game, you should be able to sell it, trade it or lend it to a friend". Cohen did not namecheck GTA 6 specifically, but did say that he had been speaking about this issue with all "the obvious" publishers.

GameStop, of course, makes a tidy chunk of change from resales of games traded in at its stores—a segment of its business that becomes impossible to maintain in a world without physical discs for players to bring in and sell. Publishers oppose trade-ins "because removing a used copy eliminates an alternative to buying new", says Cohen, accusing them of "taking away competition" by restricting sales to digital-only channels.

According to recent reports, GTA 6 is a portent of the world to come. Earlier this year, Sony unveiled that PlayStation would drop physical discs starting in January 2028, and has held firm to that course in the face of a vocal player uproar.

Concerns around game ownership have reached the point that politicians are weighing in: last month US lawmaker Richie Torres revealed the Power To The Players Act, that would prompt the US Federal Trade Commission to protect players' access to purchased games, even in the case of online-only games that get unplugged.

"When you pay for a game, you should own it", mentioned Torres. "Consumers must have the right to own, the right to play, and the right to transfer the games they buy. A game that can be taken away the moment a company pulls the plug is not a purchase. It is a rental disguised as a sale".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that stealing cars in GTA 6 is one of the easiest ways to attract attention from the police, thanks to the latest Wanted system. You've probably noticed by now that breaking into vehicles is noisy and messy, with Jason and Lucia needing to smash the window to get inside. It also takes time – precious time in which some nosey onlooker can report your description and activity to the cops. There has to be an easier way, right? There is. Which is why you need to learn how to get a Slim Jim in GTA 6.

Recent findings suggest that the Slim Jim in GTA 6 is only available from Chapter 2 onwards. This essential carjacking tool will unlock as part of the main GTA 6 mission list, coming into your possession after you begin a quest called 'Moses'. It's in this mission where you'll meet your first vehicle fence, learn how to sell cars and bikes in GTA 6, and be given the information you need to better survey vehicles for security features with the WAiNK app – which can be activated at any time by holding Up on the D-pad.

Moses will give you the Slim Jim as a part of this mission. It'll let you get into any vehicle without needing to smash the window. You will, however, still need to contend with security features – you'll have to wait until Chapter 3 to learn how to get the Key Cloner in GTA 6 and understand how to deactivate trackers to steal more modern vehicles.

Recent findings suggest that once you've got it, using the Slim Jim is GTA 6 is easy enough. Walk up to any vehicle you want to try and steal. Walk up to the driver-side or passenger door, and press Triangle/Y to bring out your Slim Jim. From there, it's a case of rotating the right thumbstick in a curve until you find the sweet spot – which you'll spot by rumble in the controller and by a slightly pink hue to the semi-circle indicator. Eventually you'll hear a little pop, meaning you can now climb inside.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Crimson Desert and DokeV developer Pearl Abyss is planning to further integrate generative AI into its workflow.

The South Korean studio said as much in its latest quarterly Earnings Letter, explaining that it had previously "validated game systems only after implementing them manually." Now, Pearl Abyss is using AI "to rapidly validate diverse design concepts prior to actual implementation," and argues the move "enables a more efficient allocation of development resources and enhances overall production speed.".

"However, AI serves strictly as a tool to support concept validation and pipeline productivity, while the core gameplay experience and actual content creation remain fully driven by our development team," the developer said.

When Crimson Desert first launched, players spotted a crop of suspicious in-game images that looked like they were prompted into existence. Pearl Abyss soon explained that some "2D visual props" were generated with AI tools, but were always intended to be replaced with human-made art, before rapidly patching them out of the hit open-world game.

Industry observers note that it seems Pearl Abyss is now even more keen on the controversial tech, however: "We are integrating AI technologies to enhance development productivity and overall quality. AI is being utilized across various stages of development - including the automation of repetitive tasks, content creation support, and test optimization - and we are expanding its implementation throughout our entire development pipeline. We view AI not as a substitute for human developers, but as a tool to elevate development efficiency and quality. We will continue to expand our application of AI to deliver higher-fidelity games to the market more expeditiously.".

According to recent reports, elsewhere in the letter, the studio mentioned its previously announced creature-collector DokeV is "targeting a launch in the second half of 2028" and we should hear more about it within the year. DokeV was initially targeting a 2023 launch a few years ago. Meanwhile, Crimson Desert is being prepped for a Nintendo Switch 2 launch "in the first half of next year.".

In a recent development, the use of generative AI in game development has been a hot topic for years, though it's only become more prevalent in recent months as 'AI slop' floods Steam and massive companies like Epic Games proudly adopt the tech. A recent report even estimated that around 40 percent of active developers use AI tools in their work.

8 Best Games Like Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Last year’s Call of Duty was one to forget, but that futuristic fever dream has been completely eclipsed by Infinity Ward’s Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4.
  • Boasting arguably the best campaign since the original Modern Warfare 1-2 punch, this is one we will be telling the next generations to play if they want a taste of what Call of Duty is like at its best.
  • If you’re like me and have been left wanting more after wolfing down the sixteen missions in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, here are games that match the vibes and mechanics of this great comeback story.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Last year’s Call of Duty was one to forget, but that futuristic fever dream has been completely eclipsed by Infinity Ward’s Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4.

Boasting arguably the best campaign since the original Modern Warfare 1-2 punch, this is one we will be telling the next generations to play if they want a taste of what Call of Duty is like at its best.

If you’re like me and have been left wanting more after wolfing down the sixteen missions in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, here are games that match the vibes and mechanics of this great comeback story.

It’s a tragedy that the 2015 remake of Star Wars: Battlefront has been relegated to the flop corner of your local second-hand games store, because to this day, nothing else quite captures the Old Trilogy as well.

If you like Modern Warfare 4 missions like Entrenched, then this one is for you. While Battlefront 2 (2017) became great after the rollback of its controversial monetization model, its predecessor is an easy contestant for the best Star Wars shooter ever.

Like Park and the ROK Marines he serves with, Battlefront made you feel like a lonely grunt fighting a war much bigger than you. There are no supersoldiers to turn the tide, only unrestricted violence and blasters scarring the air. Its biggest sin is that it had no real single-player campaign.

If you enjoyed the vibes of the Counter Attack mission, cowering behind Lt. West’s ACV as you get raked by fire from a building, you might want to check out Squad. Full disclaimer: the pacing and gunplay could not be more different from any Call of Duty game, even its slower early titles, but few games capture the plight of mechanized infantry quite like Squad.

According to recent reports, because of its enormous maps, Squad is meant to be played by riding vehicles to the hot zone. When everything works out fine, you have a quiet dismount in a remote area, set up a defensive perimeter, and nothing happens.

Recent findings suggest that however, the enemy typically has opinions about you capturing objectives. That tends to result in the squad leader shouting for everybody to get out, machine guns raking the side of the vehicle, and the medic desperately trying to work while smoke grenades cloud the area.

There’s an indescribable level of chaos that comes from a hot insertion, and Squad is the place to be if you want to experience it for longer than the ten minutes that sequence takes.

The North Koreans have taken over, Burger Town has fallen, and there’s no Ramírez to save the day. Homefront: The Revolution was much maligned on release, but it scratches a specific kind of itch for an open-world, resistance-themed shooter.

Outside of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, few games let you experience a full-scale fictional North Korean invasion, and though Homefront takes plenty of creative liberties compared to Infinity Ward’s (mostly) grounded approach, it’s a unique set of circumstances.

Alternatively, if you don’t mind some extra jank, the original Homefront is a pretty decent game in and of itself. The production value alone makes it worth a try, so long as you understand this is now a 15-year-old game.

For what feels like the first time in a long while, a Call of Duty game decided to stick with a strong art direction and identity throughout, and DMZ is arguably the best showcase of it.

This year’s extraction mode is a lot more grounded and entertaining than previous iterations, but if the skill-based matchmaking is too much to stomach, Insurgency: Sandstorm blends that fast-paced action with some of the best gunplay on the market, sans the sweatiness.

Insurgency: Sandstorm is all about close combat, with enough tactical Barbie to give you a visual identity but without ever going down the infamous Nicki Minaj route that has plagued Activision’s mainline shooter for years.

A lot of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4’s campaign is spent behind enemy lines in North Korea, and while many of the stealth and infiltration sections are fairly competent for a run-and-gun first-person shooter, they still can’t compete with the real deal.

Since we have no release date for the next Splinter Cell game, there’s no better time to revisit Sam Fisher’s finest hour as the world inched closer to nuclear armageddon once more.

Released in 2005, Chaos Theory sends Fisher snooping in South America and the Korean peninsula, with a little less-than-relaxing stop at Tokyo in the process. It’s everything John Price does in Modern Warfare 4, but better. Sorry, Captain.

According to recent reports, the gunplay in Modern Warfare 4 is hardly its strong point, but it fits the chaotic combat quite nicely. Albeit the twitchy run-and-gun was introduced in the AAA sphere by the original Modern Warfare way back in 2007, it came of age in 2011 with Battlefield 3.

In a recent development, set in a (then) hypothetical conflict between the United States and Iran, Battlefield 3 nails the vibes of Private Park’s side of the campaign. You primarily play Staff Sergeant Henry Blackburn, a Recon Marine who ends up embroiled in a mess well beyond his pay grade.

Blackburn is hardly an idealist, but it doesn’t take a genius to realize that sometimes you need to do bad things to prevent much worse things from happening.

If you prefer Price’s side of the campaign, then I’d recommend Battlefield 4 instead, with a lot less grunt business but plenty of operating in the shadows.

According to recent reports, the tenth level of Modern Warfare 4, Stranded, is one of the best showcases of how good Call of Duty can be when you take off the training wheels. Private Park and his team survive a crash deep into North Korean territory during a secretive mission, and have to live off the land to complete their objectives, then fight their way out.

Both mechanically and story-wise, Stranded is an encapsulated version of Tom Clancy’s Ghost Recon: Breakpoint, the latest instalment in the series.

Sources indicate that breakpoint is set in a near-future where an annoying tech bro built an island where technology has no safeguards, and the results are predictable. As one of the sole survivors, Nomad has to scour Auroa for weapons, equipment, and allies to help defeat its militarized owners.

If you like a good friends-to-enemies plot like Price and Ghost, Breakpoint also puts you against a former ally from Ghost Recon Wildlands.

I’ve always been a staunch defender of 2013’s Medal of Honor: Warfighter, and to this day it remains one of the most underrated shooters of its time. It is also the game with the clearest influence on Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, in both story beats and mechanics.

The foot chases, driving sequences, the ally’s execution by the main baddie, the slow-mo breaches, even the last time you pull the trigger in the campaign, all come straight from Warfighter. The campaign also features a fairly similar split, where one side of the story is told through a discharged special forces veteran operating in the shadows, and another from the front lines.

There are times when Medal of Honor: Warfighter goes a little too corny in its hunt for being respectable, like the Taco Bell cashier who notes ‘thank you for your service’ to the kid straight out of boot camp, but the meat of the game is one of the best depictions of how real special ops play out in the modern world.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, black Forest Games, developers of the Destroy All Humans! remakes, have spun out of Embracer Group-owned publishers THQ Nordic via a management buyout and announced plans to form a latest "developer-driven group" of independent studios. The new group, dubbed Third Signal, will aim to "give teams the independence, resources and creative freedom" to "bring their own ideas to life".

Black Forest, based in Germany, confirmed the move in a press release. "We are grateful to THQ Nordic and Embracer for nine good years and the games we made together," co-boss Adrian Goersch said. "Now, we're excited to shape our own future as owners again, to work on an exciting newly introduced project with a great team and strong partners behind us.".

Industry observers note that "Some of the best games of the last decade came from teams of fifty, not five hundred," added Third Signal founder Andreas Tobler. "Black Forest Games is one of them, and the right studio to launch Third Signal. Our vision is to build a developer driven group and give teams the independence, resources and creative freedom to continue their creative legacy and bring their own ideas to life." As of writing, Third Signal's website is just a logo splash which promises something coming soon. To be fair, it does also look to have an email address, plus legal and privacy notices. Black Forest's management team will become a co-owner of the studio group as part of this move, but "continue to collaborate on game development tasks" with THQ Nordic.

Industry observers note that black Forest had been in the embrace since 2017, releasing both 2020's Destroy All Humans! remake and Destroy All Humans! 2: Reprobed in that time, plus DLC Clone Carnage. Over the years they've also made multiple entries in the Giana Sisters platformer series, survival game Fade to Silence, and 2017's Bubsy: The Woolies Strike Back.

That's a right old mix of stuff, but the biggest names in it are all resurrections of series or characters created by other folks back in the day. Pandemic Studios in the case of Destroy All Humans!, Accolade in the case of Bubsy, and Germany organization Time Warp in the case of Giana Sisters. That makes the fact it sounds like this move'll give Black Forest a bit more creative freedom intriguing. Here's hoping that if they do plan to try and get some more of their own original ideas off the ground, rather than trucking on with a steady diet of remakes and revivals, they manage to stick the landing. It's all fine declaring that a 50 person team can make a top game these days, but that certainly doesn't mean it's in any way easy to pull off.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that nioh 3 has received a hot fresh revision that brings plenty of bug fixes to very specific concerns, but it also implements fixes for a few of the most common - and incredibly annoying - bugs. Patch 1.03.01 arrived earlier on all platforms, and it comes with a chunky set of notes.

This latest enhancement, predictably, doesn’t add any gameplay features, but some of the included fixes will absolutely delight - or vindicate - so many of the game’s millions of players.

There’s plenty to go through in the patch notes published today for update 1.03.01, but the most impactful is a fix for an problem that “sometimes made it impossible to use elixirs during battle.” This is only a partial fix, but if you ran into the problem of smashing that shortcut button and not seeing your character play the healing animation, you’ll be glad to see it.

Industry observers note that this is a problem myself and others have faced, especially in boss fights. You can even see the shortcut register your button press and proceed to ignore you. Another partial fix has been made to an problem that caused the game to crash. Team Ninja didn’t share specifics on that, and though Nioh 3 has been fairly stable for me in 70+ hours, it has definitely crashed a few times.

If you’ve been playing since launch, you likely have - or know someone who has - run into issues with save file corruption and other weird bugs around certain trackable items within save files.

Team Ninja already rolled out a couple of fixes there, and this latest one specifically targets losing valuables during Myths. If your save file has been affected, the game will now check and recover what was lost. Even more interesting is that the game will now automatically create a backup copy of your save data any time you load a save.

If you’ve made it into the Eternal Rift, you’ll be happy to know that today’s update takes care of a few progression blockers, and fixes an problem that allowed some players to obtain certain items before they were supposed to, locking themselves out.

One of the more amusing fixes concerns Mujina, who had a tendency to respawn if you prayed at a Shrine after opening a chest it was hiding in, which made it appear far more often than a mimic should.

Sources indicate that finally, there’s a set of fixes that address bugs (and exploits) when using specific Martial Art with certain weapons. There are a few fixes to AI, Myths, and one problem with the Minamoto no Yoritomo boss fight that made it impossible to interrupt him, even after he runs out of Ki.

Hit the link at the top for the full change log, and check out our Nioh 3 gameplay tips if you haven’t already. You should also change these settings ASAP, as they’re going to make your life much easier and save you a lot of time.

#63479. Breaking: There were 47 graphics chip makers in 1998. Where did they all go?
