Breaking: There were 47 graphics chip makers in 1998. Where did they all go?

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1908 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that some may find this hard to believe, given the absolute state of the market today, but if you were building a gaming PC in 1998, the hard part wasn’t finding somewhere that had 3D cards in stock for a reasonable price.
  • In 1998, 47 companies were designing or selling PC graphics, driving a market that hit 130 million units and outsold PCs themselves.
  • It has been revealed that but the Nvidia of the late 1990s and early 2000s was a far cry from the vast (if tarnished) juggernaut it is today, and at the time it wasn’t even the obvious survivor.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that some may find this hard to believe, given the absolute state of the market today, but if you were building a gaming PC in 1998, the hard part wasn’t finding somewhere that had 3D cards in stock for a reasonable price. It was choosing the right one among a glut of potential, reasonably affordable options.

In 1998, 47 companies were designing or selling PC graphics, driving a market that hit 130 million units and outsold PCs themselves. Just two years later, at the turn of the upcoming millennium, only 15 remained, and not long after that, there were merely two: Nvidia and ATI, nowadays part of AMD.

It has been revealed that but the Nvidia of the late 1990s and early 2000s was a far cry from the vast (if tarnished) juggernaut it is today, and at the time it wasn’t even the obvious survivor. Research firm 4th Wave put ATI top for 1998 with 24.5 million 3D chips sold, followed by S3 with 15.2 million and Intel, in its first year in the market, with 6.5 million. Nvidia came fourth on 6.4 million. 3dfx, the firm whose Voodoo cards had made 3D gaming on PC a thing in the first place, sold 5.2 million.

Each of those companies went under or sold up for one reason or another, but what’s striking is how most did so within a few years of one another. In the four years between 1998 and 2002, the graphics business essentially stopped rewarding whoever had the fastest chip, instead favouring the companies that could iterate the fastest. A fresh chip every six months or so for the same APIs everyone used, backed by enough capital to ride out the dot-com crash. Nvidia was built for that; almost nobody else was.

In a recent development, the first companies to go didn’t need any help from Nvidia, though. 3D acceleration had made the humble graphics chip a much bigger and more expensive thing to design, and plenty of incumbents that had found their footing on 2D couldn’t afford to keep going. Tseng Labs stopped developing graphics chips at the end of 1997 with roughly $28 million still in the bank, selling its graphics engineers to ATI for about $3 million. Rendition, maker of the Vérité V1000 3D accelerator, agreed to sell itself to memory maker Micron in June 1998, and ATI bought Chromatic Research for $67 million that October.

Sources indicate that in its prospectus for its January 1999 IPO, Nvidia warned that PC makers brought out newly introduced systems as often as twice a year, on a spring and fall schedule, and that missing one was a serious risk. The company subsequently reorganised itself around that schedule, releasing the GeForce 256 in October 1999 and the GeForce 3 in February 2001. By 2002, Nvidia’s annual report disclosed that separate design teams were working on several generations of chips at once.

By this point, though, the writing had been on the wall for quite some time. S3, then the world’s second-largest graphics chip maker, wrote in its annual report for 1999 that a graphics chip stayed on sale for 12 to 18 months, and that a delay "as short as a few months" could cost it a design win with a PC maker. Any firm that was rolling out just one major chip per year was launching against a rival’s refresh at best. At worst, it was launching late against next-gen chips.

That’s essentially what happened to 3dfx when Rampage, the chip that was meant to succeed the Voodoo5, never shipped. The company lost its other massive advantage around the same time with Glide, its own programming interface that only ran on Voodoo cards. Glide flourished while Direct3D, Microsoft’s rival interface built into Windows, was still lacking features, meaning that plenty of games ran best on 3dfx hardware, but that lead was quickly eroded once Direct3D and rivals’ OpenGL drivers caught up; developers could now write a game once and run it on anyone’s card. By 1999, Creative was selling Nvidia-based Riva TNT cards with drivers that let Glide games run on them. 3dfx sued, then open-sourced Glide altogether that December.

According to recent reports, by then, though, 3dfx had already made its most damaging mistake. A year earlier, on December 14, 1998, it agreed to buy graphics card maker STB Systems for about $141 million in stock, and CEO Greg Ballard noted the Voodoo3 would only be sold on 3dfx’s cards. That revelation left Diamond and Creative in a tough spot, having built their gaming lines on Voodoo chips. They were now stuck high and dry without access to the newly introduced one.

According to recent reports, 3dfx was solely concerned with its margins here. The price of its single-chip Voodoo Banshee card dropped from $150 to $89 within a month of launch. With prices in freefall, selling the finished Voodoo Banshee meant that 3dfx pocketed the margin that’d otherwise go to a partner like Diamond or Creative. Those boardmakers inevitably walked, and went where the chips were. STB had been selling Nvidia cards right up to the deal, and its last annual report includes a $3 million note it held from "Nvidia Corporation, a supplier." Creative already had Riva TNT cards on shelves, and Nvidia, which then didn’t make its own cards, would sell its chips to anyone.

Intel, meanwhile, was causing problems from the other end of the market. Its i740 "Auburn" graphics chip debuted in early 1998, and Microprocessor Report, the newsletter for the industry’s engineers, argued that Intel’s arrival encouraged Cirrus Logic, Oak and others to fold that year. Just over a year later, after lacklustre sales, Intel confirmed that it was ending support for the i740, then pulled out of standalone desktop graphics chips altogether to put graphics into its motherboard chipsets instead, starting with the i810. This was extremely problematic for companies like S3, Trident, and SiS. They survived on cheap chips for big PC makers, and by the second half of 2001, estimates say Intel’s integrated graphics business had risen to control 55% of the market. That, in turn, pushed S3 to sell its graphics business to a VIA joint venture for $323 million.

Industry observers note that then the money ran out. Venture funding for graphics startups had already dried up in 1999 as the dot-com bubble deflated, and exits inevitably followed. 3dfx lost $100.5 million in the second quarter of 2000, with its CEO blaming a late Voodoo5, and on December 15 that year it sold its assets to Nvidia for $70 million in cash (and a million Nvidia shares) after failing to secure credit. STMicroelectronics, which made the PowerVR-based Kyro II, quit PC graphics in early 2002.

Industry observers note that ATI, however, survived alongside Nvidia because it was already operating in the way the new market wanted it to. It was the biggest seller at the time, and it made its own graphics cards, which Microprocessor Report said brought in most of its revenue and margin. So, making its own cards wasn’t 3dfx’s mistake; it was locking out boardmakers who had been selling Voodoo cards for it. That pushed those boardmakers towards Nvidia, and a late Voodoo5 and cash crunch dealt the death blow. ATI also used its stock to buy the engineers that its rivals were shedding: Tseng’s, Chromatic’s, then, in February 2000, ArtX’s for $400 million, a team that’d just designed the Flipper graphics chip for Nintendo’s GameCube.

For the next two decades, the the graphics industry was dominated by ATI - which eventually folded into AMD in 2006 - and Nvidia. For a while, it was a real fight. AMD paid $5.4 billion for ATI, and in the second quarter of 2010, Radeon cards briefly overtook Nvidia in discrete graphics shipments. However, AMD had a problem: it couldn’t really afford ATI. It wrote off $1.6 billion of goodwill from the deal about a year after it closed, and its PC chip business kept struggling.

In a recent development, by early 2015, AMD’s CPU and GPU revenue was down 38% on the year, and the company was close to negative book value. Its quarterly R&D budget had fallen to its lowest level since 2004, with Nvidia spending nearly half as much again. Radeon cards stayed on the same Graphics Core Next architecture for about seven years before RDNA arrived in 2019. By then, Nvidia had already launched its RTX cards with dedicated ray tracing hardware and Tensor cores for AI, and it never gave that lead back.

Intel was the only tech giant with pockets deep enough to try breaking back in. Its first go, Larrabee, was cancelled as a consumer graphics chip in December 2009. It finally got there in 2022, when the Arc A770 went on sale from $329, alongside the cheaper A750. Both arrived after repeated delays and struggled with older DirectX 9 games, and many observers - RPS included - put their chances of breaking up the Nvidia-AMD duopoly at low. By the time then-hardware editor James returned to the A750 in 2023, Intel had drastically improved its drivers, bringing big gains to both general performance and DX9 compatibility. Even then, the Arc series had yet to prove it could work well at launch, without the need to be ironed out across months of updates.

The second generation did indeed fare better, with the Arc B580 successfully selling out at $249 in December 2024. But that still barely impacted the wider industry, with Intel sitting at just 1% of graphics card shipments in the third quarter of 2025 and around 2% this spring, when Nvidia took roughly 90% of the 12.5 million cards shipped.

According to recent reports, it now looks like Intel is on its way back out of gaming graphics cards. In April, leaker Jaykihn claimed that its next-generation Celestial gaming cards had been cancelled "long ago," and the latest rumours say B580 supply could be cut so Intel can sell more Arc Pro cards for, surprise surprise, AI work. It’s vital to note that Intel hasn’t confirmed any of that, and one of its execs has said that Arc isn’t leaving its PC roadmap. Still, Intel had everything 3dfx didn’t: the cash, the PC makers on side, and the same APIs as everyone else. But money can’t buy two decades of Nvidia and AMD fixing their drivers game by game, and it seems to have decided its capital is better spent on AI anyway.

Evidently, the question of where all the other GPU makers went does not have one single answer. Some couldn’t afford the rising costs, some couldn’t keep pace with a latest Nvidia chip every six months, and some lost their cheap business to Intel’s integrated graphics or went under when the dot-com bubble burst. Left over was a Nvidia/ATI (later AMD) duopoly, and PC gamers haven’t exactly done well out of it. We saw the RTX 4080 launch at $1,199 in 2022, nearly twice the 3080’s price, and the ongoing, AI-driven RAM shortage has pushed prices higher still.

In 1998, 47 companies wanted your money. Now there are two, and the bigger one, Nvidia, sells nine of every 10 graphics cards - yet still makes most of its money from data centres. Eighteen years on, it's a bad time to be a PC gamer, and nobody’s in a hurry to make things any better.

This one is a bit of a nostalgia play, taking everyone back to Mondstadt, the place where you may remember taking your first steps. And, as with any good return to the ol’ hunting grounds, come familiar characters, too.

In a recent development, the substantial fresh arrival is Varka, who joins as a playable character for the first time. Varka, Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius, is a character whose debut has been long-awaited. He is a 5-Star Anemo Claymore wielder with a dual-wield combat style, capable of dealing two different types of Elemental damage. His addition means that there's now finally a burly 5-Star male character of each elemental type... do with that information what you will.

Recent findings suggest that varka's dual-wielding combat style allows him to deal two different types of Elemental damage at the same time. The way it works is that his Elemental Skill boosts the damage of his regular attacks, but it also converts the damage type of his right-hand claymore to match his teammates’ elements (Pyro, Hydro, Electro, or Cryo). The left-hand claymore always deals Anemo damage.

According to recent reports, the more normal attacks you use, the more frequently he can activate a special Elemental Skill, or trigger a Charged Attack that doesn’t consume stamina. He can also rely on the Hexerei effect to trigger more instances of Elemental Skill, as well as Charged Attacks, making him a monster damage-dealer.

Sources indicate that varka, of course, has been a staple member of the cast, featuring in both the original story in a small cameo, as well as taking a bigger role in the recent Nod-Krai chapters. With the return to Mondstadt, his playable debut makes sense. His Story Quest will shed light on his encounter with the Wild Hunt, and the Great Wolf King of the North.

In a recent development, the reruns for this version are going to be Flins — who will be available in the first phase of Event Wishes — as well as Skirk and Escoffier in the second phase. You can also look forward to the return of the Chronicled Wish with Mondstadt characters.

According to recent reports, staying on the theme of reminiscence, the major event in Luna 5 is centered around revisiting memories from the beginning of your time with Genshin Impact, and reuniting with old friends. In Echoes of Memory, you’ll witness familiar scenes that have been changed slightly, and you’ll need to use the Spotter Kamera to detect and record those differences.

The Knights of Favonius are hosting several other activities for everyone to take part in, including an event that lets you catch up with old friends over drinks which you make for them.

Recent findings suggest that outside of events, there’s a fresh set of Gliding and Combat Challenges. And, of course, there are new minigames that you can relax with. The Kamera is being utilised yet again, and this time you can use to capture sights from your time in spots across Natlan, Fontaine, and Sumeru. There’s also… a horde mode of a sort, where you fend off waves of enemies.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Legend of Zelda was in "dire straits" before Breath of the Wild gave the beloved series a massive second wind, according to two former Nintendo marketing leads.
  • The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time's most recent remake has been a mega success, becoming the fastest-selling Switch 2 game so far, but the shiny new adventure has also prompted some online debate over where the series should go next.
  • Nintendo of America's ex-director of social media marketing Kit Ellis and former public relations manager Krysta Yang chimed in on the discourse in their latest podcast (below), and explained that Zelda wasn't doing too hot before the Switch era.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Legend of Zelda was in "dire straits" before Breath of the Wild gave the beloved series a massive second wind, according to two former Nintendo marketing leads.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time's most recent remake has been a mega success, becoming the fastest-selling Switch 2 game so far, but the shiny new adventure has also prompted some online debate over where the series should go next. Should Zelda lean into its carefully directed history - like the one brilliantly remade in Ocarina of Time - or keep the ball rolling with Breath of the Wild's wide open, spontaneous sandbox?

Nintendo of America's ex-director of social media marketing Kit Ellis and former public relations manager Krysta Yang chimed in on the discourse in their latest podcast (below), and explained that Zelda wasn't doing too hot before the Switch era.

"There has been some revisionist history out there lately," Ellis said in response to fans who reckon "the Zelda team ripped away" series staples, like classic dungeons and linear worlds, at the height of their popularity.

"I remember, I was going to the focus groups where it was a really dark moment," Ellis continued. "The feedback was like, 'The fan base is dwindling. This is not bringing in latest players.'".

Sources indicate that the Legend of Zelda was supposedly "shrinking," while "interest in the audience was getting smaller and smaller" with each newly introduced entry. "They had to do something dramatic," Ellis stated.

Sources indicate that "This series was in dire straits. They were selling, like, nothing," Yang added.

The Zelda series was certainly never irrelevant, but there's a pretty big gap between the roughly 8m copies Twilight Princess sold at the beginning of the Wii generation, the roughly 3m copies Skyward Sword sold at the end of the console's life, and the 34m copies that Breath of the Wild sold just one console generation later.

It was a success so significant it spawned a wildly ambitious sequel, Tears of the Kingdom, and even influenced the latest 2D Zelda, Echoes of Wisdom. Now that classic Zelda's back in the spotlight, though, I do hope Nintendo's able to slot the series' curated dungeons into whatever the next mainline game becomes.

GTA 6: How to Rob ATM Machines

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (564 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that one of GTA 6's main objectives is to make as much money as possible.
  • However, there’s another way to get a good sum of cash that most players may not know about, and that’s robbing ATM machines.
  • It has been revealed that if you are looking for an additional way to earn money in the game, this guide has you covered.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that one of GTA 6's main objectives is to make as much money as possible. There are many ways to do this, such as stealing and selling cars, robbing stores, completing missions, etc.

However, there’s another way to get a good sum of cash that most players may not know about, and that’s robbing ATM machines.

It has been revealed that if you are looking for an additional way to earn money in the game, this guide has you covered. Here’s how to rob ATM machines in GTA VI.

According to recent reports, before you can rob an ATM machine in Grand Theft Auto 6, you must steal it first. To do this, you need two things: a vehicle with a flatbed and the Winch mod attached to it.

Trucks with flatbeds are generally easy to find and acquire by simply stealing one, while the Winch can be added to the vehicle by bringing it to a Mod Shop.

Keep in mind that Mod Shops each specialize in certain services, so not all of them will have a Winch available.

If you are having trouble finding a Mod Shop that works, make sure to read the shop’s description in the map menu. The description will explain if it specializes in your vehicle.

After attaching a Winch, all you have to do is back it up into the ATM machine to automatically latch it to your vehicle. Next, drive away with the machine attached to rip it out of the building.

Industry observers note that with the ATM machine ripped out of the building and attached to your truck, it’s time to get it open so you can claim the money. There are two ways to do this.

First, you can use Sticky Bombs to blow it up, which is the faster way. You can purchase Sticky Bombs from most Ammu-Nation shops across Leonida and they don’t cost much, only costing around 185 dollars.

Sources indicate that the other way to open an ATM machine is to continue driving with it attached to the Winch of your vehicle until it breaks and busts open. However, this method isn’t recommended since you need to do a lot of damage to it to open it.

Either way you decide, you will know when an ATM breaks open when dollar signs and blocks of money appear.

Sources indicate that simply put, not all ATM machines hold the same amount of money in GTA VI. From personal experience, each ATM has, on average, rewarded me with 4k to 6k. There have been some that rewarded me with more than that, though, so it really just depends.

In a recent development, once you claim the cash from the ATM machine, there’s a good chance the money will spray pink paint on Lucia and James. Whether it does or not depends on how far you are in the story.

This is because all money from banks and ATM machines contain Marked Bills, and the paint helps cops track down the thieves who committed the robbery.

In order to deal with the paint and officially steal Marked Bills, you need to complete the mission “Credit Check” during Chapter 3 of the main story. Completing this mission will reward you with a Dye Pack Jammer that makes it possible to claim and spend Marked Bills.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ubisoft has confirmed that it is laying off a total of 166 members of staff from its Canadian offices.

Recent findings suggest that the teams affected, Ubisoft Montréal and Ubisoft Québec, are arguably two of the most prominent studios in the corporation. The former has been responsible for some of the most well-regarded entries in the Assassin's Creed series along with key entries in the Far Cry franchise.

The latter, meanwhile, worked on the excellent Assassin's Creed Shadows and also developed the underrated Switch gem Immortals Fenyx Rising.

GamesIndustry.biz states that the layoffs account for less than 4% of the total workforce at the studios, and that the employees affected were working on projects that had either been cancelled or significantly changed.

Here's the statement provided by Ubisoft:.

"Ubisoft is reducing its workforce by 166 positions across its Montréal and Québec City operations. As our portfolio evolves, our production needs are changing, requiring us to adjust the size of some teams to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs.

"We deeply value the contributions of these teams and recognise the impact this may have on our colleagues. We are committed to supporting them through this process with care and respect. Those affected are being provided with severance, extended health care benefits, career transition services and other resources.".

Ubisoft's next major release is Rayman Legends Retold, a reimagined remake of the 2013 classic Rayman Legends, developed in collaboration by Ubisoft Milan and Montpellier.

It has been revealed that even before the game came out, it was pretty easy to guess that Nioh 3 would be a hit. From the word of mouth leading up to launch, to the well-received free demo, there was little chance the action RPG wasn’t going to be a major deal.

Recent findings suggest that today, publisher Koei Tecmo has unveiled that the game has officially passed over one million copies sold worldwide across PC, and PlayStation 5. This makes it the fastest in the Nioh franchise to reach this milestone.

As a result of this fantastic launch, Nioh 3 has now pushed overall Nioh franchise sales to be over 10 million, which includes the original Nioh as well as Nioh 2. Today’s news comes just two weeks after the game arrived on PC, and PS5.

On Steam, where it’s available on PC, it shot up the Steam charts, and immediately broke the series’ previous best peak concurrent player count record. From there, the numbers kept growing, leading up to a stellar weekend where it peaked at 88,045 concurrent players on Steam, double that of its launch day.

This now stands as the largest for any Nioh game on Steam, and though we don’t have insight into how well it’s doing on PS5 specifically, it still highlights that the Nioh series continues to grow.

Nioh 3 builds on everything the two prior games established, and pushes the series into the semi-open-world realm, with several larger maps that each cover a period of time in Japan’s history. In our Nioh 3 review we called it “Team Ninja’s most accomplished action game, and the series’ most accessible.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that one half of GTA 6's leading couple, Jason Duval, is unusually reserved and soft-spoken when compared to many of the crime series' boisterous, sometimes gleefully violent protagonists. Why the change? Rockstar Games' narrative lead says the idea came from 1972's The Getaway and Jason's military background.

"When we decided we wanted to tell a story about a couple on the run, we looked at all the similar kinds of movies, and one of the ones that really stood out was [Sam] Peckinpah's The Getaway," senior vice president of narrative, Rupert Humphries, indicates in a statement given to Destructoid.

The crime flick's star Steve McQueen "was famous for pulling lines out of scripts and saying things with his presence alone," Humphries continues, and that's an energy the team at Rockstar wanted to somewhat match with Jason's characterisation. Although, he also acknowledges that "so many of our protagonists have been the opposite." Think Trevor and the like.

Industry observers note that "This also resonated with the research we were doing around veterans and particularly former Army Rangers (in our world we call them Marauders). These guys typically aren't running their mouths or reacting to something unless it's strictly necessary, while still being strong and still asserting themselves," Humphries adds.

Sources indicate that the game itself definitely plays on those ideas, too. (Something noted in our GTA 6 review.) Jason isn't the most forthcoming or chatty protagonist, but what he leaves unsaid and when he chooses to communicate is just as important as what he actually shares with Lucia - the other, more chaotic half of the game's central couple, who balances things out somewhat.

According to recent reports, "Researching the prolific and headline-grabbing criminal activity that had been taking place over decades in Florida was an obvious starting point," game writer Michael Wiafe also said of the game's sweeping story. "From then on, it was about coming up with authentic characters that didn't stray too far from reality but also were not totally bound by it either. The majority of our main characters are undeniably reprehensible on paper, full-blown criminals, but also decent human beings. Their moral makeup isn't necessarily cut-and-dry, and we don't attempt to make excuses for them. What's important is how they resonate, no matter where you're experiencing the game in the world.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, yesterday, a rumor emerged on X claiming that Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra, the upcoming World War II-era superhero game led by Uncharted creator Amy Hennig, was being cancelled. After making the rounds on social media, newly introduced reports claim this is not the case, at least for now.

The rumor stemmed from a now-deleted X post from a fan account called Marvel 1943 Rise Of Hydra Countdown claiming, through supposed inside sources, that Skydance was preparing to announce the game’s cancellation. This rumor was swiftly picked up and circulated by online gaming circles, gaining steam due to growing uncertainty around the game’s status.

In a recent development, marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra was revealed in 2022 and stars Captain America and Black Panther (Azurri, T'Challa's grandfather), alongside Howling Commandos member Gabriel Jones and Wakandan Spy Network leader Nanali, as they battle Hydra during World War II. Developed by Skydance New Media, led by Amy Hennig, it’s been repeatedly delayed, and only cinematic footage has been released. This has understandably caused many to question the game’s fate.

Sources indicate that however, a few hours after the cancellation rumor made the rounds, Bloomberg’s Jason Schreier reported on Bluesky that Skydance’s leadership addressed the rumor with the development team on Slack and assured them Marvel 1943 was not canceled. However, Schreier adds this could change due to the uncertainty caused by the recent merger between Warner Bros. Discovery and Paramount Skydance (Skydance New Media is a game development branch of the now-merged Skydance Corporation).

Skydance Games told the development team behind Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra on Slack this afternoon that the game is not canceled, despite a widely circulated rumor on Twitter today claiming that it was.

Furthermore, Kotaku’s Rebekah Valentine clarified in her report that Marvel 1943 executive producer Lu Giglotti told staff in a Skydance Slack message he’d spoken directly with the executive leadership team to confirm Marvel 1943 is still alive, saying, "There is no truth to these claims." According to Kotaku’s report, Giglotti informed the team that Marvel 1943 was approaching an Alpha milestone later this month. Giglotti also told staff not to let the rumor distract them and that Skydance was "monitoring the situation" to address in the future.

Kotaku’s report also sheds light on the game’s tumultuous development cycle. Marvel 1943 was originally pitched as a Netflix game before it was eventually turned into a console and PC title. This transition means the current iteration is “light on gameplay” and lacks substantial interactions, with players primarily using a single button to play it.

This isn't a completely surprising revelation, as Marvel 1943 was billed as a narrative-driven, linear single-player experience when it was revealed, but the style of game has never been clear. The same reveal also saw Skydance promise the game boasted "intuitive controls and exhilarating second-to-second gameplay that captures the action and excitement of Marvel, inspired by landmark comics, television, and films, as they navigate this all-fresh globe-trotting adventure." This disconnect may be attributed to Kotaku also reporting that Marvel 1943 is “well over budget,” and its overall scope has been heavily scaled back. Regardless, the outlet’s source claims the game is “close to done.”.

Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra was initially slated to launch in 2025. It was then delayed to early 2026 "to add more polish", according to Skydance, before being pushed again to an undetermined launch window. The game has no announced platforms.

Although Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra appears safe for now, other recent projects have not been as fortunate. Be sure to read our stories about the recent high-profile cancellations of Gang of Dragon and Fairgames.

[Sources: Jason Schreier, Kotaku].

The Blood of Dawnwalker is getting a New Game Plus mode in next week's update

💡 Key Takeaways
  • UPGRADE 17TH NOVEMBER: The Blood of Dawnwalker update 1.2 - the update that brings a New Game Plus mode, predominantly - is now available on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series S/X.
  • Sources indicate that fresh Game Plus, as mentioned below, raises the level cap to 100, and scales enemies and regions in the game around you.
  • There'll be new versions of equipment with new stats to find, and they'll be labelled with "NG+" so you know when you've picked one up.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPGRADE 17TH NOVEMBER: The Blood of Dawnwalker update 1.2 - the update that brings a New Game Plus mode, predominantly - is now available on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series S/X.

Sources indicate that fresh Game Plus, as mentioned below, raises the level cap to 100, and scales enemies and regions in the game around you. Previously, the game was zone-scaled, so some zones were tougher than others. In New Game Plus, this will no longer be the case, so you can go and explore Xanthe's region at the back of Vale Sangora straight away, if you want to.

There'll be new versions of equipment with new stats to find, and they'll be labelled with "NG+" so you know when you've picked one up. You can unlock New Game Plus from the main menu after choosing your base save and difficulty option. All of your accrued skill perks and abilities will be available to you at the start of the Withering Away quest in the game's prologue.

The full patch notes for Dawnwalker update 1.2 are:.

ORIGINAL STORY 13TH NOVEMBER: A Latest Game Plus mode is coming to vampiric RPG The Blood of Dawnwalker next week.

Developer Rebel Wolves has now detailed everything coming with The Blood of Dawnwalker's Update 1.2, right now planned to go live sometime next week, and top of the list of changes is a New Game Plus for players who have already rolled credits on the game.

Industry observers note that "If you completed the Epilogue, you can dive right back into Vale Sangora with Upcoming Game+," the developer revealed earlier today. "Your level, skills, and inventory will carry over." Rebel Wolves is upping the level cap to 100 for New Game Plus, which will also have items with updated stats and enemies "balanced and scaled uniformly across all regions.".

Elsewhere in Update 1.2, the studio is making tweaks to "enemy health pools and how often they use their abilities during combat," and improving terrain geometry to allow for "smoother movement during combat and exploration." We'll need to wait for more comprehensive patch notes before finding out which enemies are getting spongier or flimsier, however.

While the incoming patch doesn't seem to be as beefy as the last - the one that added animal petting and an easier Story mode - it'll be a good way to sink your teeth deeper into a game that's already begging to be replayed, thanks to a time management mechanic that can drastically change any given run.

The new game from some former The Witcher 3 veterans came out in September and seems to have been a hit. Eurogamer's The Blood of Dawnwalker review called the game a "familiar dark fantasy adventure, but one with bold and provocative ideas of its own, that's mostly, enormously successful.".

#63467. 8 Game Boy JRPGs Still Trapped on Original Hardware

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1889 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dualshockers ↗ Open Full Page

8 Game Boy JRPGs Still Trapped on Original Hardware

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1889 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Game Boy changed lives.
  • With that stated, you now know my history with the JRPG genre started out humble, and it’s only grown over the years.
  • According to recent reports, as much as we look fondly on older console life cycles and libraries, none of them are completely free of strife.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Game Boy changed lives. Some of you reading this might feel like handheld gaming has always been there, but for those of us who grew up with a Game Boy or a Game Boy Color, it was truly something special. I remember sitting on the top of a toy box shelf in my closet, playing Pokémon Gold and Silver Late at night when I was meant to be at school that morning. I’d also rush to finish Pokémon battles because we had just pulled up to school that aforementioned morning and I’d have to get out of the car. But I can’t save right now, Mom, or even pause!

With that stated, you now know my history with the JRPG genre started out humble, and it’s only grown over the years. Through my line of work, I love to dig up old retro games that I overlooked when I was younger and try them out. With JRPGs, the catalogue is as vast as its age in the industry, which means it had its place on the Game Boy even if you might not recall it. A lot of prominent Game Boy JRPGs made it off the console, but today, I want to look at some games that were left behind.

According to recent reports, as much as we look fondly on older console life cycles and libraries, none of them are completely free of strife. There are some interesting developmental stories and struggles from back then, but something that baffles me is that Lufia: The Legend Returns was originally meant to be a PlayStation game. It survived a studio closure to return to the rights of the original developers, and that team rapidly shifted gears and made it for the Game Boy instead. Wild stuff!

Recent findings suggest that if you’re thinking that shift probably led to some awkward decisions, you’d be right! Lufia: The Legend Returns didn't get the best reception when it came out. It’s a bit confusing for Lufia regulars because puzzles and typical dungeon crawls are replaced with randomized maps that leave a lot to luck above everything else, but the story is well worth picking the game up for.

It has been revealed that the Lufia series is one of the more obscure classic JRPG franchises out there, so if you haven’t played it, it’s worth checking out. Especially since, for all of its flaws, Lufia: The Legend Returns has a unique grid-based battle system and plenty of classic JRPG elements like airships you’ve probably been missing, before Final Fantasy Resonance proved how that kind of stuff just can’t be beat. Like many of the games on this list, Lufia: The Legend Returns can only be enjoyed on original software these days unless you get lucky. It was released on the 3DS Virtual Console a few years back, but unfortunately we all know the fate of the Nintendo 3DS eShop.

According to recent reports, back when the Game Boy was around, a lot of RPGs and adventure games were still trying to find the dividing line between them. One of the games for this little handheld that made that line difficult was Bomberman Quest. The story goes that Bomberman is attacked while flying through space, and when he crashes down on an unknown planet, he finds every single engine of his ship missing. Getting it back requires playing a game that feels like the Zelda Game Boy titles.

In a recent development, bomberman Quest is a game that I feel like hits a lot of highs, but also hits a lot of lows. Might be why it never caught on. It’s got a true ending waiting for you if you take on all of its challenges, but its also got the most repetitive music. There’s cute NPC interactions between every enemy possible and unique dungeons you don’t see often, like a cloud dungeon. But it runs so slowly. It’s probably why it didn’t catch on, but it’s a fun lost treasure for fans of the old school Bomberman games under Hudson Soft.

Great Greed to me is a good game to look at if you want something historically relevant, fun, and a bit ridiculous at the same time. It’s a game where you get teleported to a strange world where most of the characters are named after food, while also honing in on themes of lobbying and the dangers of pollution. It’s a strange one, but it’s the kind of fun that most games don’t dare to be these days, so I’ll always shout it out when people look for recommendations.

Against the surprising food-themed names, including one named Microwave of all things at the very start, the most wild thing about Great Greed is how it hasn’t caught on sooner. Great Greed reviewed fairly decently back in the ’90s. Considering how so many people don’t know about this game until a list like this highlights it, no one played it despite that. I think it's because no one gave it a try, but Great Greed has been left to biodegrade on the Game Boy all this time.

Pokémon was the most well-known JRPG for the Game Boy. That’s not even up for debate. With a juggernaut like that, naturally a few other companies wanted to try and cash in on something similar. Capcom introduced their Pokémon rival Metal Walker in 1999. Despite what this might suggest, Metal Walker is rather creative in execution, and if you ask me, it deserved more spotlight than it got back in the day. It’s as if there was a Pokémon: Special Eevee version from the start. And that Eevee was a robot.

It has been revealed that that’s not even a joke! One of the cool aspects of Metal Walker is that you might only have one robot companion, but this companion can literally upgrade and evolve. You can gather cores you find in towns and dungeons that change the form of your robot on the fly. There’s also another elemental dynamic with different land, sea, and sky forms you can use to your advantage. This sounds a lot like Pokémon, doesn’t it? Well, a lot of critics agreed, and it didn’t exactly drum up interest on shelves because of it. So it’s just been left alone all this time.

According to recent reports, look. I love Mystery Dungeon games. I got into the games, and roguelikes, with Pokémon Mystery Dungeon when I was a kid. Yeah, I know. You saw that coming. Randomized dungeon floors with items to find and plenty of strategy to get to the bottom (or the top depending on the dungeon) is one of my favorite ways to pass the time and challenge myself. There are a lot of Mystery Dungeon games out there, but there’s one I’d like to nominate as an honorable member: Cave Noire for the Game Boy.

It has been revealed that cave Noire is a Japan-only game that was literally Mystery Dungeon before Torneko’s Great Adventure would create Mystery Dungeon as we know it. Like many games that would come later, namely the Pokémon Mystery Dungeon games, you play as an adventurer aiming to join the local guild. To join, you have to be strong enough to get through four randomly generated dungeons with scaling levels. Beat each dungeon six times, and you join the guild and beat the game, but there’s still plenty of dungeons to conquer after that. Its short and sweet size on the Game Boy keeps the game tight and challenging, which is a great retro recommendation for those who want a newer Mystery Dungeon game. Like the Pokémon ones. Sigh.

If you’ve heard of this game before, you’re likely either thinking that I’ve made a mistake somewhere and added a PS1 game to this list, or you already know this interesting factoid. Yes, Azure Dreams is a PS1 game, but it was also ported to the Game Boy Color of all things. Unlike the developmental shift of Lufia: The Legend Returns, Azure Dreams is a decent port of the PS1 game, even if it had to cut a few features to make it happen. One change you might notice is that there's a more Pokémon-like battle system now, which probably says a lot about why this game was brought to the Game Boy Color, huh?

Truthfully, Azure Dreams is one impressive GBC game. It features some fantastic sprite work, a very lofty start that matches its upbringing as a PlayStation title, and some in-depth systems you’ll need to learn to navigate and balance. The catch is that the tutorial is pretty heavy-handed, taking up an entire floor of the first dungeon, being explained in dialogue with every step. Oh. Yeah. It’s another game with randomly generated dungeon floors. Seems like Game Boy developers were really ahead of the times with these mechanics.

Industry observers note that ayakashi no Shiro is probably as obscure as they come for Game Boy titles. The title literally means “Castle of Ayakashi,” giving away the game’s simple premise. The Ayakashi are monsters that you’re in charge of defeating. So, you crawl through dungeons, fight ghosts, rats, bats, and more. And that’s it. Literally. Ayakashi no Shiro was considered a game without much depth by those that reviewed it back in Japan, but nowadays, it might be a breath of fresh air for those of us bogged down by more modern, overstimulating games.

Out of a lot of games on this list that could probably thrive from some sort of remake or classic release on Nintendo Switch Online or something, Ayakashi no Shiro is probably better off as the retro gem it is now. While a lot of other Game Boy games spawned franchises or at least have a good number of fans, Ayakashi no Shiro is one of the few titles by the now defunct SETA Corporation. As a result, this game’s fate is to haunt the Game Boy’s catalogue like the ghosts within its dungeon walls.

Recent findings suggest that yes, this really is a vegetable-based JRPG made by Atlus for the Game Boy. Spud’s Adventure is one of my favorite games on the Game Boy just for the humor in that sentence alone. Like Ayakashi no Shiro, there isn’t much to this little portable adventure, so it isn’t one of the most iconic Game Boy games or anything, but seeing Persona-creating Atlus doing something so charming and cute during its humble beginnings is never not surprising for anyone who didn’t know about it already. So I’ll mention it any chance I get.

If you’re looking for a quick and easy Game Boy title to blow dust off of and enjoy for a little while, Spud’s Adventure is the perfect game. As Spud the potato, you’ll traverse a tower to save Princess Mato from her kidnapper. You’ll fight enemies and solve puzzles along the way like every other small adventure game before RPGs were more widely defined. It isn’t too hard, and some of the power-ups are a bit zany. It might not be a game to write home about, but it’s definitely one that I think Atlus’ biggest fans should at least try. You know. For the fact that something this charmingly goofy exists at all. You’ve gotta love it.

Tech Report: The Sims 4 developer hasn't forgotten about its quality of life commitment, and is back with an update on what to expect in 2026

💡 Key Takeaways
  • As the The Sims 4 continues into its second decade, the volume of newly introduced content, major expansions, and long-awaited features has grown in lockstep.
  • The effort required to fix them is what led developer Maxis to make a commitment to improve the game’s technical state, and the developer has now returned to update the community on what to expect in 2026.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As the The Sims 4 continues into its second decade, the volume of newly introduced content, major expansions, and long-awaited features has grown in lockstep. Unfortunately, that has also meant that, given how old the game is, a few technical problems remain a nuisance.

The effort required to fix them is what led developer Maxis to make a commitment to improve the game’s technical state, and the developer has now returned to update the community on what to expect in 2026.

Sources indicate that the quality of life pledge was made in September last year, through the introduction of a roadmap. Since then, the developer issued one revision on its progress. Which brings us to this week’s upcoming blog post, which further builds on everything that’s come before.

In the post, Maxis revealed a few key areas it’s going to be focusing on going forward. Though specific release dates for these changes were not shared, the list of complications should resonate with many players, as it covers many often-discussed topics.

Sources indicate that the first stage of the upcoming roadmap covers March through August. Over that period, you can expect Sims' autonomy to improve. This goes for things like how they choose locations for certain actions, they way they interact with certain objects, and even how often they interrupt conversations.

The infant and caregiver relationship is being updated, too, in order to improve autonomy and make sure your little Sims don’t miss out on milestones and interactions. That stage of the roadmap also includes fixes for black photo challenges, and other crashes and freezing.

According to recent reports, the next period takes place September through December, and it includes more interesting changes. One of the goals with this one is to improve Sims’ dining experience, which covers issues around eating and drinking.

According to recent reports, another crucial area of focus with this stage is family trees, and relationships between members of the same family. Maxis wants to improve the game’s genealogy systems to make relationship tracking across generations more robust so that your family history isn’t lost.

Depending on how the first stage goes, you might see more issues join the list of what the developer is looking at for the second stage of the roadmap.

Recent findings suggest that the good news is that you won’t have to wait too long for the game’s next patch. Due out in March, this next revision will feature around 55 fixes, including for some commonly reported complications.

Until then, you may want to check out The Sims 4’s Lost Legacies Event, which is available now until the middle of March. If you picked up the game’s latest expansion, check if you tried those Royalty & Legacy cheats.

GTA 6: How To Know Which Buildings Can Be Entered

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Before launch, Rockstar teased that GTA 6 would have "hundreds" of interior spaces that could be explored.
  • If you've been cruising through Leonida, you might've already tried to enter a few, awkwardly ramming into locked doors over and over and wrecking havoc on Lucia's shoulder until you give up.
  • It's not immediately obvious, but as highlighted by Reddit user u/Saladinismo, every building with an interior is marked on the map in a darker shade of blue, making them distinct from the closed-off buildings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Before launch, Rockstar teased that GTA 6 would have "hundreds" of interior spaces that could be explored.

If you've been cruising through Leonida, you might've already tried to enter a few, awkwardly ramming into locked doors over and over and wrecking havoc on Lucia's shoulder until you give up. Thankfully, there's an easy way to tell which buildings can be entered.

It's not immediately obvious, but as highlighted by Reddit user u/Saladinismo, every building with an interior is marked on the map in a darker shade of blue, making them distinct from the closed-off buildings. Just don't expect every single door to be unlocked when you pull up.

"I've also noticed that just because an entire building is dark blue, doesn't mean every entrance will work," explained u/TypeS2K_ in the comments. "For example, I saw a dark blue house but all the main doors wouldn't do anything. It was an open entrance to a basement around back. Just fyi, for anyone wondering. Sometimes you'll need to search around a bit.".

Dark blue could mean anything from the building itself to the garage, rooftop access, or even just the toilet, but it's still a good way to know where the interior spaces are. And just looking from the map, Rockstar wasn't kidding. There are hundreds of spots to explore, meaning plenty of places to rob. Don't worry about doing your shoulder in trying every possible entrance, though. As noted by u/xx_HotShot_xx, "Activating 'focus' will highlight doors that can be opened.".

Recent findings suggest that it's worth keeping an eye on the dark blue buildings in Vice City, especially around the richer areas, as you can actually break into the expensive homes and steal special vehicles from the garages. So, it's not just a gimmick to make Leonida feel bigger — it all ties back to the robberies and heists that line Jason and Lucia's pockets.

  • Industry observers note that all members of Hidden Horses own a share of the company, with bosses "democratically" appointed, in the words of a FAQ.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that back in July, Doom developers id Software laid off around a hundred people as part of wider Microsoft blood-letting. Now, a few of those devs have founded a new employee-owned studio, Hidden Horses. Their first project is Danger Pay, a single-player FPS influenced by ancient arcade blaster Smash TV (pictured) and dystopian movies such as deadly gameshow fable The Running Man – itself an influence on Smash TV.

Hidden Horses have 20 id Software alumni on the books, including former lead VFX artist Todd Boyce, principal engine programmer Dustin Land, senior AI and gameplay engineer Daniel Young, producer Andrew Willis, senior technical designer Jordan Turner, principal technical designer Tim Locke, and senior skybox artist Allison Dombek. They're looking to make "the kind of old school shooters that we think people want more of," in Land's words.

Industry observers note that all members of Hidden Horses own a share of the company, with bosses "democratically" appointed, in the words of a FAQ. "Our structure is quite flat, and we elect leaders when needed," Willis told Vertical Slice in a separate interview. "Financially, this means we are not subject to investor demands and the preservation of the company and the jobs it sustains is paramount over needless growth and our 'capital' doesn't compete for returns with other potential investments.".

All of which is obviously gesturing towards the horse elephant in the room: Microsoft, who've made enormous cuts to their Xbox biz in their eagerness to further supercharge their $4 trillion market value.

"We've replicated some things, changed some things, and added others [from our id Software days]," Willis went on. "Overall, I think top-down hierarchy is something we all have bad experiences with—we also don't want to trend chase or make a game by focus group. We want to make the kinds of classic gameplay focused games that we would play ourselves. We think there is a market for that and our experiences with the gaming community in our past work history informs that.".

Willis's hope is that the "flat" structure will motivate staff to work harder, because they feel like they have a meaningful say over the manufacturer's direction. "It allows all ideas to be considered and means we don't miss out on any contributions from our employees just because they don't sit high up in some arbitrary hierarchy," he stated..

According to recent reports, I'm cynical about "flat" firm structures, myself. I think they are very often just an excuse for the biggest egos in a company to throw their weight around. It can work given a friendly initial mix of founders, but it gets complicated when you start hiring new people who don't have the same chemistry. Mind you, there are no aims to expand the company dramatically for the foreseeable. "We want to create a vehicle that allows us to make games for our livelihoods, not to make crazy profits and get 100x returns," Willis went on. I'm also a bit leery of the fact that Hidden Horses have popped up a Kickstarter, because I'm leery about crowd-funding in general, even when Peter Molyneux isn't involved. The studio founders are presently working on some promotional initiatives to drum up support, including a studio documentary and *squints* a promotional beer? Still, I'm happy to hear that at least a few Cacodemon wranglers jettisoned by the big M have landed on their hooves feet. I wish Hidden Horses the best of luck with it all. As for Danger Pay, proper screens, footage and release details are to follow.

Netflix's long-gestating Magic: The Gathering animated series is called Planeswalker, and it's coming in 2027.

Industry observers note that the title was revealed at MagicCon Atlanta, and Netflix shared a first look at the show on Twitter/X on 13th November. "Every great story begins with a spark. Here's your first look at Planeswalker, a new animated series based on Magic: The Gathering. Coming to Netflix in 2027", the organization wrote, and shared a teaser, which you can see below:.

In a recent development, according to a synopsis shared with IGN, the series follows Chandra Nalaar, "a volatile pyromancer hunted for her gifts, and haunted by her past". It continues: "Confronted by an insidious force, Chandra and some of the most legendary Planeswalkers must harness their extraordinary abilities, navigate treacherous alliances, and battle their own inner demons to prevent a cataclysmic war that threatens to consume their very existence".

In a recent development, netflix first announced a Magic: The Gathering series in June 2019, with Avengers: Endgame directors Joe and Anthony Russo attached, and it was originally due in late 2022. Two years in, the original showrunners departed over creative differences, and in September 2024, Netflix confirmed it had started again from scratch with Star Trek: Picard and 12 Monkeys showrunner Terry Matalas in charge.

In a recent development, IGN reports that Matalas, who most recently ran Marvel's VisionQuest, is running the show alongside Cindy Appel. Budapest-based studio DIGIC Pictures is handling the animation.

8 Red Flags That Lucia Has in GTA 6

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1154 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto 6’s story is built around the relationship between Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval, and there is plenty in the game that showcases how in love they are.
  • He spends the beginning of the game putting in serious work to provide for his girl, and he even fixes up the house to make it a truly livable space.
  • She tells him that he needs to do better and envies those who have more than her.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6’s story is built around the relationship between Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval, and there is plenty in the game that showcases how in love they are. Both of them go out of their way for each other, and stick together through thick and thin.

Is that really for the best though? Let’s be honest, Jason is a stud. He spends the beginning of the game putting in serious work to provide for his girl, and he even fixes up the house to make it a truly livable space.

What does Lucia do in return? She tells him that he needs to do better and envies those who have more than her. Let’s face it, she is a walking red flag.

Recent findings suggest that it is important to stay grounded and to make sure that you don’t want too much at times, and that is something that Lucia just can’t do. She is willing to do anything to make it big. Her immediate thought after getting out of prison is that she wants to someday be on a yacht.

That is not inherently a bad dream, but the willingness to go above and beyond by breaking the law on multiple accounts and accepting sketchy deals make it a red flag.

She can work hard, get back on her feet, and provide for her son. She doesn’t need to risk it all to get a lavish lifestyle that may ultimately end up with her back in prison.

In a recent development, lucia spent time in prison, and she gets out shortly after the start of the game. You would think that Lucia would have learned to avoid crime after spending time in prison. Instead, it is the exact opposite.

She gets out of prison, and her first thought is to commit crimes in order to get money. She could let Jason keep doing his thing, but instead she calls up her friend and makes Jason ask about a job with them so that they can get more money.

It has been revealed that she doesn’t care about staying out of trouble. Instead, she jumps straight back into it. It’s almost like she wants to get caught.

There are a few rules that Lucia must abide by when she gets out of prison, with the most key of them being that she is under house arrest. This requires her to wear an ankle monitor, and she is only allowed to stray about a half mile away from Jason’s home unless she is working.

Recent findings suggest that while she pays attention to this rule at first, she ignores it the first chance she gets. While her ankle monitor is still on, she goes for a flight with Jason despite him advising her not to.

On top of this, when they have a chance to spend time with Kat and Mattia, she takes the opportunity to have her ankle monitor removed and goes for a night on the town.

There is something to be said about someone who is willing to fight for what they believe in or rush to the defense of others. However, sometimes this can be a detriment and can hurt a relationship.

In a recent development, lucia tends to have a very hot-blooded attitude. Meaning, she likes to pick fights when others are in the wrong, and she will defend her opinion until she dies.

If someone says something salty, Lucia is the first to snap back at them, and while it isn’t always good to stay quiet in every situation, there are times where she needs to learn to breathe, let it out, and move on instead of wanting to fight.

Lucia and Jason are like two sides of the same coin, but one side is focused on control while the other side is focused on chaos, and Lucia is the chaotic side. It is a fun dichotomy in the game, but in a relationship, this chaotic nature can get you killed.

Sources indicate that lucia likes to take the route of violence in most situations. She doesn’t stick to a initiative, deciding instead to throw it out and improvise.

It is this impulsive nature that landed her in jail in the first place while she was separated from Jason, and it is the same chaotic nature that could possibly land both of them in jail if Jason wasn’t around to be a bit more logical. While Lucia gets things done, that type of chaos isn’t always healthy.

Throughout GTA 6, you are wanted, and it is sometimes difficult to get by, but Lucia has the attitude of never giving up, which means that she is willing to fight until she draws her last breath. While this can be good in some circumstances, when you are wanted by the cops, it can be a major downfall.

If this wasn’t a GTA game and someone had that attitude, they would be in a world of hurt when the cops came rolling in. Even when Jason was to the point of wanting to call it in, she refused, and she dictated that they never give up.

Eventually, this is bound to land her in even more hot water than she is already in, and she will only have herself to blame.

Lying is sometimes okay, but only when it is because you are trying to hide a gift for someone or maybe you tell a little white lie to your child. It isn’t okay to lie to your partner or the police, both of which Lucia does.

As soon as she gets caught doing something she wasn’t supposed to, which she caused because she refused to listen to Jason, she lied to her parole officer.

In her defense, the parole officer is a jerk and comes off as creepy, but that is still no reason to lie, and to force your partner to lie on your behalf is also wrong, yet for Lucia, this stuff comes naturally.

There are a lot of people out there who like to party, and that is perfectly fine. They like to have a few drinks, kick back with their friends, and have a good time. Meanwhile, you have the few who are extreme party animals.

Recent findings suggest that they do drugs, hit the liquor hard, and party all night long. That is the type of girl Lucia can be, and that is a massive red flag for a lot of people.

It has been revealed that there are some online who have said that she is “for the streets” because of her willingness to let it all out and party all night long. As soon as she sees people wasting money on breaking champagne bottles and speeding through Vice City in nice cars, she immediately lets her party animal out of its cage and follows exactly what they do.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Version Luna 5 of Genshin Impact is now live, but it's a bittersweet occasion for fans of HoYoverse's breakout gacha RPG – at the very least, those who are still playing the game on PlayStation 4, which is presumably true of somebody out there.
  • According to recent reports, hoYoverse announced last year that they intended to wind down support for Genshin Impact on PS4, which – alongside PC, Android, and iOS – was one of the launch platforms for the game back in 2020.
  • The game has already been delisted on the platform since last September, meaning it was no longer available for download and could only be updated by players who already had it installed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Version Luna 5 of Genshin Impact is now live, but it's a bittersweet occasion for fans of HoYoverse's breakout gacha RPG – at the very least, those who are still playing the game on PlayStation 4, which is presumably true of somebody out there.

According to recent reports, hoYoverse announced last year that they intended to wind down support for Genshin Impact on PS4, which – alongside PC, Android, and iOS – was one of the launch platforms for the game back in 2020. And with Version Luna 5, those end days are upon us.

The game has already been delisted on the platform since last September, meaning it was no longer available for download and could only be updated by players who already had it installed. But as of today, paid purchases from the in-game store have been disabled on PS4; and in six weeks' time, on approximately April 8, Version Luna 6 will discontinue access to the PS4 version altogether.

In many ways this is unsurprising – Genshin is already available on both PS5 and Xbox Series to sate fans eager to play on console, and the PS4's hardware is increasingly struggling to keep up with this massive open-world game after more than five years of regular updates have ballooned both its file size and technical requirements.

Aptly enough, Luna 5 takes the main story action back to the nation of Mondstadt, the location where the Traveler (and, by extension, the players) took their first steps into the world of Teyvat back in September 2020. It feels like a symbolic last hurrah for the original console home of the game, as does the inclusion of a Chronicled Wish banner focussing on some of Mondstadt's most iconic (read: too old to be meta by now) 5-Star characters – namely Eula, Mona, Albedo, Klee, Diluc, and Jean.

And as the icing on the Tea Break Pancake, this banner is running alongside the long-anticipated introduction of Varka – the Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius who has been a major character in the game's lore from the very beginning, but who only became playable with today's update.

Looking ahead to that post-Luna 6 future, Genshin Impact will still be available on PS5, as well as Xbox Series consoles, PC, and mobile devices – so hopefully anyone who is still playing primarily on PS4 will find another platform they can continue the adventure on by April.

GTA 6 “Greatest Artistic Achievement In History,” Says Cyberpunk 2 Director

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto 6 is the highest-rated game in history, only rivaled by Ocarina of Time — but no developer should try to rival its scope and ambition.
  • According to recent reports, we don't know what exactly the budget was, but Rockstar head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe recently pushed back on rumors of a $2 billion price tag, clarifying it cost somewhere under $1.5 billion.
  • Indeed, Cyberpunk 2 creative director Igor Sarzynski has made it clear that CD Projekt Red has no intention of rivaling GTA 6, despite the broad-stroke similarities between both series.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 is the highest-rated game in history, only rivaled by Ocarina of Time — but no developer should try to rival its scope and ambition.

According to recent reports, we don't know what exactly the budget was, but Rockstar head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe recently pushed back on rumors of a $2 billion price tag, clarifying it cost somewhere under $1.5 billion. Most studios don't have that kind of change to throw around, because most studios aren't printing money with a game like GTA Online.

Indeed, Cyberpunk 2 creative director Igor Sarzynski has made it clear that CD Projekt Red has no intention of rivaling GTA 6, despite the broad-stroke similarities between both series.

Sources indicate that "GTA 6-induced-open-world-game-dev-depression is real," he mused on Bluesky. "Probably the single greatest artistic achievement in history, I mean it. Scale, density, coherence, thoughtfulness of it all, just a technological and creative miracle. Cyberpunk 2 is canceled, imma go sweep autumn leaves in my backyard now.

"Seriously though I think we're doing something of our own, with a different unique flavor," he continued. "GTA is impressive in a way all great art is, it expands what is possible, a captivating vision flawlessly executed.".

It's a sentiment echoed by others in the games' industry, like Larian Studios head of publishing Michael Douse, better known by his online moniker - Very AFK.

"Maybe in a world that often feels like it's going to sh*t it is nice for everyone to enjoy a cultural moment together that brings every audience (and every generation) the same excitement, behind something that has turned out to be genuinely brilliant," he posted to Twitter. "Not every game needs to be GTA, and that both makes space for other types of experiences, and the rare moment even more special!".

Naughty Dog game designer Michael Barclay even said that GTA 6 appears to him "as a Bugatti Veyron would to a nervous Victorian child.".

Considering, just three years ago, the industry warned that Baldur's Gate 3 was the game no other developer should try to replicate, given the unbelievable scope and sheer amount of interactivity, recorded dialogue, and branching paths it offered to players, that's one hell of an endorsement.

TheGamer's own Lead News Editor, George Foster, put it bluntly in his GTA 6 review, "we'll never get a game like it again," and frankly, we shouldn't.

Ballooning development budgets are already putting a target on studios' backs, making every single latest release a financial gamble that could mean mass layoffs or even closure, and those high-stakes are only making the industry increasingly risk-averse.

Industry observers note that GTA 6 shouldn't set a new bar for other developers to strive for. The unimaginable amount of resources, personnel, and time it took to develop the game is simply unrealistic for other studios. Thankfully, CDPR understands that. Let's just hope the rest of the industry does, too.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Call of Duty Endowment is marking Remembrance Day and its 17th anniversary by encouraging Modern Warfare 4 and Warzone players to pick up its Valor Pack, with all of Activision's net proceeds going towards helping veterans find jobs.

The Call of Duty Endowment Valor Pack - which has been available since Modern Warfare 4 launched on 23rd October - was designed by the Endowment and Infinity Ward with US Marine Corps veteran and Medal of Honor recipient Kyle Carpenter in mind.

The items include a melee weapon blueprint inscribed with "Worth Fighting For", plus items called Relentless and Still Standing.

According to the Call of Duty blog, 100 percent of Activision's net proceeds from the pack (after VAT and sales tax) go to the Endowment.

To mark Remembrance Day, players who owned it and launched either game before 6pm GMT on 12th November also received double XP tokens and a DMZ survival kit.

"Veterans bring incredible skills into the workplace after military service," remarked Carpenter.

The Endowment, which supports veterans in the UK as well as the US, says it has now helped place more than 180,000 into "high-quality jobs", and wants to reach 200,000 by 2030.

Other partners are also raising money, with Pilot's round-up campaign raising more than £4.7 million ($6 million) for the Endowment since 2019. Polaris will also donate around £19,500 ($25,000) if players collectively complete 5 million rides in its DAGOR vehicle across Modern Warfare 4 and Warzone by 25th November.

It comes two weeks after Activision apologised to bereaved families of the Itaewon crowd crush victims and confirmed it would remove real footage of the tragedy from Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4. Players discovered that the game's opening cinematic uses short news clips to depict fictional civilian casualties during a North Korean invasion of South Korea. Those clips have since been found to include archive footage from the 2022 Itaewon disaster, in which around 160 people died.

Call of Duty's anti-cheat team Ricochet recently revealed it's officially cracking down on Warzone Agent.

"One of those ways where you can use AI ethically": CDPR have modified Geralt's Polish voice in The Witcher 3: Songs of the Past with genAI, due to actor's stroke

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that CD Projekt Red have reportedly enlisted Ukrainian AI firm Respeecher to modify voice lines recorded for the Polish version of Geralt of Rivia in The Witcher 3's upcoming Songs of the Past expansion.
  • Recent findings suggest that game File report that after suffering a stroke in 2019 and having to rehabilitate his speech, Rozenek was able to record some lines as Geralt for a quest in The Witcher 3's 2022 next-gen update, but that doing so left the actor "so exhausted".
  • Sources indicate that after a meeting between the two sides confirmed that Rozenek's voice had grown lower and gruffer due to some combination of the stroke and him simply getting older, the studio made the decision not to recast the actor, but instead let modify Respeecher modify his lines to make them sound closer to those original recordings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that CD Projekt Red have reportedly enlisted Ukrainian AI firm Respeecher to modify voice lines recorded for the Polish version of Geralt of Rivia in The Witcher 3's upcoming Songs of the Past expansion. The move's been made with the permission of Geralt's Polish voice actor, Jacek Rozenek, and is rooted in the studio wanting his fresh lines to sound similar to the ones he recorded for the original game prior to having a stroke which has altered how he sounds.

Recent findings suggest that game File report that after suffering a stroke in 2019 and having to rehabilitate his speech, Rozenek was able to record some lines as Geralt for a quest in The Witcher 3's 2022 next-gen update, but that doing so left the actor "so exhausted". With next year's Songs of the Past expansion, CD Projekt Red were seemingly more concerned about making sure lines recorded by post-stroke Rozenek don't sound markedly different to those he recorded a decade ago for the base game and its existing expansions.

Sources indicate that after a meeting between the two sides confirmed that Rozenek's voice had grown lower and gruffer due to some combination of the stroke and him simply getting older, the studio made the decision not to recast the actor, but instead let modify Respeecher modify his lines to make them sound closer to those original recordings. Rozenek reportedly gave his blessing for this to go ahead. "The point is that this voice should be as close as possible to my voice from 12 years ago," he told Game File. "I have great trust...for the creators of this game.".

This isn't the first time CD Projekt Red have enlisted Respeecher's services. Back in 2023, it was revealed that the studio had used speech synthesis software to make ripperdoc Viktor Vektor's lines in the Polish version of Cyberpunk 2077's Phantom Liberty expansion sound like actor Miłogost Reczek. Reczek died in 2021 before he could reprise his role as Vektor for the DLC, so rather than recasting the character across the whole game to avoid noticeable differences in voice, CD Projekt got another actor to voice Vektor's new lines for Phantom Liberty, then used the genAI tech to make those lines sound like Reczek was delivering them. CD Projekt Red said at the time that they'd gotten permission from Reczek's family before going ahead with their plan.

Industry observers note that speaking to Game File about this latest use of genAI on Rozenek's Songs of the Past lines, CD Projekt localisation producer Mikołaj Szwed noted that "as a person working with voice actors over all the regions in the world, this is a big concern". "I do think this is one of those ways where you can use AI ethically, with consent and also to do something good," he added. The argument the studio are making at current is that this was "a special case" due to Rozenek's specific situation with Songs of the Past.

Geralt's English voice actor Doug Cockle reportedly won't have his lines for the new expansion get the same genAI treatment, nor will any lines Rozenek records for future Witcher games, with the studio seemingly happy to lean on the passage of in-game time as an explanation for Geralt sounding different in the latter case.

As ever, there's a debate to be had as to whether CD Projekt Red should have simply recast Rozenek's role in Songs of the Past if the difference bothered them so, possibly while bringing the actor on to help tutor whomever his human replacement for Songs of the Past would be in nailing the exact gravelly tone needed for Geralt. That way, you'd have two actors being paid for work rather than forking out for genAI instead of one of them, though it's possibly an idea that'd only work well in theory. If I were Rozenek I'm not sure I'd be totally happy aiding someone who could potentially be tapped to replace me going forwards, though it does very much seem like the lesser of two evils when compared to the potential of voice actors being replaced by genAI line readings.

As far as the game alone is concerned, I'm also not sure Geralt's voice being different in the new expansion is something that'd bother me too much when playing. One would assume he'd not suddenly be sounding like a member of Alvin and the Chipmunks, and there are plenty of storyline justifications you could concoct or lean on for him sounding that bit gruffer at times.
