10 Glitches and Bugs Plaguing GTA 6 at Launch

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1364 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, every fresh game has its… quirks.
  • Grand Theft Auto 6 is still fresh, and people are jumping into it as I write these words.
  • Planes fly through buildings, cars teleport onto the highway, and it doesn’t seem to be bound to one console, as Xbox and PlayStation users have both been reporting these issues.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, every fresh game has its… quirks. This is especially true in the modern era of gaming, as many games now release with game breaking glitches and bugs that have an effect on how people enjoy it.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is still fresh, and people are jumping into it as I write these words. While on the surface the game looks like magic, many people have been finding numerous bugs that have destroyed their experience.

Planes fly through buildings, cars teleport onto the highway, and it doesn’t seem to be bound to one console, as Xbox and PlayStation users have both been reporting these issues.

Textures and environments can be tricky, especially when you have a map that is as massive as the one in GTA 6. There are bound to be some barriers that end up becoming a bit glitchy, and players have found plenty of them.

There have been a number of reports that players have been glitching into walls inside buildings, and it seems to mostly happen when fighting.

Not all walls are affected, as it seems to only affect interior, lower cut walls, and not full size interior walls or exterior boundaries. Still it is pretty awkward when you want to fight someone and you both end up teleporting into a wall.

According to recent reports, okay, so not taking damage isn’t necessarily a bad thing, but in the world of GTA, where things are supposed to be realistic, it is kind of strange. It would be nice to not take damage at times, but it enhances the realism of the experience.

Recent findings suggest that cars have always been a bit of a tricky thing, and they are still a bit tricky in GTA 6. Players have reported being able to teleport out of their car while flying down a street without taking damage.

According to recent reports, normally, you are supposed to dive from the car, but instead, players have said the character model just teleports out of the vehicle and starts running on the road until they come to a stop. It’s a bit strange.

Sources indicate that some players have noticed a peculiar thing while flying planes in GTA 6, and that is that they sometimes don’t respect the laws of physics, allowing them to phase through objects. It doesn’t happen a lot, but it is weird when it does happen.

It could be intentional, because it seems to only happen to large buildings, but it wasn’t like that in GTA 5, so it probably wasn’t an intentional choice.

Players have noticed that when they jump out of a plane, it seems to phase through all the buildings around it, allowing it to just crash into the ground instead of hitting the building and falling like it used to.

Cops can now tase you in GTA 6, and it is pretty amusing to watch yourself get tased. Just like in real life, it locks up your character’s muscles, and it makes them fall to the ground helpless. Shortly after, they are free to stand back up.

Unfortunately, not every player has been able to stand back up, as some have said that they get stuck in the ground after getting tased. Their character model clips into the pavement, causing them to get stuck in place for a while before their character gets released.

This can be a bit jarring, but it isn’t something that completely breaks the game. It just makes things a little easier for the police to catch you.

Sources indicate that early in the game, Donnie is taken hostage. The game uses this as an opportunity to teach you about stealth and combat. It’s a nice little tutorial that is very engaging. Unfortunately, some players have reported that they need to restart this level because the game breaks for them.

Industry observers note that when sneaking around the enemies, you will spot a cage. This cage has a tendency to be a bit buggy, and sometimes you will get pulled into it if you decide to take cover against it.

This traps you inside the cage, unable to get out, and therefore, unable to complete the mission. The only thing that is worse is that if the enemies know you are in there, you basically become an easy target.

People have been waiting 13 years to get their hands on GTA 6. It has been one of the most talked about games of the last decade, and some people can’t even get into the game. Others who can, have it crash on them shortly after launch.

This isn’t a console specific issue, though I have seen more people say they have a PS5 when it comes to the crashing issue. The issue is that the game automatically crashes shortly after launch.

People have stated that they have tried to rebuild the database, and have even redownloaded the game, and nothing has worked. It is okay for some bugs to occur, but the game crashing every time you try to play it is entirely different.

Getting wanted by the police is a common occurrence in any GTA game, but things are a bit different in GTA 6. The cops are more lively, and they notice more things. There are a lot of systems in place to make the entire experience more thrilling.

Industry observers note that well, these same systems tend to bug out a bit right now, and they bug out by giving you an infinite wanted level. Well, almost infinite, as there is a way to remove the wanted level.

There have been reports of players being stuck with a wanted level for hours despite clearing all of the challenges with it. The only way to get it to end seems to be to go to sleep. Getting stuck being wanted in an area for hours sounds like a huge inconvenience.

According to recent reports, this is a bug that is affecting both consoles, but seems to be affecting Xbox more than PlayStation. Players have reported objects spawning as they drive at high speeds. By this, I mean cars will magically appear, so will NPCs, and other items.

GTA 6 is a massive game, and it could be that the loading has not been completely optimized, and when driving at very high speeds, the game may not be able to keep up with the load times.

I am not a tech wizard, so I don’t know exactly what causes it, but I do know that it has been bothering a lot of players, and they want it fixed ASAP.

This is an concern that appears to mostly be affecting those who are playing GTA 6 on the Xbox Series S, but there have been reports of players being unable to load textures and models, resulting in these low-poly models that are reminiscent of graphics you’d see on PS1 era games.

Everything turns blocky, the faces lose all texture, and all that can be made out is the basic shape of the body, some scraps for clothes, and the hair.

Industry observers note that it’s a shame that this is happening to people, and it reminds many of the crazy issues that were happening when Cyberpunk 2077 first launched. Odds are, it can be fixed with an patch, but for the time being, it sets a bad example.

It has been revealed that A significant part of any GTA game is committing crimes, and one of the many crimes that you will commit frequently is murder. This is mostly against gang members and other criminals, but it still counts, and you need these people to be able to take damage.

You also sometimes need to stop an NPC by hurting them and not killing them. Unfortunately, there is a bug that makes NPCs bulletproof, and some players have been saying they are emptying entire clips into an NPC for not a single bullet to affect them.

This breaks the game because it makes it so you can’t complete some missions. It is an urgent problem that Rockstar should fix so people can beat the game.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • GTA 6's Jason and Lucia might be hardened criminals, but Rockstar Games designed the couple to be relatable in other ways.
  • "Playing GTA 6, the main thing we want players to feel is connection.
  • "Living in the actual world in this present moment, it feels like there is so much noise and so much pressure on everyone - politics, the environment, media, social media.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6's Jason and Lucia might be hardened criminals, but Rockstar Games designed the couple to be relatable in other ways. As the studio's narrative lead explained, "we are all about two bits of bad luck away from completely losing it" in the real world.

"Playing GTA 6, the main thing we want players to feel is connection. To Jason and Lucia, who they need to believe in and inhabit for this journey through the game, but then also that connection in the game between the two characters," senior vice president of narrative, Rupert Humphries, explained in quotes given to GamesRadar+.

"Living in the actual world in this present moment, it feels like there is so much noise and so much pressure on everyone - politics, the environment, media, social media. It's coming at you from everywhere. It seems like we are all about two bits of bad luck away from completely losing it. That is the world we are showing you on the streets of Vice City and in the rest of Leonida - everyone's been driven to a kind of madness that comes out in lots of different ways, from conspiracy theories to self-help cults to get-rich-quick schemes and drug habits.".

Recent findings suggest that GTA 6's main couple doesn't exactly have many options outside of the criminal ones, and I think the game does a good job at giving them some real, personal, human stakes to ground it all - making their occasional robberies and murders a tad more understandable. As the couple says in the game, the world is stacked against them. They can't get ahead by playing by the rules.

Even so, GTA 6 still has an optimistic view on life in the modern era, which itself is a big departure from GTA 5's generally cynical world view: "With all that going on, we wanted to have two humans at the center of the story that the player can care about and see themselves in, and then this idea that maybe (however bad you are) we might all be better off when we're together and not going it alone.".

You can check our GTA 6 guide to see how to make the most of Jason and Lucia's relationship, or read our GTA 6 review if you're still on the fence.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It seems like we’re getting one of these every few months, but the world of mobile action RPGs that look like the games that, just a few years back, were only possible on consoles is expanding with another newly introduced entry.
  • Netmarble, a studio and publisher known for its free-to-play games on mobile and PC, recently unveiled the launch date for The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin, its next major release that’s very much coming for the Genshin Impact crowd.
  • Industry observers note that the Seven Deadly Sins: Origin is an open-world action RPG based on the world of The Seven Deadly Sins anime and manga.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It seems like we’re getting one of these every few months, but the world of mobile action RPGs that look like the games that, just a few years back, were only possible on consoles is expanding with another newly introduced entry.

Netmarble, a studio and publisher known for its free-to-play games on mobile and PC, recently unveiled the launch date for The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin, its next major release that’s very much coming for the Genshin Impact crowd.

Industry observers note that the Seven Deadly Sins: Origin is an open-world action RPG based on the world of The Seven Deadly Sins anime and manga. The game takes place in the world of Britannia, which looks similar to the way it does in the anime.

That stated, the story of the game is not based on the anime or manga, Instead, it’s an original story set in the universe of the show. You play as Prince Tristan of the Kingdom of Liones who must find a way to bring order back to Britannia.

The gameplay should be familiar to anyone who played a free-to-play action RPG in the last decade. It features action combat, a roster of diverse heroes that you assemble to form teams, and a large pretty world to explore where you’ll also get to meet new characters.

Speaking of which, while Origin has its own original story, expect to be teaming up with characters from the series - some of whom wouldn't be able to meet naturally. You can thank the game's multiversal story for that.

Industry observers note that beyond all the serious business of saving the world and battling monsters, The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin also has a cozy, relaxing side. You’ll be able to fish, cook, forage and take on the beauty of the world with your pals.

It has been revealed that the game has a bit of an unusual release schedule. It’s set to arrive on PC, PS5, iOS, and Android. PC (Steam), and PS5 players will be able to jump in starting March 16, whereas the global mobile launch is scheduled for one week later, on March 23.

You can pre-register right now on the official website if you’re interested in earning a few rewards when the game introduces. You can, of course, always wishlist the game on Steam and the PlayStation Store, too.

#63446. Amid soaring PC hardware prices, gaming monitors are getting cheaper and cheaper. Here's why, and what to buy

📅 12 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (2099 w)

Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rockpapershotgun ↗ Open Full Page

Amid soaring PC hardware prices, gaming monitors are getting cheaper and cheaper. Here's why, and what to buy

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2099 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Hello, good local-time-zone-adjusted afternoon, and let's just say it's been a while.
  • Instead I speak of screens, where there is actually some very good news.
  • Industry observers note that also bear in mind we've had a fair old bit of inflation in recent years.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hello, good local-time-zone-adjusted afternoon, and let's just say it's been a while. But I come back to you now at the turn of the technological tide. Well, sort of. Sadly I'm not here to predict an end to the ridiculous AI-fuelled chip crisis. That whole mess has a couple of years to run, surely.

Instead I speak of screens, where there is actually some very good news. In short, have you seen how cheap PC gaming monitors are? I mean remarkably, almost stupendously, cheap. I'm talking £60 / $60 for an entry-level 1080p panel with triple-digit refresh rate, sub-£200 / $250 for high-refresh 4K gaming. Heck, even OLED monitors now start with a "2" in both currencies.

Industry observers note that also bear in mind we've had a fair old bit of inflation in recent years. A 4K panel bought today for £200 is equivalent to paying roughly £150 back in 2020. All the while, that same £200 / $200 right now won't buy you a current-model gaming graphics card at all, even the most feeble example, and will barely secure a basic dual-channel 16GB DDR5 memory kit. Youch.

So, I think we can all agree monitors are cheap in the current chip-catastrophe context. The immediate question is why? The answer isn't all that complicated, actually. Most obviously, the display market isn't being devoured by the AI craze. All those data centres are stuffed with GPUs, memory chips and NAND flash, not monitors.

According to recent reports, by way of example, one of the largest latest AI data centres on Earth is Microsoft's new Fairwater site in Mount Pleasant, Wisconsin. It's thought to pack hundreds of thousands of Nvidia Blackwell GPUs. The cost doesn't bear thinking about, but those GPUs are built into what's known as "headless" server racks. In other words, they have no screens at all. Ultimately, the key compute hardware is all managed remotely, in which capacity the Fairwater facility is reported to currently have around 375 employees. If we generously assume each has two PC monitors, that's only 750 for the entire site.

AI isn't really driving demand on the end-user side of the equation, either. Put it this way: you don't need to buy a new phone, laptop or PC to access the latest models. At the same time, the display market is suffering from something of a glut of overcapacity. Chinese companies built out huge capacity in LCD panel manufacturing over the past decade, to the extent factories are now running underutilised. Meanwhile, even the OLED market is arguably oversupplied.

It has been revealed that in fact, Samsung and LG, the two massive noises in large OLED panel manufacturing (as opposed to OLED displays for tablets and phones), have been shifting emphasis away from TV panels to PC monitors because the latter offer better margins. Meanwhile, the AI boom has almost definitely meant lower demand for new PCs. Certainly, the big research houses point to cratering PC sales thanks to higher component costs. Long story short, that's oodles of capacity combined with weakening demand. Like I remarked, the explanation for cheap monitors isn't exactly rocket surgery, if you know what I mean.

What is a bit more complicated is making sense of what's available today in the gaming monitor market. With so much choice, where exactly is the very best value to be found? And are there any remaining pain points?

In a recent development, monitor specifications, to be sure, can be tricksy at the best of times. But if you're looking for some blanket rules to fling casually over the whole LCD monitor market - I'll be digging deeper into OLED tech another day - try these for size. Look for, at minimum, 300 nits brightness and 1ms response times. Refresh rates are a slightly more complicated call, but for the vast majority of games, 144Hz is plenty. For "esports-grade multiplayer fare like Counter-Strike or Dota 2, or I think a refresh in the high 200s will get the job done for most. If you'll benefit from more than that, you almost certainly know who you are already.

Oh, and heavily favour IPS over VA panels. Exceptions exist: there are some decent "Rapid VA" panels these days and Samsung, in particular, does some nippy VA models. But a lot of the cheaper stuff is pretty slow and smeary, making VA a risky buy. Finally, don't worry too much about claimed HDR capability, save for the fact that HDR 400 certification at least means the monitor can do 400 nits. Unless a monitor has local dimming, it won't be truly HDR capable.

In a recent development, anywho, one immediate and rather ironic issue is the growing mismatch between monitors and GPUs. For sure, it's great you can grab a high-refresh 4K monitor for such little money. It's almost hard to believe that you can have this 27-inch IPS MSI for sub-£200 (you're looking at $250 for the same model in the US), and it even has a 288Hz 1080p dual mode.

I actually favour 32 inches with my 4K gaming, and that's naturally a little pricier, especially if you insist on an IPS - which again, you probably should. But even $350 for that kind of panel (here's a comparable model for £340 in the UK) is a fraction of what you'd have paid for a similarly specced model a few years ago. And it probably wouldn't have included dual-mode functionality.

Here's the problem, though. How are you going to drive the thing, what with its eight million-plus pixels? After all, the cheapest RTX 5090 on Newegg right now is over $6,500. So high-end Nvidia GPUs now cost about as much as a decent used car.

Recent findings suggest that of course, you might be surprised just how effective the likes of an AMD RX 9070 XT or Nvidia RTX 5070-class GPU is at 4K thanks to upscaling technologies including DLSS and FSR. The latest transformer model upscalers really do knock out pretty stellar image quality. Add in a bit of frame gen and you have a compelling combination of visual sharpness, reasonably low latency and nice smoothframe rates, even in the most demanding of games. Perhaps the one thing you can't do is enable full path tracing in a game like Cyberpunk 2077 and still expect a slick experience, but standard ray tracing remains an option.

Recent findings suggest that the bigger snag, unsurprisingly, is that you can no longer bag a 5070 at (let alone below) its original £539 / $549 MSRP. Instead, you're looking at the thick end of £800 / $900. That's a bit of an ask for pairing with a £200 monitor, isn't it?

It has been revealed that I'd therefore argue that, for pure gaming purposes, the bang-for-buck sweet spot remains just where it's been sat twiddling its thumbs for the better part of a decade, namely 1440p. That applies to both its vanilla 16:9 aspect variety and my personally preferred ultrawide format, the latter being so very immersive and also pretty nifty for daily multi-tasking. Indeed, the 27-inch 1440p segment even brings the vibrant colours and infinite contrast of OLED panels into a reasonably affordable window.

According to recent reports, by way of example, £179 (or $150) is enough for a circa 200Hz, IPS 1440p panel with super low (by IPS standards) pixel response, even if the 250-nit brightness is lower than I'd like. Meanwhile, as I write these words, pricing for big-brand 27-inch 1440p gaming OLEDs kicks off at about £290 in the UK and roughly $270 in the US. Admittedly, those entry-level OLEDs come with some compromises, which I'll cover in a forthcoming post. But what you might call 'proper' OLED panels can be had around the low £300 / $300 mark - not throw-away money, for sure, but relatively accessible.

Recent findings suggest that the 34-inch 1440p ultrawide segment is a bit trickier, however. The good news is that conventional LCD models can be had for relative peanuts, with prices starting at about £220 or $249 for game-focused, high-refresh models. But those two example both use a VA panel, which usually means inferior pixel response.

It has been revealed that IPS models are a little thin on the ground when it comes to 34-inch ultrawide, but sneaking in below £300 / $300 is generally possible. The real bummer is OLED, where going ultrawide invokes a massive premium. The best price I can find on a substantial-brand 34-inch ultrawide today is $629 for this Asus model in the US and £648 for this MSI option in the UK.

That's awfully toppy, especially when you consider that you can grab a 49-inch, 5,120x1,440 ultrawide OLED for barely any more money. I do actually quite like those 49-inch ultrawides, but I have to concede the ergonomics are challenging. However, 4K OLEDs in 27-inch and 32-inch formats can also be had for as much as £100 / $100 less than the current cheapest 34-inch 1440p ultrawides, which doesn't make much sense to me.

Sources indicate that again, with 4K, there's the challenge of keeping all those pixels updated. If you already have a sufficiently mighty graphics card, though, I a 32-inch 4K OLED can make a fantastic all-round option, and something like this MSI model for £549 would be absolutely lovely. You get good pixel density and lots of space for daily desktopping, plus OLED visuals and a large enough panel to be really get you into your games.

It's just a pity that 34-inch OLED ultrawides remain so weirdly expensive, it being a format that ticks so many different boxes. As for my own personal money-no-object pick, well, I'm typing these words on the newly introduced Alienware AW3926QW, the 39-inch 5K2K beast with a Tandem WOLED panel and RGB subpixels.

Recent findings suggest that one could argue it's a relative steal at £1,079 or $1,100. I mean, it's pretty much peak current PC gaming display technology, and it's about half the price of what Nvidia's second-tier RTX 5080 graphics card is going for lately. Assuming you can even find one in stock.

At this point, the one major category I haven't covered is LCD monitors with mini-LED full-array local dimming. Cards on the table, I'm not a huge fan of mini-LED monitors. The detailed reasons for that are, perhaps, the subject for another day. But I've reviewed countless models and have yet to see one that didn't come with pretty serious compromises.

Sources indicate that that remarked, the technology has gotten a lot more accessible in the last 12 to 18 months, to the extent that 27-inch 1440p models start at just over $250. I've had that specific model in and came away pretty impressed. It's very, very punchy, and even factoring in the limitations of mini-LED versus OLED when it comes to lighting control and speed, I cannot deny the temptation.

Just for completeness, one further exception to the general rule of cheap gaming monitors involves ultra-high refresh monitors aimed at serious esports aficionados. I'm talking about panels like this 1,000Hz LG I sampled elsewhere. At £800 / $1,000 for a 25-inch 1080p IPS panel it's inevitably a niche proposition, and poor value by normal standards.

Recent findings suggest that I think a much better compromise for just about everyone, short of an actual esports pro, is to grab a larger, higher resolution monitor that offers one of those windowed 1080p modes running at about 500Hz or thereabouts. That way you've got a nice high-res panel for both work and play, as well as that ultra-low latency mode for when you want to dance around Dust 2 doling out the headshots or whatever.

Incidentally, I realise I've gone in a bit hot and heavy with the OLED content here, the implicit assumption being OLED is all that, and notably without addressing the obvious objections like the risk of burn-in. But all that, I hope you'll be pleased to hear, is very much the subject for my next RPS post on all things OLED.

Until then, all I can say is thank goodness PC monitors provide relative respite from the parlous state of much of the rest of the PC component market. It's absolutely brutal out there if you're building a gaming PC, but at least you'll get a lot of screen for your money.

Just to round things out, if anyone has any specific queries at any given price point, form factor or panel type, shout out below and I'll try to steer you in the direction of a decent model.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ubisoft is reportedly working on a new Rainbow Six Vegas game 18 years after the last entry in the series.

Recent findings suggest that according to Insider Gaming, the project is in early development at Ubisoft Montreal under the codename Spades. It’s one of three latest projects reportedly in production at the studio, and sources suggest a second of those is also set in the Rainbow Six universe. Eurogamer hasn’t been able to verify the report.

Industry observers note that it’s not yet clear what form the new game will take, but Insider Gaming’s sources said it's "likely Vegas 3 rather than a remake" of an existing game. Insider Gaming expects it will be several years before Ubisoft officially introduces a new Vegas game.

Sources indicate that rainbow Six Vegas launched in 2006, followed by Rainbow Six Vegas 2 in 2008. Since then, the series has centred on 2015's Rainbow Six Siege, and in August, Ubisoft declared Rainbow Six Tactics, a single-player, turn-based spin-off from Ubisoft Paris due in 2027.

Rainbow Six now sits under Vantage Studios, the Ubisoft subsidiary set up last year that also oversees Assassin’s Creed and Far Cry, and in which Tencent holds a 26.32 percent stake.

Last week, we learned that Ubisoft is reportedly working on two upcoming Assassin's Creed games: one set in ancient Rome, and a mobile spin-off set in Jerusalem. The leak came less than a week after Ubisoft issued a statement about the future of the Assassin's Creed series, insisting there are currently no new remakes of the series' past games in the works.

Every Voice Actor Behind GTA 6's Main Cast

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, grand Theft Auto 6 is finally here, and now that NDA's have expired, actors everywhere are finally taking a moment to confirm their roles on the project through social media.
  • Of course, being as big a release as it is, it should come as no surprise that, in addition to the main cast, a massive number of actors and celebrities are featured in supporting roles and cameos throughout the game.
  • It has been revealed that taking on the role of bank-robbing professional Raul Batista is none other than Manny Perez.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, grand Theft Auto 6 is finally here, and now that NDA's have expired, actors everywhere are finally taking a moment to confirm their roles on the project through social media. The full cast includes a mixture of well-known names, traditional actors making voice debuts, and even a few who will note GTA 6 as their first major project.

Of course, being as big a release as it is, it should come as no surprise that, in addition to the main cast, a massive number of actors and celebrities are featured in supporting roles and cameos throughout the game. So, keep an ear out, because you never know where you might run into a voice you recognize.

It has been revealed that taking on the role of bank-robbing professional Raul Batista is none other than Manny Perez. Raul's chaotic energy and simultaneously suave manner couldn't have asked for a better voice to back it than this legendary Dominican actor.

Sources indicate that unlike some of the lesser-known actors you'll see on this list, Manny has a long history of work, including Washington Heights, La Soga, El Rey de Najayo. He has also had supporting roles in shows like Law & Order: SVU, Blue Bloods, 100 Centre Street, and Hawaii Five-0.

Manny Perez has also served as a writer and producer on many of the projects he has acted in.

Industry observers note that real Dimez is the iconic rap duo, Bae-Luxe and Roxy Rashad, signed by Dre'Quan Priest at Only Raw Records. Voicing these talented women are actual Florida rappers, Hood Brat (Bae-Luxe) and Krissy Celess (Roxy). The duo has multiple tracks featured in the game, so needless to say, you'll be getting to know these voices quite well.

While Hood Brat and Krissy Celess aren't known for any other major acting roles and aren't a duo, you can find their individual music on major listening platforms like Spotify and Apple Music. So, if you're enjoying Real Dimez in GTA 6, check out some of their other work.

Dre'Quan Priest, voiced by Naiqui Macabroad, is a character you won't get to know until you've made it out to Vice City and engaged in the nightlife there, since he resides there while managing Only Raw Records and its newest talent, rap duo Real Dimez.

In a recent development, though this is Macabroad's first major voice role, he recently made his debut as a prominent recurring character on Chicago P.D., so fans of the show will be getting to know his face well over the course of Season 14. Other notable projects include guest roles on shows like Power and Law & Order.

According to recent reports, A face you'll see frequently alongside Dre'Quan is Boobie Ike, a Vice City legend. He runs several things around the city, including the adult entertainment club Jack of Hearts, while also backing the recording studio Dre'Quan manages.

Voicing Boobie Ike is Mike Forbs, whose work has primarily been supporting roles across TV and movies up to this point. That noted, if his performance as Boobie Ike is any indicator, we'll likely be seeing Forbs' name on other major projects very soon.

It has been revealed that though you won't get to spend tons of time with Donnie, he leaves a pretty unforgettable first impression and plays a major role in helping Jason earn money early on. Voicing this man of chaos is Brad Carter, an actor with several guest appearances on shows like Sons of Anarchy, Criminal Minds, Dexter, and Ozark.

A Few Supporting Voices As GTA 6 Locals That You May Recognize:.

Industry observers note that though you won't see Brian, Jason's boss, as often as some of the other supporting characters, you'll certainly be hearing his voice plenty when he calls with new orders. That voice belongs to Stephen Root, who you'll almost certainly recognize from one of his major roles. A few of those castings include Bill Dauterive in King of the Hill, Monroe Fuches in Barry, and Jim Hudson in Get Out.

In a recent development, while Lucia is a bit busy at the start of GTA 6, you'll rapidly get to know Jason's closest friend and co-worker of sorts, Cal Hampton. Bringing Cal's laid-back persona to life is none other than Bobby Moynihan, who you may recognize from Saturday Night Live and a variety of voice work and traditional acting roles. Some of his most recent include Woody on NCIS: Origins, King George in Hoppers, and Louie in Ducktales.

According to recent reports, though you're introduced to Lucia right from the start, it'll be several hours into the game before she's a consistently present face and playable character. Voicing Lucia is Manni L. Perez, who you may not recognize from other voice roles, but might know from major guest roles on indicates like Law & Order: SVU.

That said, Perez has voiced a couple of background characters in Grand Theft Auto V and GTA Online, so if you're a major fan of the franchise, you might find her voice a tad familiar.

While Lucia and Jason are both playable characters in GTA 6, Jason is widely considered the primary main character, since you spend the first several hours of the game playing as him, and this Florida man is voiced by none other than Dylan Rourke.

Though you may not recognize this uniquely deep voice from many previous major projects at the moment, it's safe to say this will put Rourke on everyone's radar.

Latest Update: GTA 6: How to Find the Kraken

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (531 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Grand Theft Auto series is well-known for its easter eggs, and GTA 6 is no different.
  • In a recent development, one of the coolest easter eggs found in GTA 6 so far is the Kraken, the legendary sea monster from Norse and Scandinavian Folklore.
  • If you want to see this easter egg for yourself, this guide has everything you need to know.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Grand Theft Auto series is well-known for its easter eggs, and GTA 6 is no different. Some notable ones include Dexter’s apartment from the hit TV show, UFO sightings, and even nods to Red Dead Redemption 2.

In a recent development, one of the coolest easter eggs found in GTA 6 so far is the Kraken, the legendary sea monster from Norse and Scandinavian Folklore. While the Kraken sighting in GTA 6 isn’t exactly a living creature, but rather just a structure near the ocean floor, it is clearly a reference to the famous sea monster.

If you want to see this easter egg for yourself, this guide has everything you need to know. Here’s how to find the Kraken in Grand Theft Auto 6.

Sources indicate that the Kraken can be found underwater, south of Catalan Bay and east of Peacock Bay in Vice City. The exact location of the Kraken can be found in the image below.

The water map can be a bit tricky to read due to there being no land, structures, or streets, but if you look closely enough, you will notice that there are distinct shapes within the water.

The Kraken is located on the second oval-like shape down from the beach of Catalan Bay. The oval shapes represent large sand hills and rocks underneath the water’s surface.

In a recent development, when you reach the location shown in the image above, equip your scuba gear and dive downward until you reach the sand. Next, take a look around you until you spot a strange-looking structure. You may have to swim a bit in case your diving point wasn’t the exact correct location.

Upon approaching the structure, you will immediately notice that it looks like a ship tangled in the Kraken’s tentacles. Unfortunately, the tentacles don’t move or anything, but it’s still a really cool easter egg that just goes to show how much love Rockstar Games put into GTA 6.

In case you need some help actually diving deep enough to reach the Kraken in GTA 6, we've got you covered on how to find scuba gear.

Sources indicate that there are a few ways to acquire scuba gear. First, you can find scuba gear on the small dock behind Jason’s house in Chapter 1, which is the earliest method. However, this method becomes unavailable to you if you have completed the first chapter.

Industry observers note that another way to get scuba gear is by exploring docks near beaches. While not all docks will have scuba gear to grab, a good number of them do.

Industry observers note that you can also get scuba gear from boats that are either docked or sailing the seas. I recommend visiting Kenton’s Charter Boat in Key Lento since it always has spare scuba gear on its seats.

Industry observers note that keep in mind that once you are finished scuba diving for the Kraken, or just scuba diving in general, and return to dry land, the scuba gear will eventually despawn. In other words, you will have to find more scuba gear the next time you want to go scuba diving.

Marathon may actually have a shot as Server Slam hits it big on Steam

📅 27 Feb 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (342 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Vg247

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Things are officially looking better for Marathon.
  • Considering how unpopular the game has been throughout its development, and judging by the feedback from earlier closed beta tests, the turnout for the Server Slam is definitely encouraging.
  • The Marathon Server Slam has been online for a little over 12 hours on Steam, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Things are officially looking better for Marathon. The game’s Server Slam, essentially an open beta that’s freely available everywhere, has kicked off. This is the last chance for anyone curious about Bungie’s next big game to play it before it officially goes on sale next week.

Considering how unpopular the game has been throughout its development, and judging by the feedback from earlier closed beta tests, the turnout for the Server Slam is definitely encouraging.

The Marathon Server Slam has been online for a little over 12 hours on Steam, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. Only one of those platforms shares player numbers, of course, but it's enough to offer some visibility into how popular the test has been.

It has been revealed that immediately after servers went live, Marathon shot up the Steam most played charts. The game swiftly achieved a peak of 143,621 concurrent players (via SteamDB), which is very respectable. Given that the Server Slam will be available for the entire weekend, there’s every chance the numbers will go up.

These figures are particularly encouraging when you look at Arc Raiders, the current top dog in the extraction shooter space, and the game that stole Marathon’s thunder last year when the two of them were being promoted by their publishers. Marathon, of course, got delayed out of 2025, which allowed Arc Raiders to launch first. It, of course, ended up proving that extraction shooters can be mainstream hits.

Like Marathon, Arc Raiders hosted its own server slam just a few days before its launch. That open test attracted 189,668 concurrent players at its peak, which is not that far off from Marathon’s so far.

Sources indicate that assuming positive word of mouth continues, more players are bound to jump in over the weekend and perhaps get Marathon to match or even exceed Arc Raiders’ record. At any rate, this is good news for beleaguered Bungie and points to what could be a significant launch.

Marathon arrives March 5 on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S.

Etsy sellers are closing their stores in response to the platform's fresh AI training policy

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Update: Etsy told the New York Times on Friday that it intends to revise the policy.

Industry observers note that online marketplace Etsy is facing backlash from customers over a recent change to its policies that allow it and other companies to use content created by sellers to train AI models. In response, numerous vendors have closed their online shops, and are encouraging others to do the same. Etsy, however, notes the latest policy isn't meant to "replace your creativity," but simply to improve storefront operations.

That seems pretty straightforward—anything you put on your Etsy page can be fed into the AI theft machine like Steve Buscemi in a Cohen Brothers film—and as reported by Cartoon Brew, it led to significant pushback from some Etsy users, including numerous store closures.

Sources indicate that you might have heard of Etsy's new terms and artists fleeing the platform. We're out, too.

Ring Cats Etsy final closure notice.

A post shared by Aaron Millard (@aaronmillardillustration).

In the wake of that reaction, Etsy vice president of customer operations James Ossman posted a separate patch saying it's not really like that at all, and that "we do not use your content to train AI models designed to copy your original work or replace your creativity.".

Sources indicate that "When we describe how we may use your content, we're enabling actions like translating your listing descriptions so buyers around the world can discover your items, or featuring your listing photos in Etsy marketing campaigns to showcase your creative work," Ossman wrote. "We also use your content to develop tools that make running your shop easier, like listing optimization tools or stats summaries that help you better understand your shop's performance. As always, your needs and feedback help guide how we build and improve these tools.".

As for providing third-party access to that content, Ossman mentioned that too is for "services and tools that can help you run your business," and promised that "when we partner with third parties, we do so thoughtfully to help protect your content and data.".

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Recent findings suggest that that hasn't satisfied everyone. Ossman's commitment doesn't exist within the actual terms of service, which as seen above states only that Etsy and partners can "use Your Content to develop, train, test and improve artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies." Ossman also noted in his update that the terms "prohibit scraping Etsy or unauthorized use of content from Etsy to train AI models," but that (as far as I can tell) applies to Etsy people and unauthorized third-parties, not Etsy itself or those it licenses.

Recent findings suggest that that's not to suggest that Etsy is being underhanded, merely that the binding legal language is imprecise. Others also complain that AI training should be opt-in rather than on by default—and worse, there's apparently no opt-out option available at all, so consumers who are opposed to having their work used for AI training for any reason are out of luck.

Ironically, the blowup over Etsy's embrace of AI training comes just weeks after it earned plaudits for banning AI-generated recipes and patterns, a move Ossman said was necessary to establish "trust" in the platform: "Sellers need clear guidance and confidence that their creativity and craftsmanship will be represented fairly; buyers need to understand what they’re buying and the human involvement behind it.".

Sources indicate that however this ultimately shakes out, the Etsy AI backlash is emblematic of a growing problem on both sides of the buy-sell divide: People want refuge from the creeping tendrils of the AI behemoth, and overtly or insidiously it's becoming increasingly difficult to find one. The more that happens, the more people are likely to react forcefully when platforms like Etsy start edging in the direction, regardless of any promises (or even carved-in-legal-stone commitments) of good intentions.

I've reached out to Etsy to ask if the newly introduced AI policy might be changed in response to the complaints and closures, and will update if I receive a reply.
